.cross_level_table <- function(x, what) {
  # `prevalence` is a profile's share of the individuals (see
  # `profile_prevalences`) or a group class's weight; fits made before it was
  # stored have `NA` for the profiles.
  long <- function(means, variances, level, prevalence) {
    cells <- expand.grid(row = seq_len(nrow(means)), indicator = seq_along(x$vars))
    data.frame(level = level, profile = rownames(means)[cells$row],
               indicator = x$vars[cells$indicator], mean = as.vector(means),
               variance = as.vector(variances),
               prevalence = unname(prevalence)[cells$row], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  class_names <- names(x$group_probabilities)
  assigned <- max.col(x$group_posteriors, ties.method = "first")
  switch(what,
    profiles = rbind(long(x$profile_means, x$profile_variances, "individual",
                          x$profile_prevalences %||%

    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +

    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = shapes) +
    .gg_theme() + .gg_top_legend() +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean") +
    .gg_titles(main, subtitle,
               if (chosen == "individual") "Individual profiles" else
                 "Group classes (means of the group means)", NULL, NULL)
}

#' Descriptive statistics and intraclass correlations of model variables
#'
#' Returns a table with one row per variable giving the number of observed and
#' missing values, the mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum and number of
#' distinct values, and, when groups are known, the number of groups and the
#' intraclass correlation (ICC): the share of the variable's variance that lies
#' between groups.
#'
#' An ICC near zero indicates little between-group variation in that
#' variable's mean. It does not rule out group classes that differ in other
#' variables, in profile prevalence, or in other features of the distributions.
#'
#' @param x A data frame, or a fitted model of this package, whose own `vars`
#'   and `id` are then used. A single-level fit has no groups, so its table
#'   has no `n_groups` or `icc`.
#' @param vars Character vector of column names to describe; repeated names
#'   are described once. Columns must be vectors: matrix-valued columns raise
#'   `latents_bad_data`. For a data frame, defaults to every numeric column
#'   other than `id` and `by`.
#' @param id Optional. The column identifying the groups the rows are nested
#'   in. Supplying it adds `n_groups` and `icc`.
#' @param by Optional. On a fitted model, `"profile"` or `"group_class"`; on a
#'   data frame, a column name. Each variable is then described once per level
#'   of it. Rows whose stratifier is `NA` form their own stratum, labelled `NA`
#'   and reported last, so every input row is counted in exactly one stratum.
#' @param ... Not used. For a data frame, any further argument raises a
#'   `latents_unused_argument` warning; for a fit, it raises
#'   `latents_bad_argument`.
#' @return A base `data.frame`, one row per variable (or per variable and `by`
#'   level), with the columns
#'   \describe{
#'     \item{`variable`}{character: the column described.}
#'     \item{`n`}{integer: observations with a value.}
#'     \item{`n_missing`}{integer: observations without one.}
#'     \item{`mean`,`sd`,`min`,`max`}{numeric; `NA_real_` for a variable
#'       that is not numeric.}
#'     \item{`n_distinct`}{integer: distinct observed values.}
#'     \item{`n_groups`,`icc`}{present only when `id` is known. `icc` is the
#'       one-way random-effects estimate; it can be slightly negative when the
#'       between-group mean square is below the within-group one, which
#'       indicates no group structure. Rows with a missing group ID do not
#'       contribute to either statistic.}
#'   }
#'   With `by`, a first column named after the stratifier holds each stratum's
#'   value (`NA` for the stratum of missing values). For every variable,
#'   `n + n_missing` summed over the strata equals the number of input rows.
#'   When describing a fit by `"profile"` or `"group_class"`, the model's
#'   assignment is used as the stratifier without replacing an indicator of
#'   the same name. A `by` named like one of the summary's own columns raises
#'   `latents_bad_data`. Describing no variables raises
#'   `latents_nothing_to_describe`.
#' @references Bliese, P. D. (2000). Within-group agreement, non-independence,
#'   and reliability. In K. J. Klein & S. W. J. Kozlowski (Eds.), *Multilevel
#'   theory, research, and methods in organizations*.
#' @seealso [multilpa()] to fit, [diagnostics()] for the after-the-fit
#'   counterpart.
#' @examples
#' descriptives(
#'   course_engagement,
#'   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
#'   id = "student"
#' )
#'
#' # A missing stratifier is a stratum of its own, not a silent loss and not
#' # missingness invented in a variable that has none.
#' descriptives(data.frame(cohort = c("A", "A", "B", NA), score = 1:4),
#'              vars = "score", by = "cohort")
#'
#' fit <- multilpa(
#'   course_engagement,
#'   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
#'   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
#'   seed = 1
#' )
#' descriptives(fit)
#' descriptives(fit, by = "profile")
#' @export

before.name: descriptives.multilpa
before.documentation:
#' @rdname descriptives
#' @export
before.source:
descriptives.multilpa <- function(x, by = NULL, ...) {
  stopifnot("`by` must be \"profile\" or \"group_class\"" =
              is.null(by) || (is.character(by) && length(by) == 1L &&
                                by %in% c("profile", "group_class")))
  # `vars` and `id` are the fit's own, so there is nothing further to pass on;
  # a supplied one would otherwise collide with them or be dropped unread.
  .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
    list(...), "descriptives()",
    "A fit supplies its own `vars` and `id`; describe a data frame to choose them.")
  frame <- .multilpa_model_frame(x)
  # A single-level fit numbers its rows as one-row groups of its own making.
  # Its grouping summaries would describe that numbering, not the data.
  id <- if (isTRUE(x$single_level)) NULL else x$id
  if (is.null(by)) {
    return(descriptives.data.frame(frame, vars = x$vars, id = id))
  }
  # The assignment is metadata, not a measurement: it is carried beside the
  # frame rather than written into it, so an indicator the caller named
  # `profile` or `group_class` keeps its own values.
  .multilpa_describe_by(frame, x$vars, id,
                        .multilpa_assignment_values(x, by), by)
}

.multilpa_describe_by.name: .multilpa_describe_by

before.name: .multilpa_describe_by
before.documentation:
#' Describe each variable once per stratum
#'
#' The stratifier arrives as a vector beside the frame, not as a column of it,
#' so describing by a class the model assigned cannot overwrite an indicator of
#' the same name.
#'
#' Rows are keyed to their stratum with `match()`, which returns `NA` for a
#' missing stratifier. Selecting with `which()` on that key therefore drops the
#' missing rows from every observed stratum instead of turning each selector
#' into a vector of `NA`s, which is what `x[[by]] == level` did: `NA` selectors
#' fabricate rows that are missing on every variable and lose the observed
#' values of the rows that carry them.
#'
#' @param data A data frame.
#' @param vars Column names to describe.
#' @param id Optional grouping column name.
#' @param by_values One stratifier value per row of `data`.
#' @param by_label The name the stratum column takes in the result.
#' @return A base `data.frame`, one row per stratum and variable, the stratum of
#'   rows with a missing stratifier last.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_describe_by <- function(data, vars, id, by_values, by_label) {
  summary_columns <- c("variable", "n", "n_missing", "mean", "sd", "min", "max",
                       "n_distinct", "n_groups", "icc")
  stopifnot(
    "`vars` must be column names of the frame being described" =
      all(vars %in% names(data)),
    "`by` must have one value for each row described" =
      length(by_values) == nrow(data))
  if (by_label %in% summary_columns) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
      "`by` names the column `%s`, which the summary itself uses, so the two could not be told apart in the result.",
      by_label), class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  # Strata in a fixed order -- a factor's own level order, otherwise sorted --
  # so the table reads class 1, 2, ... whatever order the rows came in.
  present <- by_values[!is.na(by_values)]
  observed_levels <- if (is.factor(by_values)) {
    factor(intersect(levels(by_values), as.character(present)),
           levels = levels(by_values))
  } else sort(unique(present))
  keys <- match(by_values, observed_levels)
  missing_stratum <- anyNA(keys)
  strata <- c(lapply(seq_along(observed_levels), \(index) which(keys == index)),
              if (missing_stratum) list(which(is.na(keys))))
  # A length-one vector of the stratifier's own type, so a factor keeps its
  # levels and a numeric stratifier is not coerced to character by its label.
  labels <- c(observed_levels, if (missing_stratum) by_values[NA_integer_])
  if (length(strata) == 0L) {
    empty <- cbind(stats::setNames(data.frame(by_values[NA_integer_]), by_label),
                   .multilpa_describe(data, vars, id))
    return(empty[0L, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  described <- lapply(seq_along(strata), function(index) {
    cbind(stats::setNames(data.frame(labels[index], stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                          by_label),
          .multilpa_describe(data[strata[[index]], , drop = FALSE], vars, id))
  })
  result <- do.call(rbind, described)
  row.names(result) <- NULL
  accounted <- vapply(split(result$n + result$n_missing, result$variable),
                      sum, integer(1))
  stopifnot(
    "Every described row must fall in exactly one stratum" =
      identical(sum(lengths(strata)), nrow(data)),
    "Each variable must be counted once for every described row" =
      all(accounted == nrow(data)))
  result
}

before.source:
.multilpa_describe <- function(data, vars, id) {
  .multilpa_check_descriptive_columns(data, unique(c(vars, id)))
  described <- lapply(vars, function(name) {
    values <- data[[name]]
    observed <- values[!is.na(values)]
    row <- data.frame(
      variable = name,

      mean = if (is.numeric(values)) mean(observed) else NA_real_,

      min = if (is.numeric(values) && length(observed) > 0L) min(observed) else NA_real_,

    row$icc <- if (is.numeric(values)) .multilpa_icc(values[grouped], groups) else NA_real_

.multilpa_icc.name: .multilpa_icc

before.name: .multilpa_icc
before.documentation:
#' One-way random-effects intraclass correlation
#'
#' The share of variance lying between groups, from the one-way ANOVA mean
#' squares. `n0` is the size-corrected average group size, which equals the
#' common size when the groups are balanced and is smaller when they are not, so
#' a few large groups cannot inflate the estimate.
#'
#' The estimate is returned as computed. It can fall slightly below zero when
#' the between-group mean square is smaller than the within-group one, which is
#' the estimator saying there is no group structure; truncating it at zero would
#' hide that rather than report it.
#'
#' @param values Numeric observations, already complete.
#' @param groups The group each observation belongs to.
#' @return A single number, or `NA_real_` where the design cannot support one.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_icc <- function(values, groups) {
  sizes <- tabulate(match(groups, unique(groups)))
  k <- length(sizes)
  n <- length(values)
  if (k < 2L || n <= k) return(NA_real_)
  grand_mean <- mean(values)
  group_means <- vapply(split(values, groups), mean, numeric(1))
  between <- sum(sizes * (group_means[match(unique(groups), names(group_means))] -
                            grand_mean)^2) / (k - 1L)
  within <- sum((values - group_means[match(groups, names(group_means))])^2) / (n - k)
  if (!is.finite(between) || !is.finite(within)) return(NA_real_)
  n0 <- (n - sum(sizes^2) / n) / (k - 1L)
  denominator <- between + (n0 - 1) * within
  # Zero within-group variance is not a degenerate case: every observation
  # equals its group's own value, so all of the variance is between groups and
  # the ratio is exactly one. Only a variable that is constant everywhere has
  # no ratio to report.
  if (!is.finite(denominator) || denominator <= 0) return(NA_real_)
  (between - within) / denominator
}

#' The formula behind each criterion, keyed by its name

                   bic = "-2L + q log(n)",
                   sabic = "-2L + q log((n + 2) / 24)",
                   caic = "-2L + q (log(n) + 1)",

  stopifnot("Every criterion must have a definition" =
              all(criterion %in% names(definitions)))
  unname(definitions[criterion])
}

.multilpa_information_criteria.name: .multilpa_information_criteria

before.name: .multilpa_information_criteria
before.documentation:
#' Every likelihood-penalty criterion a fit supports
#'
#' The formulas, the two sample-size conventions, the entropy each criterion
#' penalizes and the references are documented on `?get_results`, which is where
#' a caller reaches this table from.
#'
#' @param x A fitted model of this package.
#' @param definitions `TRUE` adds the formula and the reference per criterion,
#'   which only the long form has a row for.
#' @param format `"wide"` for the one-row reporting shape, `"long"` for one row
#'   per criterion and sample-size convention.
#' @return A base `data.frame`, one row in the wide form and one row per
#'   criterion and convention in the long form.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_information_criteria <- function(x, definitions = FALSE,
                                 format = c("wide", "long")) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x),
            "`definitions` must be TRUE or FALSE" =
              isTRUE(definitions) || isFALSE(definitions))
  format <- match.arg(format)
  if (isTRUE(definitions) && identical(format, "wide")) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "`definitions` describes one criterion per row, which the wide form has not. Use format = \"long\".",
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  q <- x$n_parameters
  deviance <- -2 * x$log_likelihood
  conventions <- data.frame(
    convention = c("groups", "individuals"),
    n = c(.multilpa_group_sample_size(x),
          x$n_informative %||% x$n_observations))
  entropies <- c(groups = if (is.null(x$group_posteriors)) NA_real_ else
                   .multilpa_entropy_sum(.multilpa_classified_group_posteriors(x)),
                 individuals = .multilpa_entropy_sum(.multilpa_classified_posteriors(x)))
  scale_free <- data.frame(
    criterion = c("deviance", "aic", "kic"),
    convention = NA_character_, n = NA_integer_,
    penalty = c(0, 2 * q, 3 * (q + 1)))
  scaled <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(conventions)), function(row) {
    convention <- conventions$convention[row]
    n <- conventions$n[row]
    entropy_sum <- entropies[[convention]]
    penalties <- c(bic = q * log(n),
                   sabic = q * log((n + 2) / 24),
                   caic = q * (log(n) + 1),
                   awe = 2 * q * (1.5 + log(n)) + 2 * entropy_sum,
                   icl = q * log(n) + 2 * entropy_sum,
                   # The only criterion here that does not use the sample size.
                   # Its convention still matters, because it decides which
                   # level's classification uncertainty is being penalized.
                   clc = 2 * entropy_sum)
    data.frame(criterion = names(penalties), convention = convention, n = n,
               penalty = unname(penalties))
  }))
  result <- rbind(scale_free, scaled)
  # Every row is the same deviance plus its own penalty, so the `value` column
  # means one thing throughout: smaller is a better-supported model. The penalty
  # itself is not a column: nobody reports it, and it is the difference between
  # two numbers the table already carries.
  result$value <- deviance + result$penalty
  result <- result[c("criterion", "convention", "n", "value")]
  row.names(result) <- NULL
  if (identical(format, "wide")) return(.multilpa_criteria_wide(result, x))
  if (isTRUE(definitions)) {
    result$definition <- .multilpa_criterion_definitions(result$criterion)
  }
  result
}

#' One row per class of classification diagnostics for one level
#'
#' Modal counts and average posteriors describe the rows supplied; the
#' estimated class sizes and shares (and so the odds of correct
#' classification) are the model's, which under sampling weights are the
#' weighted posterior totals.
#'
#' @param probabilities Posterior probability matrix.
#' @param level Label recorded in the `level` column.
#' @param weights `NULL`, or one sampling weight per row.
#' @return A tidy `data.frame`, one row per class.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(probabilities, level, weights = NULL) {
    average <- .multilpa_average_posterior_matrix(probabilities)
    n_classes <- ncol(probabilities)
    classes <- seq_len(n_classes)
    assigned <- max.col(probabilities, ties.method = "first")
    n_modal <- tabulate(assigned, nbins = n_classes)
    estimated_n <- if (is.null(weights)) 
        colSums(probabilities)
    else colSums(probabilities * weights)
    estimated_proportion <- estimated_n/if (is.null(weights)) 
        nrow(probabilities)
    else sum(weights)
    diagonal <- average[cbind(classes, classes)]
    data.frame(level = level, class = .multilpa_class_labels(probabilities), n_modal = n_modal, proportion_modal = n_modal/nrow(probabilities), estimated_n = estimated_n, estimated_proportion = estimated_proportion, average_posterior = diagonal, odds_correct_classification = .multilpa_odds_correct(diagonal, estimated_proportion))
}

.multilpa_odds_correct.name: .multilpa_odds_correct

before.name: .multilpa_odds_correct
before.documentation:
#' Odds of correct classification
#' @param average Average posterior probability in the assigned class.
#' @param proportion Model-estimated class proportion.
#' @return Odds ratio; `Inf` for a class whose average posterior is one to
#'   within rounding (perfect classification), and `NA_real_` where the ratio
#'   is undefined (no modal members, or a class proportion of zero or one).
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(average, proportion) {
    stopifnot(`\`average\` and \`proportion\` must have equal length` = length(average) == length(proportion))
    sized <- !is.na(average) & !is.na(proportion) & proportion > 0 & proportion < 1
    perfect <- sized & average >= 1 - sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
    defined <- sized & !perfect & average > 0
    odds <- rep(NA_real_, length(average))
    odds[perfect] <- Inf
    odds[defined] <- (average[defined]/(1 - average[defined]))/(proportion[defined]/(1 - proportion[defined]))
    odds
}

.multilpa_odds_correct <- function(average, proportion) {
  stopifnot("`average` and `proportion` must have equal length" =
              length(average) == length(proportion))
  sized <- !is.na(average) & !is.na(proportion) & proportion > 0 & proportion < 1
  # Within rounding of one, 1 - average is floating-point noise, and dividing
  # by it would report odds such as 7e15 that measure only that noise.
  perfect <- sized & average >= 1 - sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
  defined <- sized & !perfect & average > 0
  odds <- rep(NA_real_, length(average))
  odds[perfect] <- Inf
  odds[defined] <- (average[defined] / (1 - average[defined])) /
    (proportion[defined] / (1 - proportion[defined]))
  odds
}

.multilpa_entropy_table <- function(x) {
  stopifnot("`object` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x))
  posteriors <- list(individuals = .multilpa_classified_posteriors(x),
                     groups = .multilpa_classified_group_posteriors(x))

.latents_center_direct.name: .latents_center_direct

before.name: .latents_center_direct
before.documentation:
#' Centre the covariates of direct effects for fitting
#'
#' The model y = m + B z is the same model as y = (m + B c) + B (z - c), so
#' EM can run on centred covariates, where the intercepts and the effects are
#' nearly uncorrelated, and `.latents_uncenter_direct()` moves the means back.
#'
#' @param extra The extra carrier, or `NULL`.
#' @param x Continuous indicators, used to select the observations of each
#'   effect's target; `NULL` uses every row.
#' @param row_weights Optional sampling weights in observation order.
#' @return The carrier with one centred internal covariate column per effect,
#'   its target-specific `centers` and `scales`. The original carrier is kept
#'   on the reported fit, retaining the caller's covariate names and columns.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_center_direct <- function(extra, x = NULL, row_weights = NULL) {
  stopifnot(is.null(extra) || is.list(extra), is.null(x) || is.matrix(x),
            is.null(row_weights) || is.numeric(row_weights))
  if (is.null(extra$direct)) return(extra)
  effects <- extra$direct$effects
  values <- extra$direct$covariates[, effects$covariate_column, drop = FALSE]
  weights <- row_weights %||% rep(1, nrow(values))
  stopifnot(length(weights) == nrow(values),
            is.null(x) || nrow(x) == nrow(values))
  # A predictor value on a missing target or a zero-weight row supplies no
  # information about this effect. Including it in the centre can make a
  # regular intercept/slope pair arbitrarily collinear. Each target gets its
  # own chart, even when its predictor is shared with another target.
  observed <- if (is.null(x)) matrix(TRUE, nrow(values), ncol(values)) else
    !is.na(x[, effects$column, drop = FALSE])
  observed <- observed & weights > 0
  centers <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(values)), function(column) {
    rows <- observed[, column]
    stats::weighted.mean(values[rows, column], weights[rows])
  }, numeric(1))
  scales <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(values)), function(column) {
    stats::sd(values[observed[, column], column])
  }, numeric(1))
  extra$direct$covariates <- sweep(values, 2L, centers, "-")
  extra$direct$effects$covariate_column <- seq_len(nrow(effects))
  extra$direct$centers <- centers
  extra$direct$scales <- scales
  extra
}

.latents_direct_maximize.name: .latents_direct_maximize

before.name: .latents_direct_maximize
before.documentation:
#' Update the direct effects given the class means and variances
#'
#' With the means and the diagonal variances held, the expected complete-data
#' log likelihood of indicator j is a weighted least squares in its effects:
#' sum_i sum_k r_ik (x_ij - mu_kj - b_j' z_i)^2 / s2_kj, whose minimum solves
#' (sum_i w_ij z_i z_i') b_j = sum_i z_i sum_k r_ik (x_ij - mu_kj) / s2_kj with
#' w_ij = sum_k r_ik / s2_kj. Rows where the indicator is unobserved carry no
#' information about it under a diagonal covariance.
#'
#' @param x The continuous matrix, unshifted.
#' @param extra The extra carrier.
#' @param posteriors Rows by profiles.
#' @param means,variances Profiles by indicators.
#' @return The effects, one per row of `extra$direct$effects`.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(x, extra, posteriors, means, variances) {
    direct <- extra$direct
    effects <- direct$effects
    updated <- numeric(nrow(effects))
    indicators <- unique(effects$column)
    solved <- lapply(indicators, function(column) {
        rows <- which(effects$column == column)
        observed <- !is.na(x[, column])
        precision <- sweep(posteriors[observed, , drop = FALSE], 2L, variances[, column], "/")
        weight <- rowSums(precision)
        residual <- rowSums(precision * outer(x[observed, column], means[, column], "-"))
        design <- direct$covariates[observed, effects$covariate_column[rows], drop = FALSE]
        positive <- weight > 0
        root_weight <- sqrt(weight[positive])
        as.vector(qr.solve(design[positive, , drop = FALSE] * root_weight, residual[positive]/root_weight))
    })
    updated[unlist(lapply(indicators, function(column) which(effects$column == column)))] <- unlist(solved)
    updated
}

.latents_direct_maximize <- function(x, extra, posteriors, means, variances) {
  direct <- extra$direct
  effects <- direct$effects
  updated <- numeric(nrow(effects))
  indicators <- unique(effects$column)
  solved <- lapply(indicators, function(column) {
    rows <- which(effects$column == column)
    observed <- !is.na(x[, column])
    precision <- sweep(posteriors[observed, , drop = FALSE], 2L, variances[, column], "/")
    weight <- rowSums(precision)
    residual <- rowSums(precision * outer(x[observed, column], means[, column], "-"))
    design <- direct$covariates[observed, effects$covariate_column[rows], drop = FALSE]
    # Solve on the weighted design: its cross-product squares the condition
    # number and can appear singular even when the covariates have full rank.
    positive <- weight > 0
    root_weight <- sqrt(weight[positive])
    as.vector(qr.solve(design[positive, , drop = FALSE] * root_weight,
                       residual[positive] / root_weight))
  })
  updated[unlist(lapply(indicators, function(column) which(effects$column == column)))] <-
    unlist(solved)
  updated
}

    residual <- rowSums(precision * outer(x[observed, column], means[, column], "-"))
    design <- direct$covariates[observed, effects$covariate_column[rows], drop = FALSE]
    # Solve on the weighted design: its cross-product squares the condition
    # number and can appear singular even when the covariates have full rank.
    positive <- weight > 0
    root_weight <- sqrt(weight[positive])
    as.vector(qr.solve(design[positive, , drop = FALSE] * root_weight,
                       residual[positive] / root_weight))
  })
  updated[unlist(lapply(indicators, function(column) which(effects$column == column)))] <-
    unlist(solved)
  updated
}

}

enumerate_classes.name: enumerate_classes

before.name: enumerate_classes
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(data = , vars = , id = , n_profiles = 1:4, n_group_classes = 1:3, model = "basic", seed = NULL, family = "profiles", between_variance = c("varying", "equal"), time = NULL, ... = , cores = 1L, type = NULL, verbose = cores > 1L))
before.documentation:
#' Enumerate numbers of individual profiles and group classes
#'
#' Fits every requested combination of profile count, group-class count and
#' covariance structure and returns the candidates with their information
#' criteria and classification diagnostics. Errors and warnings of each
#' candidate are kept in the table alongside the successful fits. Information
#' criteria are descriptive: neither the smallest BIC nor high entropy
#' guarantees the correct number of classes. Unconverged, boundary and
#' unreplicated fits are reported, not silently selected.
#' @param data Data frame.
#' @param vars Indicator column names.
#' @param id The column identifying the groups the observations are nested in
#'   (students in schools, reports in students). Required; `NULL` enumerates
#'   single-level models, with a message. [enumerate_lpa()] and
#'   [enumerate_lca()] fit single-level models directly.
#' @param n_profiles Positive integer profile counts to try. Default `1:4`.
#' @param n_group_classes Positive integer group-class counts to try. Default
#'   `1:3`. With `id = NULL` it is 1 and may be left out.
#' @param model The covariance structures to cross with the class counts.
#'   `"basic"` (the default) fits four structures: `"EEI"` (equal variances,
#'   no covariances), `"VVI"` (varying variances, no covariances), `"EEE"`
#'   (one covariance matrix shared by all profiles) and `"VVV"` (a covariance
#'   matrix for each profile). Omitting covariances between correlated
#'   indicators tends to favour additional profiles. `"all"` fits all 14
#'   structures of Celeux and Govaert (1995). Otherwise, name structures by
#'   their three-letter codes, as [multilpa()]'s `model` takes them: the
#'   letters give the volume, shape and orientation of each profile's
#'   covariance matrix, each equal (`E`) or varying (`V`) across profiles,
#'   with `I` for no covariances. `NULL` crosses no structures. With one
#'   continuous indicator, codes that coincide (equal or varying variance)
#'   are fitted once; with only categorical indicators no structure is
#'   crossed. A structure set through `variance_model`, `covariance_model`,
#'   `volume`, `shape` or `orientation` in `...` replaces the default.
#' @param seed Optional seed for each fit: a whole number `set.seed()`
#'   accepts. Anything else raises `latents_bad_argument` before any candidate
#'   is fitted.
#' @param family `"profiles"` (the default) enumerates the profile model over
#'   `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes` and `model`. One or more of the
#'   group-class families `"additive"`, `"dispersion"` and
#'   `"additive_dispersion"` enumerates those instead, over `family`,
#'   `n_group_classes` and `between_variance`; these need `id`, `n_profiles`
#'   and `model` are then refused, and the result is a
#'   `latents_family_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and
#'   [get_candidate()].
#' @param between_variance For group-class families: the between-variance
#'   restrictions to cross, `"varying"`, `"equal"` or both (the default). The
#'   dispersion family is always fitted with `"equal"`. Refused for the
#'   profile family.
#' @param time The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models
#'   ([lta()]) over `n_profiles` (default `2:4`) and `n_group_classes`
#'   (default `1`), with every other `lta()` argument given in `...` held
#'   fixed. `model`, when given, crosses those covariance structures. Only
#'   the profile family is available. The result is a
#'   `latents_transition_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and
#'   [get_candidate()].
#' @param cores Number of processor cores to fit the candidates on (default
#'   1). Each candidate sets and restores its own random seed, so with `seed`
#'   given the result is identical to `cores = 1`. Candidates are fitted by
#'   forked processes on macOS and Linux, and by a socket cluster on Windows
#'   and on macOS when R uses Apple's Accelerate BLAS (socket workers load the
#'   installed package). Warnings and messages from the workers are passed on
#'   in grid order once all have finished. Without `seed`, the random starts
#'   differ between runs on any number of cores. Lost worker results are retried
#'   once with half as many workers (rounded up). One `latents_worker_lost`
#'   warning reports how many tasks were lost and recovered, and suggests fewer
#'   cores. A task still lost becomes a failed start (for flat start grids) or
#'   a failed candidate; the other results are retained. On sockets, bounded
#'   chunks preserve earlier results when a connection breaks; completed tasks
#'   within the failed chunk may also be retried. Each core holds its own copy
#'   of the fits it computes; `parallel::detectCores()` gives the number
#'   available.
#'   Transition grids (`time`) and profile grids (including categorical-only
#'   latent class models) distribute individual starts across one pool,
#'   longest estimated first, with at most `cores` workers and no nested
#'   workers. Both emEM screening and finalist runs use the pool; `search`
#'   keeps the same defaults as [multilpa()]. Setup, ordered starting values,
#'   start selection and finalisation stay in the current process. Profile
#'   models with membership covariates or joined categorical `local_dependence`
#'   pairs instead occupy one worker per candidate in the same pool, with
#'   serial starts. Group-class families also keep candidate-level parallelism.
#' @param verbose Whether to report progress: one message each when the
#'   candidates are prepared, when their starts are fitted, and when the grid
#'   is done, with the elapsed time. The default reports when `cores > 1`,
#'   where a grid is usually long. Group-class families (`family`) are not
#'   reported.
#' @param type Optional model type: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`. `NULL`
#'   (the default) keeps the existing routing and measurement settings.
#'   `"lca"` treats every indicator as categorical, as [multilca()] does:
#'   indicators named in `ordinal` or `count` keep those distributions, and
#'   `categorical` adds to the set rather than replacing it. Numeric response
#'   codes are categorical with `type = "lca"`. `"lpa"` requires continuous
#'   indicators and refuses non-empty `categorical`, `ordinal` or `count`.
#'   Both require `time = NULL`. `"lta"` requires `time` and takes its
#'   measurement settings from `categorical`, as [lta()] does; it does not
#'   make numeric indicators categorical. An explicit type requires
#'   `family = "profiles"`; leave `type = NULL` for group-class families.
#' @param ... Further arguments to [multilpa()] (or to [lta()] with `time`),
#'   applied to every candidate, such as `n_starts` (random starts per
#'   candidate), `max_iter`, `missing`, `categorical`, `centering`, `scaling`,
#'   `drop_empty` and `boundary` (`"exclude"` sets aside starts with a
#'   variance at `min_variance`, degenerate solutions that become more likely
#'   as `n_starts` grows). For example, `enumerate_classes(data, vars, id,
#'   n_profiles = 2:6, n_starts = 20, seed = 1)`. Group-class families take
#'   only `n_starts`, `max_iter`, `tol` and `min_variance`.
#' @return An object of class `multilpa_enumeration` (or the transition or
#'   family enumeration described above). Its `type` records the resolved
#'   model: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`, or `"mixed"`/`"family"` for
#'   those grids under `type = NULL`. The print header shows this type; table
#'   columns are unchanged. [as.data.frame()] gives
#'   one row per candidate, starting with its name (`"profiles3_groups2"`),
#'   with every criterion and diagnostic (including both entropies and, at
#'   each level, the smallest, largest and mean average posterior probability
#'   and the number of classes below a cutoff) and the candidate's warnings
#'   and error. `get_results(x, "best")` names the candidate at each
#'   criterion's minimum; `get_results(x, "classification")` gives every
#'   class's average posterior probability and relative entropy for every
#'   candidate; `get_results(x, "deltas")` and `"knees"` give model-selection
#'   evidence. [summary()] prints each criterion's minimum and every table,
#'   [plot()] draws the information criteria (and, with `what`,
#'   classification quality and model-selection views), [get_candidate()]
#'   returns the fitted model of one candidate, and [compare_models()] puts
#'   candidates side by side; these verbs take candidates by name.
#' @seealso [get_candidate()] to take one fitted model out of the grid,
#'   `summary()` for the criterion-by-criterion comparison.
#' @section Conditions:
#'   `latents_bad_argument` when `model` names an unknown structure, when it is
#'   given together with another way of setting the structure, or when it is
#'   given although no indicator is continuous; when `seed` is not a seed
#'   `set.seed()` accepts; when `...` contains an argument [multilpa()] does
#'   not take; when `n_group_classes` other than 1 is given with `id = NULL`;
#'   when `id` is missing; when `between_variance` is given for the profile
#'   family; when `n_profiles` or `model` is given for a group-class family,
#'   or `id` is `NULL`; when `time` is combined with a group-class family or
#'   with `between_variance`; and when `cores` is not a whole number of at
#'   least 1; and when `type` is invalid or conflicts with `time`, `family`
#'   or the requested measurement distributions.
#' @references
#' Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (1995). Gaussian parsimonious clustering models.
#' *Pattern Recognition*, 28(5), 781--793.
#' @examples
#' set.seed(1)
#' d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100))
#' candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,
#'                               n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#' as.data.frame(candidates)
#' summary(candidates)
#'
#' # Numeric response codes, explicitly categorical:
#' codes <- data.frame(g = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10), item = rep(0:1, 50))
#' classes <- enumerate_classes(codes, "item", "g", type = "lca",
#'                              n_profiles = 1, n_group_classes = 1,
#'                              n_starts = 1, seed = 1)
#'
#' # Single level, crossing class counts with two named structures:
#' single <- enumerate_lpa(iris, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width",
#'                                 "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),
#'                         n_profiles = 1:3, model = c("VVV", "EEE"),
#'                         n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#' summary(single)
#' @export
before.source:
enumerate_classes <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles = 1:4,
                              n_group_classes = 1:3, model = "basic",
                              seed = NULL, family = "profiles",
                              between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
                              time = NULL, ..., cores = 1L, type = NULL,
                              verbose = cores > 1L) {
  data_expression <- substitute(data)
  # A socket worker receives the candidates' closure serialized; an unforced
  # `data` would travel as a promise naming the caller's variable, which the
  # worker cannot find. The transition and family paths never touch `data`
  # before the workers start, so it is forced here for every path.
  force(data)
  cores <- .latents_check_cores(cores)
  stopifnot("`verbose` must be TRUE or FALSE" =
              is.logical(verbose) && length(verbose) == 1L && !is.na(verbose))
  if (missing(id)) {
    .multilpa_missing_id("enumerate_classes",
                         "`enumerate_lpa()` or `enumerate_lca()`")
  }
  # Every candidate's refusal is recorded as that candidate's failure, so a
  # seed set.seed() would not take must be refused here, once, or it comes
  # back as a grid in which every candidate failed.
  .multilpa_check_seed(seed)
  type <- .latents_check_enumeration_type(type, time, family)
  if (!is.null(time)) {
    # Transition models: profiles x group classes (x structures when `model`
    # names codes); every other lta() argument is held fixed through `...`.
    if (!identical(family, "profiles") || !missing(between_variance)) {
      stop(errorCondition(
        "Transition models (`time`) are enumerated for the profile family only.",
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    result <- .latents_report_once(.lta_enumerate(data, vars, id, time,
                          if (missing(n_profiles)) 2:4 else n_profiles,
                          if (missing(n_group_classes)) 1L else n_group_classes,
                          if (missing(model)) NULL else model, seed, list(...),
                          match.call(), cores = cores, verbose = verbose))
    result$type <- "lta"
    return(result)
  }
  if (!identical(family, "profiles")) {
    # Group-class families have no individual profiles and no covariance
    # structure codes; they are enumerated over family and class count.
    if (!missing(n_profiles) || !missing(model) || is.null(id)) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "Group-class families take `id`, `family`, `n_group_classes` and",
        "`between_variance`; `n_profiles` and `model` belong to the profile model."),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    result <- .latents_report_once(.additive_enumerate(data, vars, id, family,
                                  n_group_classes, between_variance, seed, list(...),
                                  match.call(), cores = cores))
    result$type <- "family"
    return(result)
  }
  if (!missing(between_variance)) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "`between_variance` belongs to the group-class families (`family = `).",
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  model_given <- !missing(model)
  single_level <- is.null(id)
  if (single_level) {
    # One observation per unit leaves no composition for a group class to
    # differ in, so the only group-class count is 1.
    if (!missing(n_group_classes) &&
        !isTRUE(all(as.integer(n_group_classes) == 1L))) {
      stop(errorCondition(paste(
        "`id = NULL` fits single-level models, which have one group class;",
        "leave `n_group_classes` out, or pass `id` to enumerate group classes."),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    n_group_classes <- 1L
  }
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(data), is.character(vars),
            "`id` must be a single column name, or NULL for single-level models" =
              single_level || (is.character(id) && length(id) == 1L),
            is.numeric(n_profiles), length(n_profiles) > 0L,
            all(is.finite(n_profiles)), all(n_profiles >= 1), all(n_profiles == as.integer(n_profiles)),
            is.numeric(n_group_classes), length(n_group_classes) > 0L,
            all(is.finite(n_group_classes)), all(n_group_classes >= 1),
            all(n_group_classes == as.integer(n_group_classes)),
            "`model` must be \"basic\", \"all\", covariance model codes, or NULL" =
              is.null(model) || (is.character(model) &&
                                   length(model) > 0L &&
                                   !anyNA(model)))

  # with "matched by multiple actual arguments" before `...` is assembled.
  extra <- list(...)
  if (identical(type, "lca")) {
    extra$categorical <- .latents_lca_categorical(vars, extra)
  }
  if (identical(type, "lpa")) {
    conflicts <- c("categorical", "ordinal", "count")
    conflicts <- conflicts[vapply(extra[conflicts], length, integer(1)) > 0L]
    if (length(conflicts)) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "`type = \"lpa\"` requires continuous indicators and conflicts with %s.",
        "Remove those measurement arguments, or use `type = NULL` for a mixed model."),
        paste(sprintf("`%s`", conflicts), collapse = ", ")),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    # Empty declarations carry no distribution under an all-continuous type.
    extra[intersect(names(extra), c("categorical", "ordinal", "count"))] <- NULL
  }
  # Anything `multilpa()` does not take would otherwise fail inside every
  # candidate and be recorded as a grid of failures; refuse it here instead.
  unknown_arguments <- setdiff(names(extra), names(formals(multilpa)))
  if (length(unknown_arguments) > 0L) {
    hint <- if ("structure" %in% unknown_arguments)
      " Covariance models are named with `model`." else ""
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
      "%s %s not an argument of multilpa().%s",
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", unknown_arguments), collapse = ", "),
      if (length(unknown_arguments) == 1L) "is" else "are", hint),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  # `NA` stands for "whatever the other arguments already said": no structure
  # is crossed, and each candidate is fitted as `multilpa()` would fit it.
  grid <- expand.grid(n_profiles = unique(n_profiles),
                      n_group_classes = unique(n_group_classes),
                      model = .multilpa_enumeration_models(
                        model, model_given, vars, extra),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  indices <- seq_len(nrow(grid))
  requested <- lapply(grid$model, .multilpa_enumeration_arguments,
                       vars = vars, extra = extra)
  arguments <- lapply(indices, function(i) c(
    list(data = data, vars = vars, id = id, n_profiles = grid$n_profiles[i],
         n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes[i], seed = seed),
    requested[[i]], extra))
  calls <- lapply(indices, function(i) .latents_candidate_call(
    "multilpa", data_expression, arguments[[i]][setdiff(names(arguments[[i]]), "data")]))
  costs <- grid$n_group_classes * grid$n_profiles *
    .multilpa_pool_width(data, vars, extra)
  fitted <- .multilpa_enumerate_fits(arguments, calls, costs, cores, verbose)
  # The candidates' conditions come back deferred and are signalled here,
  # candidate by candidate.
  runs <- .latents_report_once(lapply(indices, function(i) {
    conditions <- Filter(function(condition) !inherits(condition, "latents_single_level"),
                          fitted[[i]]$conditions)
    .latents_signal_conditions(conditions)
    warnings <- vapply(Filter(function(condition) inherits(condition, "warning"),
                               conditions), conditionMessage, character(1))
    failed <- inherits(fitted[[i]]$value, "error")
    fit <- if (failed) NULL else fitted[[i]]$value
    error_text <- if (failed) conditionMessage(fitted[[i]]$value) else NA_character_
    row <- cbind(
      data.frame(n_profiles = grid$n_profiles[i], n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes[i],
        # A latent class model has no covariance structure; naming one (the
        # default the fit records for its absent Gaussian block) misleads.
        model = if (is.null(fit)) grid$model[i] else
          if (length(.multilpa_continuous_names(fit)) == 0L) NA_character_ else
            .latents_comparison_structure(fit),
        log_likelihood = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else fit$log_likelihood,
        n_parameters = if (is.null(fit)) NA_integer_ else fit$n_parameters,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
      .multilpa_enumeration_indices(fit),
      data.frame(
        profile_entropy = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else
          .multilpa_relative_entropy(.multilpa_classified_posteriors(fit)),
        group_entropy = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else
          .multilpa_relative_entropy(.multilpa_classified_group_posteriors(fit)),
        converged = !is.null(fit) && fit$converged,
        boundary = if (is.null(fit)) NA else fit$boundary,
        min_standardized_eigenvalue = .latents_gaussian_minimum(
          fit, "min_standardized_eigenvalue"),
        min_gaussian_mass = .latents_gaussian_minimum(fit, "gaussian_mass"),
        n_best_replicated = if (is.null(fit)) NA_integer_ else fit$n_best_replicated %||% NA_integer_,
        warnings = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = "; "), error = error_text))
    list(fit = fit, row = row)
  }))
  if (single_level) {
    .multilpa_single_level_notice(
      latent_class = all(vars %in% extra$categorical))
  }
  result <- list(table = do.call(rbind, lapply(runs, `[[`, "row")),
       fits = lapply(runs, `[[`, "fit"), call = match.call())
  class(result) <- "multilpa_enumeration"
  result$type <- type %||% .latents_enumeration_measurement_type(vars, extra)
  names(result$fits) <- .latents_candidate_names(result)
  result
}

#' Enumerate numbers of individual profiles and group classes
#'
#' Fits every requested combination of profile count, group-class count and
#' covariance structure and returns the candidates with their information
#' criteria and classification diagnostics. Errors and warnings of each
#' candidate are kept in the table alongside the successful fits. Information
#' criteria are descriptive: neither the smallest BIC nor high entropy
#' guarantees the correct number of classes. Unconverged, boundary and
#' unreplicated fits are reported, not silently selected.
#' @param data Data frame.
#' @param vars Indicator column names.
#' @param id The column identifying the groups the observations are nested in
#'   (students in schools, reports in students). Required; `NULL` enumerates
#'   single-level models, with a message. [enumerate_lpa()] and
#'   [enumerate_lca()] fit single-level models directly.
#' @param n_profiles Positive integer profile counts to try. Default `1:4`.
#' @param n_group_classes Positive integer group-class counts to try. Default
#'   `1:3`. With `id = NULL` it is 1 and may be left out.
#' @param model The covariance structures to cross with the class counts.
#'   `"basic"` (the default) fits four structures: `"EEI"` (equal variances,
#'   no covariances), `"VVI"` (varying variances, no covariances), `"EEE"`
#'   (one covariance matrix shared by all profiles) and `"VVV"` (a covariance
#'   matrix for each profile). Omitting covariances between correlated
#'   indicators tends to favour additional profiles. `"all"` fits all 14
#'   structures of Celeux and Govaert (1995). Otherwise, name structures by
#'   their three-letter codes, as [multilpa()]'s `model` takes them: the
#'   letters give the volume, shape and orientation of each profile's
#'   covariance matrix, each equal (`E`) or varying (`V`) across profiles,
#'   with `I` for no covariances. `NULL` crosses no structures. With one
#'   continuous indicator, codes that coincide (equal or varying variance)
#'   are fitted once; with only categorical indicators no structure is
#'   crossed. A structure set through `variance_model`, `covariance_model`,
#'   `volume`, `shape` or `orientation` in `...` replaces the default.
#' @param seed Optional seed for each fit: a whole number `set.seed()`
#'   accepts. Anything else raises `latents_bad_argument` before any candidate
#'   is fitted.
#' @param family `"profiles"` (the default) enumerates the profile model over
#'   `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes` and `model`. One or more of the
#'   group-class families `"additive"`, `"dispersion"` and
#'   `"additive_dispersion"` enumerates those instead, over `family`,
#'   `n_group_classes` and `between_variance`; these need `id`, `n_profiles`
#'   and `model` are then refused, and the result is a
#'   `latents_family_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and
#'   [get_candidate()].
#' @param between_variance For group-class families: the between-variance
#'   restrictions to cross, `"varying"`, `"equal"` or both (the default). The
#'   dispersion family is always fitted with `"equal"`. Refused for the
#'   profile family.
#' @param time The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models
#'   ([lta()]) over `n_profiles` (default `2:4`) and `n_group_classes`
#'   (default `1`), with every other `lta()` argument given in `...` held
#'   fixed. `model`, when given, crosses those covariance structures. Only
#'   the profile family is available. The result is a
#'   `latents_transition_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and
#'   [get_candidate()].
#' @param cores Number of processor cores to fit the candidates on (default
#'   1). Each candidate sets and restores its own random seed, so with `seed`
#'   given the result is identical to `cores = 1`. Candidates are fitted by
#'   forked processes on macOS and Linux, and by a socket cluster on Windows
#'   and on macOS when R uses Apple's Accelerate BLAS (socket workers load the
#'   installed package). Warnings and messages from the workers are passed on
#'   in grid order once all have finished. Without `seed`, the random starts
#'   differ between runs on any number of cores. Lost worker results are retried
#'   once with half as many workers (rounded up). One `latents_worker_lost`
#'   warning reports how many tasks were lost and recovered, and suggests fewer
#'   cores. A task still lost becomes a failed start (for flat start grids) or
#'   a failed candidate; the other results are retained. On sockets, bounded
#'   chunks preserve earlier results when a connection breaks; completed tasks
#'   within the failed chunk may also be retried. Each core holds its own copy
#'   of the fits it computes; `parallel::detectCores()` gives the number
#'   available.
#'   Transition grids (`time`) and profile grids (including categorical-only
#'   latent class models) distribute individual starts across one pool,
#'   longest estimated first, with at most `cores` workers and no nested
#'   workers. Both emEM screening and finalist runs use the pool; `search`
#'   keeps the same defaults as [multilpa()]. Setup, ordered starting values,
#'   start selection and finalisation stay in the current process. Profile
#'   models with membership covariates or joined categorical `local_dependence`
#'   pairs instead occupy one worker per candidate in the same pool, with
#'   serial starts. Group-class families also keep candidate-level parallelism.
#' @param verbose Whether to report progress: one message each when the
#'   candidates are prepared, when their starts are fitted, and when the grid
#'   is done, with the elapsed time. The default reports when `cores > 1`,
#'   where a grid is usually long. Group-class families (`family`) are not
#'   reported.
#' @param type Optional model type: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`. `NULL`
#'   (the default) keeps the existing routing and measurement settings.
#'   `"lca"` treats every indicator as categorical, as [multilca()] does:
#'   indicators named in `ordinal` or `count` keep those distributions, and
#'   `categorical` adds to the set rather than replacing it. Numeric response
#'   codes are categorical with `type = "lca"`. `"lpa"` requires continuous
#'   indicators and refuses non-empty `categorical`, `ordinal` or `count`.
#'   Both require `time = NULL`. `"lta"` requires `time` and takes its
#'   measurement settings from `categorical`, as [lta()] does; it does not
#'   make numeric indicators categorical. An explicit type requires
#'   `family = "profiles"`; leave `type = NULL` for group-class families.
#' @param ... Further arguments to [multilpa()] (or to [lta()] with `time`),
#'   applied to every candidate, such as `n_starts` (random starts per
#'   candidate), `max_iter`, `missing`, `categorical`, `centering`, `scaling`,
#'   `drop_empty` and `boundary` (`"exclude"` sets aside starts with a
#'   variance at `min_variance`, degenerate solutions that become more likely
#'   as `n_starts` grows). For example, `enumerate_classes(data, vars, id,
#'   n_profiles = 2:6, n_starts = 20, seed = 1)`. Group-class families take
#'   only `n_starts`, `max_iter`, `tol` and `min_variance`.
#' @return An object of class `multilpa_enumeration` (or the transition or
#'   family enumeration described above). Its `type` records the resolved
#'   model: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`, or `"mixed"`/`"family"` for
#'   those grids under `type = NULL`. The print header shows this type; table
#'   columns are unchanged. [as.data.frame()] gives
#'   one row per candidate, starting with its name (`"profiles3_groups2"`),
#'   with every criterion and diagnostic (including both entropies and, at
#'   each level, the smallest, largest and mean average posterior probability
#'   and the number of classes below a cutoff) and the candidate's warnings
#'   and error. `get_results(x, "best")` names the candidate at each
#'   criterion's minimum; `get_results(x, "classification")` gives every
#'   class's average posterior probability and relative entropy for every
#'   candidate; `get_results(x, "deltas")` and `"knees"` give model-selection
#'   evidence. [summary()] prints each criterion's minimum and every table,
#'   [plot()] draws the information criteria (and, with `what`,
#'   classification quality and model-selection views), [get_candidate()]
#'   returns the fitted model of one candidate, and [compare_models()] puts
#'   candidates side by side; these verbs take candidates by name.
#' @seealso [get_candidate()] to take one fitted model out of the grid,
#'   `summary()` for the criterion-by-criterion comparison.
#' @section Conditions:
#'   `latents_bad_argument` when `model` names an unknown structure, when it is
#'   given together with another way of setting the structure, or when it is
#'   given although no indicator is continuous; when `seed` is not a seed

#'   not take; when `n_group_classes` other than 1 is given with `id = NULL`;
#'   when `id` is missing; when `between_variance` is given for the profile
#'   family; when `n_profiles` or `model` is given for a group-class family,
#'   or `id` is `NULL`; when `time` is combined with a group-class family or
#'   with `between_variance`; and when `cores` is not a whole number of at

#' @references
#' Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (1995). Gaussian parsimonious clustering models.
#' *Pattern Recognition*, 28(5), 781--793.
#' @examples
#' set.seed(1)
#' d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100))
#' candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,
#'                               n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#' as.data.frame(candidates)
#' summary(candidates)
#'
#' # Numeric response codes, explicitly categorical:

#' classes <- enumerate_classes(codes, "item", "g", type = "lca",
#'                              n_profiles = 1, n_group_classes = 1,
#'                              n_starts = 1, seed = 1)
#'
#' # Single level, crossing class counts with two named structures:
#' single <- enumerate_lpa(iris, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width",
#'                                 "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),
#'                         n_profiles = 1:3, model = c("VVV", "EEE"),
#'                         n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#' summary(single)
#' @export

                              n_group_classes = 1:3, model = "basic",
                              seed = NULL, family = "profiles",

  # worker cannot find. The transition and family paths never touch `data`

                          if (missing(n_group_classes)) 1L else n_group_classes,
                          if (missing(model)) NULL else model, seed, list(...),

    return(result)
  }
  if (!identical(family, "profiles")) {

    # structure codes; they are enumerated over family and class count.

        "Group-class families take `id`, `family`, `n_group_classes` and",
        "`between_variance`; `n_profiles` and `model` belong to the profile model."),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    result <- .latents_report_once(.additive_enumerate(data, vars, id, family,
                                  n_group_classes, between_variance, seed, list(...),
                                  match.call(), cores = cores))

    return(result)
  }

      "`between_variance` belongs to the group-class families (`family = `).",
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))

    }
    n_group_classes <- 1L
  }
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(data), is.character(vars),
            "`id` must be a single column name, or NULL for single-level models" =
              single_level || (is.character(id) && length(id) == 1L),

            all(is.finite(n_profiles)), all(n_profiles >= 1), all(n_profiles == as.integer(n_profiles)),
            is.numeric(n_group_classes), length(n_group_classes) > 0L,
            all(is.finite(n_group_classes)), all(n_group_classes >= 1),
            all(n_group_classes == as.integer(n_group_classes)),

                                   !anyNA(model)))

  # with "matched by multiple actual arguments" before `...` is assembled.
  extra <- list(...)

    extra$categorical <- .latents_lca_categorical(vars, extra)
  }
  if (identical(type, "lpa")) {
    conflicts <- c("categorical", "ordinal", "count")
    conflicts <- conflicts[vapply(extra[conflicts], length, integer(1)) > 0L]
    if (length(conflicts)) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "`type = \"lpa\"` requires continuous indicators and conflicts with %s.",
        "Remove those measurement arguments, or use `type = NULL` for a mixed model."),
        paste(sprintf("`%s`", conflicts), collapse = ", ")),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    # Empty declarations carry no distribution under an all-continuous type.
    extra[intersect(names(extra), c("categorical", "ordinal", "count"))] <- NULL
  }

  # candidate and be recorded as a grid of failures; refuse it here instead.
  unknown_arguments <- setdiff(names(extra), names(formals(multilpa)))

      "%s %s not an argument of multilpa().%s",
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", unknown_arguments), collapse = ", "),
      if (length(unknown_arguments) == 1L) "is" else "are", hint),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }

  # is crossed, and each candidate is fitted as `multilpa()` would fit it.
  grid <- expand.grid(n_profiles = unique(n_profiles),
                      n_group_classes = unique(n_group_classes),
                      model = .multilpa_enumeration_models(
                        model, model_given, vars, extra),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  indices <- seq_len(nrow(grid))
  requested <- lapply(grid$model, .multilpa_enumeration_arguments,
                       vars = vars, extra = extra)
  arguments <- lapply(indices, function(i) c(
    list(data = data, vars = vars, id = id, n_profiles = grid$n_profiles[i],
         n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes[i], seed = seed),
    requested[[i]], extra))
  calls <- lapply(indices, function(i) .latents_candidate_call(
    "multilpa", data_expression, arguments[[i]][setdiff(names(arguments[[i]]), "data")]))
  costs <- grid$n_group_classes * grid$n_profiles *
    .multilpa_pool_width(data, vars, extra)
  fitted <- .multilpa_enumerate_fits(arguments, calls, costs, cores, verbose)
  # The candidates' conditions come back deferred and are signalled here,
  # candidate by candidate.
  runs <- .latents_report_once(lapply(indices, function(i) {
    conditions <- Filter(function(condition) !inherits(condition, "latents_single_level"),
                          fitted[[i]]$conditions)
    .latents_signal_conditions(conditions)
    warnings <- vapply(Filter(function(condition) inherits(condition, "warning"),
                               conditions), conditionMessage, character(1))
    failed <- inherits(fitted[[i]]$value, "error")
    fit <- if (failed) NULL else fitted[[i]]$value
    error_text <- if (failed) conditionMessage(fitted[[i]]$value) else NA_character_
    row <- cbind(
      data.frame(n_profiles = grid$n_profiles[i], n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes[i],
        # A latent class model has no covariance structure; naming one (the
        # default the fit records for its absent Gaussian block) misleads.
        model = if (is.null(fit)) grid$model[i] else
          if (length(.multilpa_continuous_names(fit)) == 0L) NA_character_ else
            .latents_comparison_structure(fit),
        log_likelihood = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else fit$log_likelihood,
        n_parameters = if (is.null(fit)) NA_integer_ else fit$n_parameters,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
      .multilpa_enumeration_indices(fit),
      data.frame(
        profile_entropy = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else
          .multilpa_relative_entropy(.multilpa_classified_posteriors(fit)),
        group_entropy = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else
          .multilpa_relative_entropy(.multilpa_classified_group_posteriors(fit)),
        converged = !is.null(fit) && fit$converged,
        boundary = if (is.null(fit)) NA else fit$boundary,
        min_standardized_eigenvalue = .latents_gaussian_minimum(
          fit, "min_standardized_eigenvalue"),
        min_gaussian_mass = .latents_gaussian_minimum(fit, "gaussian_mass"),
        n_best_replicated = if (is.null(fit)) NA_integer_ else fit$n_best_replicated %||% NA_integer_,
        warnings = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = "; "), error = error_text))
    list(fit = fit, row = row)
  }))
  if (single_level) {
    .multilpa_single_level_notice(
      latent_class = all(vars %in% extra$categorical))
  }
  result <- list(table = do.call(rbind, lapply(runs, `[[`, "row")),
       fits = lapply(runs, `[[`, "fit"), call = match.call())
  class(result) <- "multilpa_enumeration"
  result$type <- type %||% .latents_enumeration_measurement_type(vars, extra)
  names(result$fits) <- .latents_candidate_names(result)
  result
}

old_inventory_record.name: enumerate_classes
old_inventory_record.documentation: Enumerate numbers of individual profiles and group classes  Fits every requested combination of profile count, group-class count and covariance structure and returns the candidates with their information criteria and classification diagnostics. Errors and warnings of each candidate are kept in the table alongside the successful fits. Information criteria are descriptive: neither the smallest BIC nor high entropy guarantees the correct number of classes. Unconverged, boundary and unreplicated fits are reported, not silently selected. @param data Data frame. @param vars Indicator column names. @param id The column identifying the groups the observations are nested in   (students in schools, reports in students). Required; `NULL` enumerates   single-level models, with a message. [enumerate_lpa()] and   [enumerate_lca()] fit single-level models directly. @param n_profiles Positive integer profile counts to try. Default `1:4`. @param n_group_classes Positive integer group-class counts to try. Default   `1:3`. With `id = NULL` it is 1 and may be left out. @param model The covariance structures to cross with the class counts.   `"basic"` (the default) fits four structures: `"EEI"` (equal variances,   no covariances), `"VVI"` (varying variances, no covariances), `"EEE"`   (one covariance matrix shared by all profiles) and `"VVV"` (a covariance   matrix for each profile). Omitting covariances between correlated   indicators tends to favour additional profiles. `"all"` fits all 14   structures of Celeux and Govaert (1995). Otherwise, name structures by   their three-letter codes, as [multilpa()]'s `model` takes them: the   letters give the volume, shape and orientation of each profile's   covariance matrix, each equal (`E`) or varying (`V`) across profiles,   with `I` for no covariances. `NULL` crosses no structures. With one   continuous indicator, codes that coincide (equal or varying variance)   are fitted once; with only categorical indicators no structure is   crossed. A structure set through `variance_model`, `covariance_model`,   `volume`, `shape` or `orientation` in `...` replaces the default. @param seed Optional seed for each fit: a whole number `set.seed()`   accepts. Anything else raises `latents_bad_argument` before any candidate   is fitted. @param family `"profiles"` (the default) enumerates the profile model over   `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes` and `model`. One or more of the   group-class families `"additive"`, `"dispersion"` and   `"additive_dispersion"` enumerates those instead, over `family`,   `n_group_classes` and `between_variance`; these need `id`, `n_profiles`   and `model` are then refused, and the result is a   `latents_family_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and   [get_candidate()]. @param between_variance For group-class families: the between-variance   restrictions to cross, `"varying"`, `"equal"` or both (the default). The   dispersion family is always fitted with `"equal"`. Refused for the   profile family. @param time The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models   ([lta()]) over `n_profiles` (default `2:4`) and `n_group_classes`   (default `1`), with every other `lta()` argument given in `...` held   fixed. `model`, when given, crosses those covariance structures. Only   the profile family is available. The result is a   `latents_transition_enumeration`, read with [get_results()] and   [get_candidate()]. @param cores Number of processor cores to fit the candidates on (default   1). Each candidate sets and restores its own random seed, so with `seed`   given the result is identical to `cores = 1`. Candidates are fitted by   forked processes on macOS and Linux, and by a socket cluster on Windows   and on macOS when R uses Apple's Accelerate BLAS (socket workers load the   installed package). Warnings and messages from the workers are passed on   in grid order once all have finished. Without `seed`, the random starts   differ between runs on any number of cores. Lost worker results are retried   once with half as many workers (rounded up). One `latents_worker_lost`   warning reports how many tasks were lost and recovered, and suggests fewer   cores. A task still lost becomes a failed start (for flat start grids) or   a failed candidate; the other results are retained. On sockets, bounded   chunks preserve earlier results when a connection breaks; completed tasks   within the failed chunk may also be retried. Each core holds its own copy   of the fits it computes; `parallel::detectCores()` gives the number   available.   Transition grids (`time`) and profile grids (including categorical-only   latent class models) distribute individual starts across one pool,   longest estimated first, with at most `cores` workers and no nested   workers. Both emEM screening and finalist runs use the pool; `search`   keeps the same defaults as [multilpa()]. Setup, ordered starting values,   start selection and finalisation stay in the current process. Profile   models with membership covariates or joined categorical `local_dependence`   pairs instead occupy one worker per candidate in the same pool, with   serial starts. Group-class families also keep candidate-level parallelism. @param verbose Whether to report progress: one message each when the   candidates are prepared, when their starts are fitted, and when the grid   is done, with the elapsed time. The default reports when `cores > 1`,   where a grid is usually long. Group-class families (`family`) are not   reported. @param type Optional model type: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`. `NULL`   (the default) keeps the existing routing and measurement settings.   `"lca"` treats every indicator as categorical, as [multilca()] does:   indicators named in `ordinal` or `count` keep those distributions, and   `categorical` adds to the set rather than replacing it. Numeric response   codes are categorical with `type = "lca"`. `"lpa"` requires continuous   indicators and refuses non-empty `categorical`, `ordinal` or `count`.   Both require `time = NULL`. `"lta"` requires `time` and takes its   measurement settings from `categorical`, as [lta()] does; it does not   make numeric indicators categorical. An explicit type requires   `family = "profiles"`; leave `type = NULL` for group-class families. @param ... Further arguments to [multilpa()] (or to [lta()] with `time`),   applied to every candidate, such as `n_starts` (random starts per   candidate), `max_iter`, `missing`, `categorical`, `centering`, `scaling`,   `drop_empty` and `boundary` (`"exclude"` sets aside starts with a   variance at `min_variance`, degenerate solutions that become more likely   as `n_starts` grows). For example, `enumerate_classes(data, vars, id,   n_profiles = 2:6, n_starts = 20, seed = 1)`. Group-class families take   only `n_starts`, `max_iter`, `tol` and `min_variance`. @return An object of class `multilpa_enumeration` (or the transition or   family enumeration described above). Its `type` records the resolved   model: `"lca"`, `"lpa"` or `"lta"`, or `"mixed"`/`"family"` for   those grids under `type = NULL`. The print header shows this type; table   columns are unchanged. [as.data.frame()] gives   one row per candidate, starting with its name (`"profiles3_groups2"`),   with every criterion and diagnostic (including both entropies and, at   each level, the smallest, largest and mean average posterior probability   and the number of classes below a cutoff) and the candidate's warnings   and error. `get_results(x, "best")` names the candidate at each   criterion's minimum; `get_results(x, "classification")` gives every   class's average posterior probability and relative entropy for every   candidate; `get_results(x, "deltas")` and `"knees"` give model-selection   evidence. [summary()] prints each criterion's minimum and every table,   [plot()] draws the information criteria (and, with `what`,   classification quality and model-selection views), [get_candidate()]   returns the fitted model of one candidate, and [compare_models()] puts   candidates side by side; these verbs take candidates by name. @seealso [get_candidate()] to take one fitted model out of the grid,   `summary()` for the criterion-by-criterion comparison. @section Conditions:   `latents_bad_argument` when `model` names an unknown structure, when it is   given together with another way of setting the structure, or when it is   given although no indicator is continuous; when `seed` is not a seed   `set.seed()` accepts; when `...` contains an argument [multilpa()] does   not take; when `n_group_classes` other than 1 is given with `id = NULL`;   when `id` is missing; when `between_variance` is given for the profile   family; when `n_profiles` or `model` is given for a group-class family,   or `id` is `NULL`; when `time` is combined with a group-class family or   with `between_variance`; and when `cores` is not a whole number of at   least 1; and when `type` is invalid or conflicts with `time`, `family`   or the requested measurement distributions. @references Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (1995). Gaussian parsimonious clustering models. *Pattern Recognition*, 28(5), 781--793. @examples set.seed(1) d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100)) candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,                               n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) as.data.frame(candidates) summary(candidates)  # Numeric response codes, explicitly categorical: codes <- data.frame(g = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10), item = rep(0:1, 50)) classes <- enumerate_classes(codes, "item", "g", type = "lca",                              n_profiles = 1, n_group_classes = 1,                              n_starts = 1, seed = 1)  # Single level, crossing class counts with two named structures: single <- enumerate_lpa(iris, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width",                                 "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),                         n_profiles = 1:3, model = c("VVV", "EEE"),                         n_starts = 2, seed = 1) summary(single) @export

#' Take one fitted model out of an enumeration grid or a comparison
#'
#' Returns one fitted model from an enumeration, selected by its name or by
#' its number of profiles and group classes (and its covariance structure when
#' the grid has several), or one model from a comparison, selected by its row
#' label.
#'
#' A candidate is selected by its name, as the grid's `candidate` column shows
#' it (`get_candidate(grid, "profiles3_groups4")`; `classes` instead of
#' `profiles` when every indicator is categorical); by its class counts,
#' `get_candidate(grid, 3, 4)` or `get_candidate(grid, c(3, 4))`; or, on a grid
#' that crosses covariance structures, by its counts and `model`. From a
#' comparison, give the row label: `get_candidate(comparison,
#' "profiles3_groups4")`.
#'
#' @param x An enumeration grid from [enumerate_classes()] (a profile, latent
#'   class, transition or group-class family grid), or a comparison from
#'   [compare_models()]. On a family grid, give the name, or `n_group_classes`
#'   with `model`.
#' @param n_profiles Number of individual profiles of the candidate, the
#'   candidate's name (`"profiles3_groups4"`), or its two class counts
#'   (`c(3, 4)`). For a comparison, the row label, as its `model` column shows
#'   it.
#' @param n_group_classes Number of group classes of the candidate. Default 1.
#' @param model The covariance structure of the candidate, needed when
#'   [enumerate_classes()] crossed several structures and the class counts
#'   match several candidates; on a group-class family grid, the family model
#'   as the grid's `model` column shows it.
#' @return The fitted model of that candidate, the same kind of object its
#'   fitting function returns (for a profile grid, class `multilpa`), so the
#'   verbs for a fitted model apply to it.
#' @section Conditions:
#'   `latents_unknown_candidate` for a name or class counts not in the grid,
#'   for counts that match several candidates (the message lists their
#'   names), and for a label that is not a row of a comparison;
#'   `latents_failed_candidate` when the candidate's fit raised an error, so
#'   there is no model to return; `latents_bad_argument` for a name or pair of
#'   counts given together with `n_group_classes` or `model`, for a value that
#'   names no candidate, and for a comparison given no label;
#'   `latents_incomplete_fit` for a comparison that no longer carries its
#'   models. Counts that are not single positive whole numbers fail the
#'   argument checks.
#' @examples
#' set.seed(1)
#' d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100))
#' candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,
#'                               n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)

#' get_candidate(candidates, "profiles2_groups1_VVI")

#'                            "profiles2_groups1_VVI")
#' get_candidate(compared, "profiles2_groups1_VVI")
#' @export

before.documentation:
#' Check the class counts that name a candidate
#' @param n_profiles,n_group_classes The counts [get_candidate()] received.
#' @return `NULL`, invisibly; an argument error for anything but a single

before.name: .multilpa_enumeration_minima
before.documentation:
#' Which candidate minimises each information criterion
#' @param grid The enumeration table.
#' @return One row per criterion carried by the grid.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_enumeration_minima <- function(grid) {
  present <- intersect(.multilpa_enumeration_criteria(), names(grid))
  eligible <- grid$converged %in% TRUE
  rows <- lapply(present, function(name) {
    values <- grid[[name]]
    values[!eligible] <- NA_real_
    best <- if (all(is.na(values))) NA_integer_ else which.min(values)
    data.frame(
      criterion = sub("_(groups|individual)$", "", name),
      convention = if (grepl("_groups$", name)) "groups" else
        if (grepl("_individual$", name)) "individuals" else NA_character_,
      candidate = if (is.na(best) || is.null(grid$candidate)) NA_character_ else
        grid$candidate[best],
      n_profiles = if (is.na(best)) NA_integer_ else
        as.integer(grid$n_profiles[best]),
      n_group_classes = if (is.na(best)) NA_integer_ else
        as.integer(grid$n_group_classes[best]),
      model = if (is.na(best)) NA_character_ else
        as.character(grid$model[best]),
      value = if (is.na(best)) NA_real_ else values[best],
      row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
