after.documentation:
#' Extract the result tables of a fitted model
#'
#' Returns one tidy table of a fitted model or related object, named by
#' `what`, as a base `data.frame`; `what = "all"` returns every table the
#' object offers as a named list. The tables available depend on the class of
#' the object and are listed under *Tables*.
#'
#' Every object also has `print()`, which shows a compact overview,
#' `summary()`, which collects its main tables (taking `level` and
#' `vcov_type` where the model has standard errors), and `as.data.frame()`,
#' which returns its primary table, the same as `get_results(x)`.
#'
#' Tables joining caller-supplied columns to fitted rows check their alignment.
#' Numeric columns may also match R's canonical CSV serialization, provided
#' that serialization does not merge distinct values. This row-alignment check
#' differs from the stricter fitted-data checks used for inference and model
#' comparison; supplying unrelated columns alone cannot verify row order.
#'
#' @param x A fitted model of this package, an enumeration grid, a model
#'   comparison, a bootstrap comparison, a starting-value set, a
#'   classification-diagnostics object, or the summary of any of them.
#' @param what Name of the table to return, or `"all"` for every table the
#'   object offers. `NULL` (default) returns the primary table: the
#'   measurement model for a fit, the candidate grid for an enumeration, the
#'   test row for a bootstrap comparison and the entropy table for a
#'   diagnostics object. A name the object does not offer raises
#'   `latents_bad_argument`, listing the names it does offer.
#' @param ... Arguments for the requested table. Each table accepts only the
#'   arguments listed for it under *Tables*; any other argument raises
#'   `latents_bad_argument`.
#'
#' @section Tables:
#' Every fitted model offers these:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{`"profiles"`}{The Gaussian measurement model, one row per profile
#'     and continuous indicator: `profile`, `indicator`, `mean`, `variance`,
#'     `standard_deviation`, `mean_standard_error`, `variance_standard_error`.
#'     Zero rows, with the same columns, when every indicator is categorical.
#'     Takes `scale` and `data`.}
#'   \item{`"responses"`}{The categorical measurement model, one row per
#'     profile, categorical indicator and category: `profile`, `indicator`,
#'     `category`, `probability`, `threshold`, `probability_standard_error`.
#'     `threshold` is `qlogis(P(y <= category))` and is `NA_real_` for each
#'     indicator's final category; a probability on its bound has an
#'     `NA_real_` standard error. Zero rows, with the same columns, when no
#'     indicator is categorical. Takes `data`.}
#'   \item{`"covariances"`}{The within-profile residual covariance matrices,
#'     one row per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators:
#'     `profile`, `indicator`, `indicator_2`, `covariance`. Under the diagonal
#'     parameterization the off-diagonal covariances are reported as exact
#'     zeros.}
#'   \item{`"ordinal"`, `"count_means"`}{Fits with ordinal or count
#'     indicators only: the ordinal and count measurement models. Take
#'     `data`.}
#'   \item{`"counts"`}{Effective class sizes, one row per class at each level
#'     of the fit: `level`, `class`, `effective_count` (the summed posteriors)
#'     and `effective_proportion`. These differ from the modal counts in
#'     `"classification"` whenever entropy is below one.}
#'   \item{`"model"`}{One row describing the fit: its dimensions, likelihood,
#'     parameter counts, `aic`, `bic_groups`, `bic_individual` and its
#'     convergence and boundary diagnostics. The columns differ by family (a
#'     covariate fit adds its predictor counts); `"information_criteria"` has
#'     the same columns for every family.}
#'   \item{`"posteriors"`}{One row per individual and profile: `row`, `group`,
#'     `profile`, `posterior`, `modal`. Takes `format`.}
#'   \item{`"assignments"`}{One row per observation: the columns the fit was
#'     built from (or those of `data`), then `profile`, `group_class` where the
#'     model has one, `uncertainty` (one minus the posterior of the assigned
#'     profile) and one `posterior_profile_*` column per profile, plus
#'     `posterior_noise` for a fit with a noise component (whose cases are
#'     profile 0). Takes `data` and `truth`; with `truth` it returns a recovery
#'     table instead (see *Recovery*).}
#'   \item{`"classification"`}{Classification quality, one row per level and
#'     class: `level`, `class`, `n_modal`, `proportion_modal`, `estimated_n`,
#'     `estimated_proportion`, `average_posterior`,
#'     `odds_correct_classification`. Takes `level`. Under sampling weights
#'     `estimated_n` and `estimated_proportion` (and hence the odds of correct
#'     classification) are weighted posterior totals; the modal and average
#'     posterior columns describe the units supplied. The odds are `Inf` for a
#'     class classified perfectly (average posterior one to within rounding)
#'     and `NA` where they are undefined: a class with no modal members, or a
#'     single class, whose proportion is one.}
#'   \item{`"average_posteriors"`}{For the units modally assigned to each
#'     class, their mean posterior for every class: `level`, `assigned_class`,
#'     `class`, `n_assigned`, `average_posterior`. Rows sum to one within each
#'     assigned class. This conditions on the assigned class, whereas
#'     `"classification_errors"` conditions on the true class. Takes `level`.}
#'   \item{`"classification_errors"`}{The probability that a unit in one true
#'     class is assigned to another: `level`, `true_class`, `assigned_class`,
#'     `probability`, summing to one within each `true_class`. Takes `level`.
#'     On a membership-covariate fit this is a marginal summary over the fitted
#'     units, not conditional on the covariates. A fit with a noise component
#'     raises `latents_unsupported_noise`, as [three_step()] does, and `"all"`
#'     and `summary()` omit the table.}
#'   \item{`"bch_weights"`}{The BCH inverse-error weights, one row per unit and
#'     class: `level`, `unit`, `assigned_class`, `class`, `weight`. Takes
#'     `level`; a weighted regression should use one level, not `"both"`. On a
#'     membership-covariate fit the weights invert the marginal error matrix
#'     and are not a conditional three-step correction. Not available for a fit
#'     with a noise component, as for `"classification_errors"`.}
#'   \item{`"entropy"`}{One row per level: `level`, `n_classes`, `n_units`,
#'     `entropy_sum`, `relative_entropy`.}
#'   \item{`"residuals"`}{Bivariate residuals for every indicator pair, testing
#'     within-profile independence: `profile`, `indicator_1`, `indicator_2`,
#'     `kind`, `observed`, `expected`, `residual`, `effective_n`, `statistic`,
#'     `df`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`. Takes `data`, `by` and `adjust`.}
#'   \item{`"information_criteria"`}{Every information criterion the package
#'     computes (see *Information criteria*). Takes `format` and
#'     `definitions`.}
#'   \item{`"sequences"`}{The assignments in occasion order, one row per
#'     observation: `group`, `group_class`, `time`, `profile`. Takes `format`.
#'     Raises `latents_no_time` for a fit made without `time`.}
#'   \item{`"sequence_summary"`}{One row per group class: `group_class`,
#'     `groups`, `observations`, `mean_length`, `median_length`, `shortest`,
#'     `longest`, `complete`, `gaps`. Raises `latents_no_time` for a fit made
#'     without `time`.}
#'   \item{`"starts"`}{One row per EM start: `start`, `log_likelihood`,
#'     `converged`, `iterations`, `error` and, where the family records it,
#'     `boundary`. Under `search = "emEM"`, one row per start of the pool,
#'     with its `kind`, its `stage` (`"final"` when run to convergence,
#'     `"screened"` otherwise) and its `screened_log_likelihood`.}
#'   \item{`"data"`}{The data the model was fitted to, one row per observation
#'     in input order: the identifier (except for a single-level fit), the
#'     occasion where there is one, the sampling weights of a weighted fit (as
#'     rescaled for fitting) and the indicators under their original names.
#'     Columns the model did not use, including membership covariates, are not
#'     included; [three_step()] and [r3step()] therefore take `data`.}
#' }
#' Fits with discrete group classes also offer:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{`"group_posteriors"`}{One row per observed group and group class:
#'     `group`, `group_size`, `log_likelihood`, `group_class`, `posterior`,
#'     `modal`. Takes `format`.}
#' }
#' Tables specific to one family or object:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{`"gaussian_diagnostics"`}{Gaussian profile, membership-covariate,
#'     transition and cross-level fits that record these diagnostics. One row
#'     per Gaussian component and measurement context: `context`, `profile`,
#'     `gaussian_mass`, `positive_rows`, `weight_effective_n`,
#'     `min_variance_ratio`, `min_standardized_eigenvalue`, `boundary`.
#'     `gaussian_mass` sums posterior times normalized sampling weight over
#'     rows with at least one observed Gaussian indicator; `positive_rows`
#'     counts rows with positive contributions. `weight_effective_n` is the
#'     concentration measure `(sum(a)^2 / sum(a^2))` for those contributions,
#'     not an identification guarantee; Gaussian mass is not this effective
#'     sample size. `min_variance_ratio` is the smallest component variance
#'     divided by its observed sampling-weighted marginal variance on the
#'     fitted scale, including between-component variation.
#'     `min_standardized_eigenvalue` is the smallest eigenvalue of the
#'     component covariance after standardizing every indicator by its
#'     observed sampling-weighted marginal standard deviation. Missing reference
#'     variation gives `NA` ratios. `boundary` concerns the absolute variance
#'     or eigenvalue floor. These descriptive measures use no automatic spike
#'     cutoff and do not alter start selection.}
#'   \item{`"profile_probabilities"`, `"stages"`}{A `multilpa` fit.
#'     `"profile_probabilities"` has one row per group class and profile:
#'     `group_class`, `profile`, `probability`, `group_class_probability`.
#'     `"stages"` has one row per estimation stage: `stage`, `group_classes`,
#'     `fixed`, `log_likelihood`, `parameters`, `parameters_with_measurement`,
#'     `converged`. An ordinary fit has one `"joint"` row and a [fit_staged()]
#'     result has two; `fixed` is `NA_character_` for a stage that estimated
#'     every block.}
#'   \item{`"coefficients"`}{A covariate fit. One row per estimated membership
#'     coefficient: `level` (`"profile"` or `"group"`), `outcome`, `term`,
#'     `parameter` (always `"logit"`), `estimate`. Standard errors are given by
#'     [parameter_inference()].}
#'   \item{`"transitions"`, `"initial"`, `"sequence_lengths"`}{A transition
#'     fit. `"transitions"` has one row per group class and ordered pair of
#'     profiles: `group_class`, `from`, `to`, `probability`, `expected_count`,
#'     `stable`, `estimated`, `group_class_probability`; it takes `estimated`
#'     and `stable`. `"initial"` has one row per group class and profile:
#'     `group_class`, `profile`, `probability`, `prevalence`,
#'     `group_class_probability`. `"sequence_lengths"` has one row per group:
#'     `group`, `group_class`, `occasions`, `observations`, `complete`.}
#'   \item{`"candidates"`, `"best"`, `"classification"`}{An enumeration
#'     grid. `"candidates"` has one row per candidate model: its name
#'     (`candidate`, first), its class counts, covariance `model`, log
#'     likelihood, parameter count, every criterion under both sample-size
#'     conventions, both entropies, the average posterior probability (AvePP)
#'     summaries of each level (`avepp_min`, `avepp_max`, `avepp_mean`,
#'     `avepp_below` and the same four prefixed `group_`) and the convergence,
#'     boundary, replication, warning and error diagnostics, including
#'     `min_standardized_eigenvalue` and `min_gaussian_mass` where Gaussian
#'     diagnostics are available. These are descriptive summaries, without
#'     an automatic cutoff or change to candidate selection. Failed candidates
#'     are kept with `NA` estimates and their error text. It takes `cutoff`
#'     (default `0.8`): `avepp_below` and `group_avepp_below` count the classes
#'     whose AvePP is below it. A class with no modally assigned unit has no
#'     AvePP; it is excluded from the minimum, maximum and mean and counted as
#'     below the cutoff. A level with one class has `NA` summaries. `"best"`
#'     has one row per information criterion and sample-size convention:
#'     `criterion`, `convention`, `candidate` (the converged candidate with the
#'     lowest value), `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`, `model` and `value`;
#'     `what = "criteria"` is accepted as a deprecated name for it.
#'     `"classification"` has one row per fitted candidate, level and class:
#'     `candidate`, `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`, `model`, then the columns
#'     of a fit's `"classification"` table and that level's
#'     `relative_entropy`. Failed candidates and single-class levels
#'     contribute no rows.}
#'   \item{`"deltas"`, `"knees"`}{Model-selection evidence of an enumeration
#'     grid, each taking `using` (default `"bic_groups"`). Neither selects a
#'     model. `"deltas"` has one row per candidate: `candidate`, its class
#'     counts and `model`, `criterion`, `value`, `delta_profile` (the decrease
#'     in the criterion from the converged candidate with one profile fewer,
#'     the same group classes and the same structure; positive means this
#'     candidate is lower), `from_profile` naming that candidate, and
#'     `delta_group_class` with `from_group_class` for one group class fewer.
#'     `value` and both deltas are `NA` for a candidate that did not converge,
#'     and a delta is `NA` when the smaller neighbour is missing or did not
#'     converge. `"knees"` has one row per line of the grid: `direction`
#'     (`"profiles"`, along the profiles at fixed group classes;
#'     `"group_classes"`, along the group classes at fixed profiles;
#'     `"parameters"`, every candidate by its number of parameters, one line
#'     per structure), `line`, `criterion`, `from`, `to`, `n_points`,
#'     `knee_candidate`, `distance`, `knee_without_largest` (the knee when the
#'     last candidate of the line is left out), `stable` and `note`. The knee
#'     is the candidate furthest below the straight line from the first to the
#'     last candidate, measured perpendicular to it with both axes rescaled to
#'     0-1. This is a simplified rule inspired by Kneedle (Satopaa et al.,
#'     2011), without its smoothing or sensitivity thresholds, so a very small positive distance
#'     can still name a knee. A line needs three candidates for a knee and four
#'     for `knee_without_largest` and `stable`; otherwise they are `NA` and
#'     `note` gives the reason.}
#'   \item{`"local_dependence"`}{For a fit with `local_dependence`: `pair`,
#'     `kind` (`"categorical"` or `"continuous"`), `profile`, `item_1`,
#'     `category_1`, `item_2`, `category_2`, `probability`, `independent`,
#'     `ratio`, `covariance` and `correlation`. A categorical pair has one row
#'     per profile and combination of the two items' categories: the fitted
#'     joint `probability`, the product of the two marginal probabilities
#'     (`independent`, the joint probability under independence within the
#'     profile) and their `ratio`; its covariance columns are `NA`. A
#'     continuous pair has one row per profile, with the pair's `covariance`
#'     and the `correlation` it implies; its category and probability
#'     columns are `NA`. A fit without pairs raises
#'     `latents_no_local_dependence`, and `what = "all"` leaves the table out.}
#'   \item{`"direct_effects"`}{For a fit with `direct_effects`, one row per
#'     effect: `indicator`, `covariate`, `estimate` (the change in the
#'     indicator's mean per unit of the covariate, the same in every profile),
#'     `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`
#'     (Wald, from [parameter_inference()]). A fit without direct effects
#'     raises `latents_no_direct_effects`, and `what = "all"` leaves the table
#'     out.}
#'   \item{`"lmr"`}{The Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin (VLMR) and adjusted
#'     Lo-Mendell-Rubin (aLMR) tests of an enumeration grid (Vuong 1989; Lo,
#'     Mendell and Rubin 2001; Vermunt 2024), one row per pair of converged
#'     candidates that differ by one profile (`direction = "profiles"`) or one
#'     group class (`"group_classes"`) at the same structure: `direction`,
#'     `null_candidate`, `alternative_candidate`, `n_profiles`,
#'     `n_group_classes` and `model` of the alternative, `n_units` (the
#'     independent units scored: groups, or observations without groups),
#'     `parameters_added`, `lr` (twice the log-likelihood difference),
#'     `vlmr_p`, `adjusted_lr` (`lr / (1 + 1 / (parameters_added * log(n_units)))`),
#'     `almr_p`, `reference_mean` and `reference_sd` of the weighted
#'     chi-square reference distribution, whose weights are the eigenvalues of
#'     Vuong's matrix of the two models' scores and Hessians, and `note`. The
#'     p-values are computed by Imhof's method to about `1e-9`. A pair whose
#'     information matrix is singular, or whose candidate is on a boundary,
#'     keeps its row with `NA` statistics and the reason in `note`; warnings
#'     raised while scoring a candidate are recorded there too. Every
#'     candidate's information is computed, so the table is built only when
#'     asked for, and `what = "all"` leaves it out. A grid with no such pair
#'     raises `latents_no_lmr`.}
#'   \item{`"tree"`}{The flows of [plot_tree()], on every grid, taking its
#'     arguments `n_group_classes`, `n_profiles` (`n_classes` on a regression
#'     grid), `model`, `candidates`, `from`, `to` and `level`
#'     (default `"individuals"`). One row per pair of classes in consecutive
#'     rows of each tree: `tree` (the tree's name, as in the plot list),
#'     `level`, `from_candidate`, `from_class`, `from_share`, `to_candidate`,
#'     `to_class`, `to_share`, `mass` (the share of all units the two classes
#'     share, the sum over units of the product of their posterior
#'     probabilities, weighted by sampling weights at the individual level),
#'     `share_of_from` and `share_of_to` (`mass` as a part of each class).
#'     Every pair is listed, including those that share no mass. Units are
#'     the rows and groups the fit counts (see `drop_empty`), weighted by
#'     their sampling weights at both levels. A grid with no tree raises
#'     `latents_no_tree`, a fit with a noise component
#'     `latents_unsupported_noise`, and `what = "all"` leaves the table out.
#'     The summary of a grid carries the default table only, without these
#'     arguments.}
#'   \item{`"comparison"`, `"classification"`}{A [compare_models()] result.
#'     `"comparison"` is its table, one row per model. `"classification"`,
#'     offered when every model is a profile, class, membership-covariate or
#'     transition model, has one row per model, level and class: `model`, then
#'     the columns of a fit's `"classification"` table and that level's
#'     `relative_entropy`; single-class levels are left out. The models
#'     themselves are returned by [get_candidate()].}
#'   \item{`"test"`, `"replicates"`}{A bootstrap comparison. `"test"` is the
#'     one-row result; `"replicates"` has one row per simulated dataset.}
#'   \item{`"profiles"`, `"responses"`, `"profile_probabilities"`,
#'     `"covariances"`}{A starting-value set: its Gaussian means and
#'     variances, response probabilities, profile probabilities and, one row
#'     per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators, its covariances
#'     (`profile`, `indicator`, `indicator_2`, `covariance`).}
#'   \item{`"entropy"`, `"classification"`, `"average_posteriors"`,
#'     `"residuals"`}{A [diagnostics()] object: the tables of the same names
#'     described above.}
#' }
#'
#' @section Tables of the other model families:
#' Each family's first table is its default `what`; `"all"` returns a named
#' list of every table (without `"recovery"`, which needs `data` and `truth`).
#' Tables with intervals take `level`, and `vcov_type` (`"observed"`,
#' `"robust"` or `"opg"`; `NULL` reuses the type stored with a regression
#' fit). These objects also have `coef()`, `vcov(type = )`,
#' `confint(parm = , level = )`, `logLik()` and `nobs()` methods.
#' \describe{
#'   \item{Mixture regressions ([mixture_regression()])}{`"coefficients"`
#'     (one row per class and term, with Wald statistics, `p_adjusted` by
#'     Benjamini-Hochberg over non-intercepts and `exp_estimate` for the
#'     binomial, Poisson and ordinal families; ordinal thresholds lead each
#'     class as terms `"threshold:<lower>|<upper>"`), `"classes"`,
#'     `"membership"` (multinomial logits and odds ratios), `"group_classes"`
#'     (rows for two-level fits only), `"fit"` (`bic` penalised by the number
#'     of independent units, `bic_rows` by the number of rows, as flexmix
#'     reports it), `"assignments"`, `"groups"`, `"fitted"`, `"starts"`
#'     (`stage` `"screened"` or `"completed"`), `"classification"` and
#'     `"recovery"` (`by = "class"` or `"group_class"`).}
#'   \item{Growth mixtures (`mixture_regression(random = )`)}{The tables
#'     above plus `"random"` (random-effect variances, standard deviations
#'     and correlations, with intervals on the log and Fisher-z scales),
#'     `"random_effects"` (one row per person), `"trajectories"` (each class's
#'     mean trajectory with a band) and `"individual"` (each person's
#'     predicted curve); the last two take `time`. A multilevel growth mixture
#'     adds `"group_classes"` and `"clusters"`, and its `"fit"` uses the number
#'     of clusters in `bic` (persons in `bic_persons`).}
#'   \item{Additive fits (`multilpa(family = "additive")`)}{`"parameters"`
#'     (class means, between- and within-group variances and class weights;
#'     variance intervals on the log scale, weights on the logit scale;
#'     `adjust` sets the p-value adjustment, `"none"` by default),
#'     `"group_classes"`, `"groups"`, `"intercepts"` and
#'     `"conditional_intercepts"` (each group's posterior intercept, overall
#'     or given each class), `"assignments"`, `"classification"`, `"fit"`,
#'     `"recovery"` and `"starts"`. `effective_groups` in `"group_classes"` is
#'     `w^2 (1 - w) / Var(w)`, the number of perfectly classified groups that
#'     would estimate the class weight as precisely; below 50 the class's
#'     intervals carry a `latents_weak_class` warning.}
#'   \item{Cross-level fits (`multilpa(family = "full_cross_level")` or
#'     `"restricted_cross_level"`)}{`"profiles"` (individual profiles, then
#'     the group classes' means of group means), `"group_classes"`,
#'     `"composition"` (profile shares within each class: model-implied for
#'     the full family, a posterior-weighted description for the restricted
#'     one), `"groups"`, `"assignments"`, `"fit"` and `"starts"`. The
#'     likelihood is a working likelihood, comparable only between
#'     cross-level fits of the same data.}
#'   \item{General transition fits ([lta()] with `transitions = "occasion"`,
#'     transition or initial covariates, `measurement = "occasion"`,
#'     `order = 2`, `mover_stayer = TRUE`, `weights`, or `ordinal`/`count`
#'     indicators)}{
#'     `"transitions"` (model-implied, averaged over the observed groups, with
#'     their sampling weights in a weighted fit; `"initial"` and
#'     `"second_order_transitions"` likewise),
#'     `"transition_coefficients"` (log odds of each move against staying,
#'     with odds ratios), `"second_order_transitions"` and
#'     `"second_order_coefficients"` (`order = 2`), `"initial"` and
#'     `"initial_coefficients"`, `"profiles"`, `"responses"` (categorical
#'     indicators: `occasion`, `profile`, `indicator`, `category`,
#'     `probability`), `"ordinal"` and
#'     `"count_means"` (ordinal and count indicators), `"group_classes"`,
#'     `"assignments"`, `"fit"` and `"starts"`.}
#'   \item{Pooled imputations ([pool_imputations()])}{`"estimates"` (the
#'     pooled table), `"imputations"` (each imputation's aligned estimates)
#'     and `"fits"` (one row per imputation).}
#'   \item{Transition and group-class family grids
#'     (`enumerate_classes(time = )`, `enumerate_classes(family = )`)}{
#'     `"candidates"` (one row per candidate, its name first, with its
#'     likelihood, criteria, entropy and diagnostics) or `"best"`, the row
#'     with the lowest `criterion` (`"bic"` by groups, the default, `"aic"`
#'     or `"bic_individual"`). `"best"` reports the lowest value of a
#'     criterion; it does not select a model. With one group class every
#'     family is the same model, so those rows share a likelihood. Candidates
#'     are extracted by name with [get_candidate()]; transition grids can also
#'     be passed to [compare_models()].}
#' }
#' @section What `"all"` returns: A named list of every table the object
#'   offers, in catalogue order, each built with its default arguments;
#'   supplying any further argument raises `latents_bad_argument`. A table
#'   this object cannot produce (for example a sequence table for a fit made
#'   without `time`, or bivariate residuals for a family without discrete
#'   group classes) is omitted, so the names of the list show what was
#'   available. Only the conditions that mean the table does not exist for
#'   this object are skipped; any other error is raised.
#'
#' @section Arguments the tables take:
#'   These are passed through `...`; each table takes only those listed for it
#'   under *Tables*.
#' \describe{
#'   \item{`data`}{A data frame with one row per observation of the fit, in
#'   the order it was fitted in. `NULL` uses the columns the fit carries. The
#'   standard errors of `"profiles"` and `"responses"` come from
#'   [parameter_inference()] on these data. Without `data`, a fit that cannot
#'   supply them (bound-active, unconverged, singular information, a noise
#'   component) gives `NA` with a `latents_no_standard_errors` message; with
#'   `data`, the underlying condition is raised.
#'   }
#'   \item{`scale`}{For `"profiles"`: `"raw"` (default) reports estimates in
#'   input units; `"standardized"` divides each indicator's deviation from its
#'   grand mean by that indicator's observed standard deviation, as
#'   `plot(x, scale = "standardized")` draws. The standard errors are divided
#'   by the same constant.
#'   }
#'   \item{`format`}{For the posterior tables and `"sequences"`, `"long"`
#'   (default) gives one row per unit and class and `"wide"` one row per unit
#'   with one column per class. For `"information_criteria"`, `"wide"`
#'   (default) gives one row and `"long"` one row per criterion and
#'   sample-size convention.
#'   }
#'   \item{`level`}{The classification level to report: `"individuals"`,
#'   `"groups"` or `"both"`. `NULL` (default) gives `"both"` for a fit with
#'   discrete group classes and `"individuals"` otherwise, as in
#'   [diagnostics()].
#'   }
#'   \item{`truth`}{For `"assignments"`, one or more column names of `data`
#'   holding known labels to compare the assignments with. See *Recovery*.
#'   }
#'   \item{`by`}{For `"residuals"`, `"profile"` (default) assesses each
#'   profile separately and `"overall"` pools them.
#'   }
#'   \item{`adjust`}{For `"residuals"`, the multiplicity correction applied
#'   across the indicator pairs: `"none"` (default) or one of the
#'   [stats::p.adjust()] methods.
#'   }
#'   \item{`definitions`}{For `"information_criteria"` in long format, `TRUE`
#'   adds each criterion's formula and reference. Default `FALSE`.
#'   }
#'   \item{`estimated`, `stable`}{For `"transitions"`, `TRUE` or `FALSE`
#'   restricts the table to the rows estimated (or not) from observed
#'   occupancy, or to the diagonal (or off-diagonal) cells. `NULL` (default)
#'   keeps every row.
#'   }
#' }
#'
#' @section Recovery: `what = "assignments"` with `truth` returns a
#'   cross-tabulation of the model's labels against known ones instead of the
#'   per-observation table: one row per class and truth value, with columns
#'   `assignment` (the model label compared against), `class`, `truth` (the
#'   column name), `value`, `n` and `proportion` (the share of units with that
#'   truth value assigned to that class). Several truth columns are stacked.
#'
#'   A truth column that is constant within every group is compared against
#'   `group_class`; one that varies within any group is compared against
#'   `profile`. The `assignment` column records which comparison was made.
#'   Group-level recovery counts each group once. Unused factor levels are
#'   omitted. For a fit without discrete group classes every column is
#'   compared against `profile`.
#'
#'   The model's labels are arbitrary, so mass off the diagonal indicates
#'   relabelling, not failure.
#'
#' @section Information criteria: Let `q` be the number of free parameters,
#'   `n` the chosen sample size, and `EN` the classification entropy of the
#'   level matching that convention. The criteria are `deviance = -2L`,
#'   `aic = -2L + 2q`, `bic = -2L + q log(n)`,
#'   `sabic = -2L + q log((n + 2) / 24)`, `caic = -2L + q (log(n) + 1)`,
#'   `awe = -2(L - EN) + 2q (1.5 + log(n))`, `icl = -2L + q log(n) + 2 EN`,
#'   `kic = -2L + 3(q + 1)`, and `clc = -2L + 2 EN`. `clc`, like `icl` and
#'   `awe`, uses the entropy sum; `tidyLPA` reports a `CLC` based on relative
#'   entropy, and the two values are not comparable.
#'
#'   Every criterion that depends on a sample size is reported under both
#'   multilevel conventions, `"groups"` and `"individuals"`, using group-level
#'   posteriors under the first and individual-level posteriors under the
#'   second. Use one convention consistently across compared candidates.
#'   `deviance`, `aic` and `kic` carry `convention = NA_character_`. `clc`
#'   depends on no sample size, but its convention selects which level's
#'   classification entropy it penalises, so it is reported once per
#'   convention. Individual sample sizes exclude rows with no observed
#'   indicators, and group sample sizes exclude groups in which every row has
#'   none (`n_informative_groups`); the classification statistics of each
#'   level exclude the same rows and groups, as in Mplus. Where the group
#'   classification entropy is undefined, group-level `awe`, `icl` and `clc`
#'   are `NA`.
#'
#' @section Classification quality: The odds of correct classification for
#'   class `k` is `(p / (1 - p)) / (r / (1 - r))`, where `p` is the average
#'   posterior in the assigned class and `r` is the model-estimated class
#'   proportion. Values near one indicate classification no better than the
#'   class proportions alone; values of five or more are conventionally taken
#'   as adequate separation. It is `NA_real_` when `average_posterior` is
#'   missing or zero, or when `estimated_proportion` is zero or one. A perfect
#'   `average_posterior` of one gives `Inf` at an interior estimated proportion; a
#'   single-class solution always reports `NA_real_`. `average_posterior` is
#'   `NA_real_` for a class with no modal members. `n_modal` and
#'   `estimated_n` differ whenever entropy is below one.
#'
#'   `relative_entropy` is `1 - EN / (n log K)`, between zero and one, higher
#'   meaning sharper classification; `entropy_sum` is the raw `EN` used by the
#'   entropy-penalised criteria, lower meaning sharper. `relative_entropy` is
#'   `NA_real_` for a level with a single class.
#'
#'   A fit with individual profiles but no discrete group classes reports
#'   individuals only for `level = "both"` and raises
#'   `latents_no_group_classes` for `level = "groups"`.
#'
#' @section Bivariate residuals: `"residuals"` tests, pair by pair, the
#'   assumption that indicators are independent within a profile, weighting
#'   each observation by its posterior. `data` must be in the order the model
#'   was fitted in; the alignment is checked. A large residual indicates
#'   local dependence between two indicators, which otherwise tends to be
#'   absorbed by an extra profile. The p-values are approximate, and
#'   `p_adjusted` applies the correction named by `adjust` across the pairs.
#'   A fit with sampling weights uses them in the descriptive associations
#'   and `effective_n`; design-based inference is not implemented, so
#'   `statistic`, `df`, `p_value` and `p_adjusted` are `NA` for weighted fits.
#'
#' @references Schwarz, G. (1978). Estimating the dimension of a model.
#'   *Annals of Statistics*, 6, 461--464.
#'   Sclove, S. L. (1987). Application of model-selection criteria to some
#'   problems in multivariate analysis. *Psychometrika*, 52, 333--343.
#'   Bozdogan, H. (1987). Model selection and Akaike's information criterion.
#'   *Psychometrika*, 52, 345--370.
#'   Banfield, J. D., & Raftery, A. E. (1993). Model-based Gaussian and
#'   non-Gaussian clustering. *Biometrics*, 49, 803--821.
#'   Biernacki, C., & Govaert, G. (1997). Using the classification likelihood
#'   to choose the number of clusters. *Computing Science and Statistics*, 29,
#'   451--457.
#'   Cavanaugh, J. E. (1999). A large-sample model selection criterion based on
#'   Kullback's symmetric divergence. *Statistics and Probability Letters*, 42,
#'   333--343.
#'   Biernacki, C., Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (2000). Assessing a mixture model
#'   for clustering with the integrated completed likelihood. *IEEE
#'   Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence*, 22, 719--725.
#'   Bolck, A., Croon, M., & Hagenaars, J. (2004). Estimating latent structure
#'   models with categorical variables. *Political Analysis*, 12, 3--27.
#'   Nagin, D. S. (2005). *Group-Based Modeling of Development*. Harvard
#'   University Press.
#'   Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: two improved
#'   three-step approaches. *Political Analysis*, 18, 450--469.
#'   Satopaa, V., Albrecht, J., Irwin, D., & Raghavan, B. (2011). Finding a
#'   "kneedle" in a haystack: Detecting knee points in system behavior.
#'   *Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Distributed
#'   Computing Systems Workshops*, 166--171.
#' @return A base `data.frame` for a single `what`, whose columns are given
#'   under *Tables*, or a named list of such data frames for `what = "all"`.
#' @seealso [as.data.frame()], which returns the primary table alone,
#'   [summary()], which prints every table, and [diagnostics()] for the
#'   classification tables gathered with a condensed reading.
#' @examples
#' fit <- multilpa(
#'   course_engagement,
#'   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
#'   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
#'   seed = 1
#' )
#' get_results(fit)
#' get_results(fit, what = "profile_probabilities")
#' get_results(fit, what = "entropy")

old_inventory_record.name: get_results
old_inventory_record.documentation: Extract the result tables of a fitted model  Returns one tidy table of a fitted model or related object, named by `what`, as a base `data.frame`; `what = "all"` returns every table the object offers as a named list. The tables available depend on the class of the object and are listed under *Tables*.  Every object also has `print()`, which shows a compact overview, `summary()`, which collects its main tables (taking `level` and `vcov_type` where the model has standard errors), and `as.data.frame()`, which returns its primary table, the same as `get_results(x)`.  @param x A fitted model of this package, an enumeration grid, a model   comparison, a bootstrap comparison, a starting-value set, a   classification-diagnostics object, or the summary of any of them. @param what Name of the table to return, or `"all"` for every table the   object offers. `NULL` (default) returns the primary table: the   measurement model for a fit, the candidate grid for an enumeration, the   test row for a bootstrap comparison and the entropy table for a   diagnostics object. A name the object does not offer raises   `latents_bad_argument`, listing the names it does offer. @param ... Arguments for the requested table. Each table accepts only the   arguments listed for it under *Tables*; any other argument raises   `latents_bad_argument`.  @section Tables: Every fitted model offers these: \describe{   \item{`"profiles"`}{The Gaussian measurement model, one row per profile     and continuous indicator: `profile`, `indicator`, `mean`, `variance`,     `standard_deviation`, `mean_standard_error`, `variance_standard_error`.     Zero rows, with the same columns, when every indicator is categorical.     Takes `scale` and `data`.}   \item{`"responses"`}{The categorical measurement model, one row per     profile, categorical indicator and category: `profile`, `indicator`,     `category`, `probability`, `threshold`, `probability_standard_error`.     `threshold` is `qlogis(P(y <= category))` and is `NA_real_` for each     indicator's final category; a probability on its bound has an     `NA_real_` standard error. Zero rows, with the same columns, when no     indicator is categorical. Takes `data`.}   \item{`"covariances"`}{The within-profile residual covariance matrices,     one row per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators:     `profile`, `indicator`, `indicator_2`, `covariance`. Under the diagonal     parameterization the off-diagonal covariances are reported as exact     zeros.}   \item{`"ordinal"`, `"count_means"`}{Fits with ordinal or count     indicators only: the ordinal and count measurement models. Take     `data`.}   \item{`"counts"`}{Effective class sizes, one row per class at each level     of the fit: `level`, `class`, `effective_count` (the summed posteriors)     and `effective_proportion`. These differ from the modal counts in     `"classification"` whenever entropy is below one.}   \item{`"model"`}{One row describing the fit: its dimensions, likelihood,     parameter counts, `aic`, `bic_groups`, `bic_individual` and its     convergence and boundary diagnostics. The columns differ by family (a     covariate fit adds its predictor counts); `"information_criteria"` has     the same columns for every family.}   \item{`"posteriors"`}{One row per individual and profile: `row`, `group`,     `profile`, `posterior`, `modal`. Takes `format`.}   \item{`"assignments"`}{One row per observation: the columns the fit was     built from (or those of `data`), then `profile`, `group_class` where the     model has one, `uncertainty` (one minus the posterior of the assigned     profile) and one `posterior_profile_*` column per profile, plus     `posterior_noise` for a fit with a noise component (whose cases are     profile 0). Takes `data` and `truth`; with `truth` it returns a recovery     table instead (see *Recovery*).}   \item{`"classification"`}{Classification quality, one row per level and     class: `level`, `class`, `n_modal`, `proportion_modal`, `estimated_n`,     `estimated_proportion`, `average_posterior`,     `odds_correct_classification`. Takes `level`. Under sampling weights     `estimated_n` and `estimated_proportion` (and hence the odds of correct     classification) are weighted posterior totals; the modal and average     posterior columns describe the units supplied. The odds are `Inf` for a     class classified perfectly (average posterior one to within rounding)     and `NA` where they are undefined: a class with no modal members, or a     single class, whose proportion is one.}   \item{`"average_posteriors"`}{For the units modally assigned to each     class, their mean posterior for every class: `level`, `assigned_class`,     `class`, `n_assigned`, `average_posterior`. Rows sum to one within each     assigned class. This conditions on the assigned class, whereas     `"classification_errors"` conditions on the true class. Takes `level`.}   \item{`"classification_errors"`}{The probability that a unit in one true     class is assigned to another: `level`, `true_class`, `assigned_class`,     `probability`, summing to one within each `true_class`. Takes `level`.     On a membership-covariate fit this is a marginal summary over the fitted     units, not conditional on the covariates. A fit with a noise component     raises `latents_unsupported_noise`, as [three_step()] does, and `"all"`     and `summary()` omit the table.}   \item{`"bch_weights"`}{The BCH inverse-error weights, one row per unit and     class: `level`, `unit`, `assigned_class`, `class`, `weight`. Takes     `level`; a weighted regression should use one level, not `"both"`. On a     membership-covariate fit the weights invert the marginal error matrix     and are not a conditional three-step correction. Not available for a fit     with a noise component, as for `"classification_errors"`.}   \item{`"entropy"`}{One row per level: `level`, `n_classes`, `n_units`,     `entropy_sum`, `relative_entropy`.}   \item{`"residuals"`}{Bivariate residuals for every indicator pair, testing     within-profile independence: `profile`, `indicator_1`, `indicator_2`,     `kind`, `observed`, `expected`, `residual`, `effective_n`, `statistic`,     `df`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`. Takes `data`, `by` and `adjust`.}   \item{`"information_criteria"`}{Every information criterion the package     computes (see *Information criteria*). Takes `format` and     `definitions`.}   \item{`"sequences"`}{The assignments in occasion order, one row per     observation: `group`, `group_class`, `time`, `profile`. Takes `format`.     Raises `latents_no_time` for a fit made without `time`.}   \item{`"sequence_summary"`}{One row per group class: `group_class`,     `groups`, `observations`, `mean_length`, `median_length`, `shortest`,     `longest`, `complete`, `gaps`. Raises `latents_no_time` for a fit made     without `time`.}   \item{`"starts"`}{One row per EM start: `start`, `log_likelihood`,     `converged`, `iterations`, `error` and, where the family records it,     `boundary`. Under `search = "emEM"`, one row per start of the pool,     with its `kind`, its `stage` (`"final"` when run to convergence,     `"screened"` otherwise) and its `screened_log_likelihood`.}   \item{`"data"`}{The data the model was fitted to, one row per observation     in input order: the identifier (except for a single-level fit), the     occasion where there is one, the sampling weights of a weighted fit (as     rescaled for fitting) and the indicators under their original names.     Columns the model did not use, including membership covariates, are not     included; [three_step()] and [r3step()] therefore take `data`.} } Fits with discrete group classes also offer: \describe{   \item{`"group_posteriors"`}{One row per observed group and group class:     `group`, `group_size`, `log_likelihood`, `group_class`, `posterior`,     `modal`. Takes `format`.} } Tables specific to one family or object: \describe{   \item{`"gaussian_diagnostics"`}{Gaussian profile, membership-covariate,     transition and cross-level fits that record these diagnostics. One row     per Gaussian component and measurement context: `context`, `profile`,     `gaussian_mass`, `positive_rows`, `weight_effective_n`,     `min_variance_ratio`, `min_standardized_eigenvalue`, `boundary`.     `gaussian_mass` sums posterior times normalized sampling weight over     rows with at least one observed Gaussian indicator; `positive_rows`     counts rows with positive contributions. `weight_effective_n` is the     concentration measure `(sum(a)^2 / sum(a^2))` for those contributions,     not an identification guarantee; Gaussian mass is not this effective     sample size. `min_variance_ratio` is the smallest component variance     divided by its observed sampling-weighted marginal variance on the     fitted scale, including between-component variation.     `min_standardized_eigenvalue` is the smallest eigenvalue of the     component covariance after standardizing every indicator by its     observed sampling-weighted marginal standard deviation. Missing reference     variation gives `NA` ratios. `boundary` concerns the absolute variance     or eigenvalue floor. These descriptive measures use no automatic spike     cutoff and do not alter start selection.}   \item{`"profile_probabilities"`, `"stages"`}{A `multilpa` fit.     `"profile_probabilities"` has one row per group class and profile:     `group_class`, `profile`, `probability`, `group_class_probability`.     `"stages"` has one row per estimation stage: `stage`, `group_classes`,     `fixed`, `log_likelihood`, `parameters`, `parameters_with_measurement`,     `converged`. An ordinary fit has one `"joint"` row and a [fit_staged()]     result has two; `fixed` is `NA_character_` for a stage that estimated     every block.}   \item{`"coefficients"`}{A covariate fit. One row per estimated membership     coefficient: `level` (`"profile"` or `"group"`), `outcome`, `term`,     `parameter` (always `"logit"`), `estimate`. Standard errors are given by     [parameter_inference()].}   \item{`"transitions"`, `"initial"`, `"sequence_lengths"`}{A transition     fit. `"transitions"` has one row per group class and ordered pair of     profiles: `group_class`, `from`, `to`, `probability`, `expected_count`,     `stable`, `estimated`, `group_class_probability`; it takes `estimated`     and `stable`. `"initial"` has one row per group class and profile:     `group_class`, `profile`, `probability`, `prevalence`,     `group_class_probability`. `"sequence_lengths"` has one row per group:     `group`, `group_class`, `occasions`, `observations`, `complete`.}   \item{`"candidates"`, `"best"`, `"classification"`}{An enumeration     grid. `"candidates"` has one row per candidate model: its name     (`candidate`, first), its class counts, covariance `model`, log     likelihood, parameter count, every criterion under both sample-size     conventions, both entropies, the average posterior probability (AvePP)     summaries of each level (`avepp_min`, `avepp_max`, `avepp_mean`,     `avepp_below` and the same four prefixed `group_`) and the convergence,     boundary, replication, warning and error diagnostics, including     `min_standardized_eigenvalue` and `min_gaussian_mass` where Gaussian     diagnostics are available. These are descriptive summaries, without     an automatic cutoff or change to candidate selection. Failed candidates     are kept with `NA` estimates and their error text. It takes `cutoff`     (default `0.8`): `avepp_below` and `group_avepp_below` count the classes     whose AvePP is below it. A class with no modally assigned unit has no     AvePP; it is excluded from the minimum, maximum and mean and counted as     below the cutoff. A level with one class has `NA` summaries. `"best"`     has one row per information criterion and sample-size convention:     `criterion`, `convention`, `candidate` (the converged candidate with the     lowest value), `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`, `model` and `value`;     `what = "criteria"` is accepted as a deprecated name for it.     `"classification"` has one row per fitted candidate, level and class:     `candidate`, `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`, `model`, then the columns     of a fit's `"classification"` table and that level's     `relative_entropy`. Failed candidates and single-class levels     contribute no rows.}   \item{`"deltas"`, `"knees"`}{Model-selection evidence of an enumeration     grid, each taking `using` (default `"bic_groups"`). Neither selects a     model. `"deltas"` has one row per candidate: `candidate`, its class     counts and `model`, `criterion`, `value`, `delta_profile` (the decrease     in the criterion from the converged candidate with one profile fewer,     the same group classes and the same structure; positive means this     candidate is lower), `from_profile` naming that candidate, and     `delta_group_class` with `from_group_class` for one group class fewer.     `value` and both deltas are `NA` for a candidate that did not converge,     and a delta is `NA` when the smaller neighbour is missing or did not     converge. `"knees"` has one row per line of the grid: `direction`     (`"profiles"`, along the profiles at fixed group classes;     `"group_classes"`, along the group classes at fixed profiles;     `"parameters"`, every candidate by its number of parameters, one line     per structure), `line`, `criterion`, `from`, `to`, `n_points`,     `knee_candidate`, `distance`, `knee_without_largest` (the knee when the     last candidate of the line is left out), `stable` and `note`. The knee     is the candidate furthest below the straight line from the first to the     last candidate, measured perpendicular to it with both axes rescaled to     0-1. This is a simplified rule inspired by Kneedle (Satopaa et al.,     2011), without its smoothing or sensitivity thresholds, so a very small positive distance     can still name a knee. A line needs three candidates for a knee and four     for `knee_without_largest` and `stable`; otherwise they are `NA` and     `note` gives the reason.}   \item{`"local_dependence"`}{For a fit with `local_dependence`: `pair`,     `kind` (`"categorical"` or `"continuous"`), `profile`, `item_1`,     `category_1`, `item_2`, `category_2`, `probability`, `independent`,     `ratio`, `covariance` and `correlation`. A categorical pair has one row     per profile and combination of the two items' categories: the fitted     joint `probability`, the product of the two marginal probabilities     (`independent`, the joint probability under independence within the     profile) and their `ratio`; its covariance columns are `NA`. A     continuous pair has one row per profile, with the pair's `covariance`     and the `correlation` it implies; its category and probability     columns are `NA`. A fit without pairs raises     `latents_no_local_dependence`, and `what = "all"` leaves the table out.}   \item{`"direct_effects"`}{For a fit with `direct_effects`, one row per     effect: `indicator`, `covariate`, `estimate` (the change in the     indicator's mean per unit of the covariate, the same in every profile),     `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `conf_low` and `conf_high`     (Wald, from [parameter_inference()]). A fit without direct effects     raises `latents_no_direct_effects`, and `what = "all"` leaves the table     out.}   \item{`"lmr"`}{The Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin (VLMR) and adjusted     Lo-Mendell-Rubin (aLMR) tests of an enumeration grid (Vuong 1989; Lo,     Mendell and Rubin 2001; Vermunt 2024), one row per pair of converged     candidates that differ by one profile (`direction = "profiles"`) or one     group class (`"group_classes"`) at the same structure: `direction`,     `null_candidate`, `alternative_candidate`, `n_profiles`,     `n_group_classes` and `model` of the alternative, `n_units` (the     independent units scored: groups, or observations without groups),     `parameters_added`, `lr` (twice the log-likelihood difference),     `vlmr_p`, `adjusted_lr` (`lr / (1 + 1 / (parameters_added * log(n_units)))`),     `almr_p`, `reference_mean` and `reference_sd` of the weighted     chi-square reference distribution, whose weights are the eigenvalues of     Vuong's matrix of the two models' scores and Hessians, and `note`. The     p-values are computed by Imhof's method to about `1e-9`. A pair whose     information matrix is singular, or whose candidate is on a boundary,     keeps its row with `NA` statistics and the reason in `note`; warnings     raised while scoring a candidate are recorded there too. Every     candidate's information is computed, so the table is built only when     asked for, and `what = "all"` leaves it out. A grid with no such pair     raises `latents_no_lmr`.}   \item{`"tree"`}{The flows of [plot_tree()], on every grid, taking its     arguments `n_group_classes`, `n_profiles` (`n_classes` on a regression     grid), `model`, `candidates`, `from`, `to` and `level`     (default `"individuals"`). One row per pair of classes in consecutive     rows of each tree: `tree` (the tree's name, as in the plot list),     `level`, `from_candidate`, `from_class`, `from_share`, `to_candidate`,     `to_class`, `to_share`, `mass` (the share of all units the two classes     share, the sum over units of the product of their posterior     probabilities, weighted by sampling weights at the individual level),     `share_of_from` and `share_of_to` (`mass` as a part of each class).     Every pair is listed, including those that share no mass. Units are     the rows and groups the fit counts (see `drop_empty`), weighted by     their sampling weights at both levels. A grid with no tree raises     `latents_no_tree`, a fit with a noise component     `latents_unsupported_noise`, and `what = "all"` leaves the table out.     The summary of a grid carries the default table only, without these     arguments.}   \item{`"comparison"`, `"classification"`}{A [compare_models()] result.     `"comparison"` is its table, one row per model. `"classification"`,     offered when every model is a profile, class, membership-covariate or     transition model, has one row per model, level and class: `model`, then     the columns of a fit's `"classification"` table and that level's     `relative_entropy`; single-class levels are left out. The models     themselves are returned by [get_candidate()].}   \item{`"test"`, `"replicates"`}{A bootstrap comparison. `"test"` is the     one-row result; `"replicates"` has one row per simulated dataset.}   \item{`"profiles"`, `"responses"`, `"profile_probabilities"`,     `"covariances"`}{A starting-value set: its Gaussian means and     variances, response probabilities, profile probabilities and, one row     per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators, its covariances     (`profile`, `indicator`, `indicator_2`, `covariance`).}   \item{`"entropy"`, `"classification"`, `"average_posteriors"`,     `"residuals"`}{A [diagnostics()] object: the tables of the same names     described above.} }  @section Tables of the other model families: Each family's first table is its default `what`; `"all"` returns a named list of every table (without `"recovery"`, which needs `data` and `truth`). Tables with intervals take `level`, and `vcov_type` (`"observed"`, `"robust"` or `"opg"`; `NULL` reuses the type stored with a regression fit). These objects also have `coef()`, `vcov(type = )`, `confint(parm = , level = )`, `logLik()` and `nobs()` methods. \describe{   \item{Mixture regressions ([mixture_regression()])}{`"coefficients"`     (one row per class and term, with Wald statistics, `p_adjusted` by     Benjamini-Hochberg over non-intercepts and `exp_estimate` for the     binomial, Poisson and ordinal families; ordinal thresholds lead each     class as terms `"threshold:<lower>|<upper>"`), `"classes"`,     `"membership"` (multinomial logits and odds ratios), `"group_classes"`     (rows for two-level fits only), `"fit"` (`bic` penalised by the number     of independent units, `bic_rows` by the number of rows, as flexmix     reports it), `"assignments"`, `"groups"`, `"fitted"`, `"starts"`     (`stage` `"screened"` or `"completed"`), `"classification"` and     `"recovery"` (`by = "class"` or `"group_class"`).}   \item{Growth mixtures (`mixture_regression(random = )`)}{The tables     above plus `"random"` (random-effect variances, standard deviations     and correlations, with intervals on the log and Fisher-z scales),     `"random_effects"` (one row per person), `"trajectories"` (each class's     mean trajectory with a band) and `"individual"` (each person's     predicted curve); the last two take `time`. A multilevel growth mixture     adds `"group_classes"` and `"clusters"`, and its `"fit"` uses the number     of clusters in `bic` (persons in `bic_persons`).}   \item{Additive fits (`multilpa(family = "additive")`)}{`"parameters"`     (class means, between- and within-group variances and class weights;     variance intervals on the log scale, weights on the logit scale;     `adjust` sets the p-value adjustment, `"none"` by default),     `"group_classes"`, `"groups"`, `"intercepts"` and     `"conditional_intercepts"` (each group's posterior intercept, overall     or given each class), `"assignments"`, `"classification"`, `"fit"`,     `"recovery"` and `"starts"`. `effective_groups` in `"group_classes"` is     `w^2 (1 - w) / Var(w)`, the number of perfectly classified groups that     would estimate the class weight as precisely; below 50 the class's     intervals carry a `latents_weak_class` warning.}   \item{Cross-level fits (`multilpa(family = "full_cross_level")` or     `"restricted_cross_level"`)}{`"profiles"` (individual profiles, then     the group classes' means of group means), `"group_classes"`,     `"composition"` (profile shares within each class: model-implied for     the full family, a posterior-weighted description for the restricted     one), `"groups"`, `"assignments"`, `"fit"` and `"starts"`. The     likelihood is a working likelihood, comparable only between     cross-level fits of the same data.}   \item{General transition fits ([lta()] with `transitions = "occasion"`,     transition or initial covariates, `measurement = "occasion"`,     `order = 2`, `mover_stayer = TRUE`, `weights`, or `ordinal`/`count`     indicators)}{     `"transitions"` (model-implied, averaged over the observed groups, with     their sampling weights in a weighted fit; `"initial"` and     `"second_order_transitions"` likewise),     `"transition_coefficients"` (log odds of each move against staying,     with odds ratios), `"second_order_transitions"` and     `"second_order_coefficients"` (`order = 2`), `"initial"` and     `"initial_coefficients"`, `"profiles"`, `"responses"` (categorical     indicators: `occasion`, `profile`, `indicator`, `category`,     `probability`), `"ordinal"` and     `"count_means"` (ordinal and count indicators), `"group_classes"`,     `"assignments"`, `"fit"` and `"starts"`.}   \item{Pooled imputations ([pool_imputations()])}{`"estimates"` (the     pooled table), `"imputations"` (each imputation's aligned estimates)     and `"fits"` (one row per imputation).}   \item{Transition and group-class family grids     (`enumerate_classes(time = )`, `enumerate_classes(family = )`)}{     `"candidates"` (one row per candidate, its name first, with its     likelihood, criteria, entropy and diagnostics) or `"best"`, the row     with the lowest `criterion` (`"bic"` by groups, the default, `"aic"`     or `"bic_individual"`). `"best"` reports the lowest value of a     criterion; it does not select a model. With one group class every     family is the same model, so those rows share a likelihood. Candidates     are extracted by name with [get_candidate()]; transition grids can also     be passed to [compare_models()].} } @section What `"all"` returns: A named list of every table the object   offers, in catalogue order, each built with its default arguments;   supplying any further argument raises `latents_bad_argument`. A table   this object cannot produce (for example a sequence table for a fit made   without `time`, or bivariate residuals for a family without discrete   group classes) is omitted, so the names of the list show what was   available. Only the conditions that mean the table does not exist for   this object are skipped; any other error is raised.  @section Arguments the tables take:   These are passed through `...`; each table takes only those listed for it   under *Tables*. \describe{   \item{`data`}{A data frame with one row per observation of the fit, in   the order it was fitted in. `NULL` uses the columns the fit carries. The   standard errors of `"profiles"` and `"responses"` come from   [parameter_inference()] on these data. Without `data`, a fit that cannot   supply them (bound-active, unconverged, singular information, a noise   component) gives `NA` with a `latents_no_standard_errors` message; with   `data`, the underlying condition is raised.   }   \item{`scale`}{For `"profiles"`: `"raw"` (default) reports estimates in   input units; `"standardized"` divides each indicator's deviation from its   grand mean by that indicator's observed standard deviation, as   `plot(x, scale = "standardized")` draws. The standard errors are divided   by the same constant.   }   \item{`format`}{For the posterior tables and `"sequences"`, `"long"`   (default) gives one row per unit and class and `"wide"` one row per unit   with one column per class. For `"information_criteria"`, `"wide"`   (default) gives one row and `"long"` one row per criterion and   sample-size convention.   }   \item{`level`}{The classification level to report: `"individuals"`,   `"groups"` or `"both"`. `NULL` (default) gives `"both"` for a fit with   discrete group classes and `"individuals"` otherwise, as in   [diagnostics()].   }   \item{`truth`}{For `"assignments"`, one or more column names of `data`   holding known labels to compare the assignments with. See *Recovery*.   }   \item{`by`}{For `"residuals"`, `"profile"` (default) assesses each   profile separately and `"overall"` pools them.   }   \item{`adjust`}{For `"residuals"`, the multiplicity correction applied   across the indicator pairs: `"none"` (default) or one of the   [stats::p.adjust()] methods.   }   \item{`definitions`}{For `"information_criteria"` in long format, `TRUE`   adds each criterion's formula and reference. Default `FALSE`.   }   \item{`estimated`, `stable`}{For `"transitions"`, `TRUE` or `FALSE`   restricts the table to the rows estimated (or not) from observed   occupancy, or to the diagonal (or off-diagonal) cells. `NULL` (default)   keeps every row.   } }  @section Recovery: `what = "assignments"` with `truth` returns a   cross-tabulation of the model's labels against known ones instead of the   per-observation table: one row per class and truth value, with columns   `assignment` (the model label compared against), `class`, `truth` (the   column name), `value`, `n` and `proportion` (the share of units with that   truth value assigned to that class). Several truth columns are stacked.    A truth column that is constant within every group is compared against   `group_class`; one that varies within any group is compared against   `profile`. The `assignment` column records which comparison was made.   Group-level recovery counts each group once. Unused factor levels are   omitted. For a fit without discrete group classes every column is   compared against `profile`.    The model's labels are arbitrary, so mass off the diagonal indicates   relabelling, not failure.  @section Information criteria: Let `q` be the number of free parameters,   `n` the chosen sample size, and `EN` the classification entropy of the   level matching that convention. The criteria are `deviance = -2L`,   `aic = -2L + 2q`, `bic = -2L + q log(n)`,   `sabic = -2L + q log((n + 2) / 24)`, `caic = -2L + q (log(n) + 1)`,   `awe = -2(L - EN) + 2q (1.5 + log(n))`, `icl = -2L + q log(n) + 2 EN`,   `kic = -2L + 3(q + 1)`, and `clc = -2L + 2 EN`. `clc`, like `icl` and   `awe`, uses the entropy sum; `tidyLPA` reports a `CLC` based on relative   entropy, and the two values are not comparable.    Every criterion that depends on a sample size is reported under both   multilevel conventions, `"groups"` and `"individuals"`, using group-level   posteriors under the first and individual-level posteriors under the   second. Use one convention consistently across compared candidates.   `deviance`, `aic` and `kic` carry `convention = NA_character_`. `clc`   depends on no sample size, but its convention selects which level's   classification entropy it penalises, so it is reported once per   convention. Individual sample sizes exclude rows with no observed   indicators, and group sample sizes exclude groups in which every row has   none (`n_informative_groups`); the classification statistics of each   level exclude the same rows and groups, as in Mplus. Where the group   classification entropy is undefined, group-level `awe`, `icl` and `clc`   are `NA`.  @section Classification quality: The odds of correct classification for   class `k` is `(p / (1 - p)) / (r / (1 - r))`, where `p` is the average   posterior in the assigned class and `r` is the model-estimated class   proportion. Values near one indicate classification no better than the   class proportions alone; values of five or more are conventionally taken   as adequate separation. It is `NA_real_` when `average_posterior` is   missing, or when it or `estimated_proportion` is zero or one, so a   single-class solution always reports `NA_real_`. `average_posterior` is   `NA_real_` for a class with no modal members. `n_modal` and   `estimated_n` differ whenever entropy is below one.    `relative_entropy` is `1 - EN / (n log K)`, between zero and one, higher   meaning sharper classification; `entropy_sum` is the raw `EN` used by the   entropy-penalised criteria, lower meaning sharper. `relative_entropy` is   `NA_real_` for a level with a single class.    A fit with individual profiles but no discrete group classes reports   individuals only for `level = "both"` and raises   `latents_no_group_classes` for `level = "groups"`.  @section Bivariate residuals: `"residuals"` tests, pair by pair, the   assumption that indicators are independent within a profile, weighting   each observation by its posterior. `data` must be in the order the model   was fitted in; the alignment is checked. A large residual indicates   local dependence between two indicators, which otherwise tends to be   absorbed by an extra profile. The p-values are approximate, and   `p_adjusted` applies the correction named by `adjust` across the pairs.   A fit with sampling weights uses them in the descriptive associations   and `effective_n`; design-based inference is not implemented, so   `statistic`, `df`, `p_value` and `p_adjusted` are `NA` for weighted fits.  @references Schwarz, G. (1978). Estimating the dimension of a model.   *Annals of Statistics*, 6, 461--464.   Sclove, S. L. (1987). Application of model-selection criteria to some   problems in multivariate analysis. *Psychometrika*, 52, 333--343.   Bozdogan, H. (1987). Model selection and Akaike's information criterion.   *Psychometrika*, 52, 345--370.   Banfield, J. D., & Raftery, A. E. (1993). Model-based Gaussian and   non-Gaussian clustering. *Biometrics*, 49, 803--821.   Biernacki, C., & Govaert, G. (1997). Using the classification likelihood   to choose the number of clusters. *Computing Science and Statistics*, 29,   451--457.   Cavanaugh, J. E. (1999). A large-sample model selection criterion based on   Kullback's symmetric divergence. *Statistics and Probability Letters*, 42,   333--343.   Biernacki, C., Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (2000). Assessing a mixture model   for clustering with the integrated completed likelihood. *IEEE   Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence*, 22, 719--725.   Bolck, A., Croon, M., & Hagenaars, J. (2004). Estimating latent structure   models with categorical variables. *Political Analysis*, 12, 3--27.   Nagin, D. S. (2005). *Group-Based Modeling of Development*. Harvard   University Press.   Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: two improved   three-step approaches. *Political Analysis*, 18, 450--469.   Satopaa, V., Albrecht, J., Irwin, D., & Raghavan, B. (2011). Finding a   "kneedle" in a haystack: Detecting knee points in system behavior.   *Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Distributed   Computing Systems Workshops*, 166--171. @return A base `data.frame` for a single `what`, whose columns are given   under *Tables*, or a named list of such data frames for `what = "all"`. @seealso [as.data.frame()], which returns the primary table alone,   [summary()], which prints every table, and [diagnostics()] for the   classification tables gathered with a condensed reading. @examples fit <- multilpa(   course_engagement,   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,   seed = 1 ) get_results(fit) get_results(fit, what = "profile_probabilities") get_results(fit, what = "entropy") names(get_results(fit, what = "all"))  # `engagement` and `student_type` are the kinds each row was simulated from, # which the model never saw. before.name: .multilpa_coerce
before.documentation:
#' Coerce an object of this package to its primary table
#'
#' The one body behind every `as.data.frame()` method here, so no class can
#' coerce to something other than the first entry of its own catalogue.
#'
#' @param x The object.
#' @param row.names The caller's `row.names`.
#' @param extra `list(...)` as the method received it, which must be empty.
#' @return A base `data.frame`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_coerce <- function(x, row.names, extra) {
  .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
    extra, "as.data.frame()",
    "It coerces to the primary table; get_results(x, what = ) has the others.")
  result <- get_results(x)
  row.names(result) <- row.names
  result
}

.multilpa_absent_table_conditions.name: .multilpa_absent_table_conditions

before.name: .multilpa_absent_table_conditions
before.documentation:
#' Classed refusals that mean "this object has no such table"
#'
#' `what = "all"` walks the whole catalogue, and some of its entries cannot be
#' built for every object: a fit made without `time` has no sequences, a fit
#' without discrete group classes has no bivariate residuals. Those are refusals about
#' the object, not failures, and `"all"` leaves the table out. Every other
#' condition propagates, so a genuine defect is never swallowed.
#'
#' @return A character vector of condition classes.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_absent_table_conditions <- function() {
  c("latents_no_time", "latents_no_group_classes",
    "latents_no_indicator_data", "latents_incomplete_fit",
    "latents_no_continuous", "latents_no_categorical",
    # A fit whose classes cannot be separated has no three-step correction to
    # report, which is a fact about the fit and not a reason for `summary()`
    # to fail.
    "latents_inseparable_classes",
    # A noise component has no classification-error correction yet.
    "latents_unsupported_noise",
    # A grid with one solution per model has no tree.
    "latents_no_tree",
    # A fit without locally dependent pairs has no table of them.
    "latents_no_local_dependence",
    # Nor does a fit without direct effects.
    "latents_no_direct_effects")
}

}

before.documentation:
#' What a grid can draw
#'
#' The registry every grid verb consults. A view is offered when the grid's
#' table or fits carry what it draws: the criterion columns of the table; the
#' classification-quality views from the fits' posteriors (or the table's
#' entropy); the model-selection views, which lay the candidates out by number
#' of classes and number of group classes; and the tree, which divides each
#' named candidate's units by their posteriors. A view that is not offered has
#' a reason, which the refusal gives.
#'
#' @param x An enumeration grid.
#' @param verb The calling function's name, for the refusal of a non-grid.
#' @return A list: `kind`; `criteria`, the criterion columns, named by their
#'   display titles; `default`, the criteria drawn when `what` is not given;
#'   `using`, the criterion the selection views read by default; `axis`, the

before.source:
.latents_grid_view_table <- function(x) {
  views <- .latents_grid_views(x, "plot_views")
  criteria <- unname(views$criteria)
  titles <- names(views$criteria) %||% toupper(criteria)
  if (identical(views$kind, "profiles")) {
    titles <- names(.multilpa_distinct_criteria(data.frame(), criteria))
  }
  named <- .latents_grid_view_names()
  described <- c(
    entropy = "Relative entropy of every candidate, at each level with two or more classes",
    avepp = "The lowest average posterior probability of every candidate, with the cutoff dashed",
    diagnostics = "Entropy and lowest AvePP together",
    deltas = "The decrease in the criterion in `using` with each added class and each added group class",
    heatmap = "The criterion in `using` over classes and group classes, relative to the lowest",
    smallest = "The share of the smallest class of every candidate, with 5% dashed",
    trust = "Convergence, boundary and replication of every candidate",
    selection = "Every selection view the grid offers, and diagnostics, as a list",
    tree = "How classes split as more are added, one plot per tree (see plot_tree())")
  data.frame(
    type = c(criteria, "all", named),
    group = c(rep("criteria", length(criteria) + 1L),
              ifelse(named %in% c("entropy", "avepp", "diagnostics"), "quality",
                     ifelse(named == "tree", "tree", "selection"))),
    supported = c(rep(TRUE, length(criteria) + 1L), named %in% views$views),
    description = c(sprintf("%s across the candidates; lower is preferred", titles),
                    "Every criterion of the grid, as panels of one plot",
                    unname(described[named])),
    reason = c(rep(NA_character_, length(criteria) + 1L),
               unname(views$refused[named])),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

#' Draw a transition, family or regression grid through the shared views
#'
#' The `plot()` methods of these grids keep their 0.9.21 call: `what` (or its
#' former name `criterion`) names a criterion, matched as `match.arg()`
#' matched `"bic"`, `"aic"` and `"bic_individual"`, so a unique abbreviation
#' such as `"bic_i"` still works. Without either, the grid's summary of its
#' default criteria is drawn, as [plot_enumeration()] draws it. Any other value is
#' passed to [plot_enumeration()], which draws every view the grid offers.
#' Arguments of [plot_enumeration()] and, for the tree, of [plot_tree()] given
#' through `...` are passed on; any other is ignored with a
#' `latents_unused_argument` warning, as 0.9.21 ignored it.
#'
#' @param x A transition or group-class family grid.
#' @param what The caller's `what`.
#' @param what_given Whether the caller supplied `what`.
#' @param criterion The caller's `criterion`, `NULL` when not given.
#' @param main,subtitle Titles.
#' @param extra `list(...)` as the method received it.
#' @return A ggplot object, or a `latents_plots` list.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(x, what, what_given, criterion, main, subtitle, extra) {
    views <- .latents_grid_views(x, "plot")
    what <- if (!what_given && is.null(criterion)) 
        views$default
    else .latents_grid_criterion(.latents_former_argument(what, what_given, criterion, c("what", "criterion")), views)
    supplied <- names(extra) %||% rep("", length(extra))
    passed <- c("combine", "labels", "mark_minimum", "cutoff", "using", if (identical(what, "tree")) .latents_tree_arguments())
    forwarded <- nzchar(supplied) & supplied %in% passed
    .latents_warn_unused_arguments(extra[!forwarded], "plot()", .latents_grid_plot_advice())
    do.call(plot_enumeration, c(list(x, what = what, main = main, subtitle = subtitle), extra[forwarded]))
}

.growth_dense_terms.name: .growth_dense_terms

before.name: .growth_dense_terms
before.documentation:
#' Class log densities and random-effect posteriors with correlated residuals
#'
#' @return A list over classes with `log_density` (per person), `mean`
#'   (persons by random effects: posterior means of b), `u` (each row's
#'   V^-1 r, laid out by row), `inverse` (per pattern) and `covariance`
#'   (random by random by patterns: posterior covariances).
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(spec, stats, params, marginal = NULL) {
    marginal <- marginal %||% .growth_dense_covariances(spec, stats, params)
    covariances <- .growth_covariances(spec, params)
    design <- stats$raw$design
    y <- stats$raw$y
    rows <- stats$raw$rows
    n_persons <- length(rows)
    n_random <- ncol(spec$random_design)
    lapply(seq_len(spec$n_classes), function(k) {
        residual <- y - as.vector(design %*% .growth_coefficients(params, k))
        log_density <- numeric(n_persons)
        means <- matrix(0, n_persons, n_random)
        u <- numeric(length(y))
        inverses <- vector("list", length(stats$dense))
        posterior_covariance <- array(0, c(n_random, n_random, length(stats$dense)))
        invisible(lapply(seq_along(stats$dense), function(g) {
            pattern <- stats$dense[[g]]
            factor <- tryCatch(chol(marginal[[k]][[g]]), error = function(condition) {
                stop(errorCondition(paste("A marginal covariance is numerically singular (a process variance", "far beyond the residual variance):", conditionMessage(condition)), class = "latents_singular_covariance", call = NULL))
            })
            inverse <- chol2inv(factor)
            members <- pattern$members
            at <- do.call(rbind, rows[members])
            r <- matrix(residual[at], length(members))
            solved <- r %*% inverse
            log_density[members] <<- -0.5 * (ncol(r) * log(2 * pi) + 2 * sum(log(diag(factor))) + rowSums(r * solved))
            u[at] <<- solved
            gz <- covariances[[k]] %*% t(pattern$random)
            means[members, ] <<- solved %*% t(gz)
            inverses[[g]] <<- inverse
            posterior_covariance[, , g] <<- covariances[[k]] - gz %*% inverse %*% t(gz)
        }))
        list(log_density = log_density, mean = means, u = u, inverse = inverses, covariance = posterior_covariance)
    })
}

before.name: .growth_correlated_bounds
before.documentation:
#' Bounds of the correlated growth coordinates
#'
#' Variances are floored as in the uncorrelated engine: the residual
#' variance, the process variance and each random-effect variance (through
#' its log-Cholesky diagonal) at `min_variance`. The process rate is kept
#' within a factor of 10^4 of the reciprocal median time gap, beyond which an
#' autoregressive process cannot be told from white noise (fast) or from a
#' random intercept (slow).
#'
#' @return A list with `lower` and `upper`, named like the coordinates.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(spec, theta, gap) {
    names_theta <- names(theta)
    floor <- 0.5 * log(spec$min_variance)
    lower <- stats::setNames(rep(-Inf, length(theta)), names_theta)
    upper <- stats::setNames(rep(Inf, length(theta)), names_theta)
    variance_like <- startsWith(names_theta, "log_sigma.") | startsWith(names_theta, "random.log_cholesky.") | names_theta == "residual_correlation.log_sd"
    lower[variance_like] <- floor
    rate <- names_theta == "residual_correlation.log_rate"
    lower[rate] <- log(1e-04/gap)
    upper[rate] <- log(10000/gap)
    list(lower = lower, upper = upper)
}
