.latents_vuong_weights.name: .latents_vuong_weights

before.name: .latents_vuong_weights
before.documentation:
#' The weights of the reference distribution of Vuong's statistic
#'
#' With `A = -information`, `-B A^-1 = B information^-1`, so in terms of the
#' information matrices
#' `W = [ B1 I1^-1, B10 I0^-1 ; -B10' I1^-1, -B0 I0^-1 ]`.
#' For two regular nested models whose information equals the variance of
#' the score, the nonzero eigenvalues are `p1 - p0` ones, and the reference
#' distribution is the familiar chi-square on `p1 - p0` degrees of freedom.
#' @param alternative,null From `.latents_vuong_parts()`, on the same units.
#' @return The eigenvalues of `W`, computed from an equivalent symmetric matrix.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_vuong_weights <- function(alternative, null) {
  stopifnot("the two models must be scored on the same units" =
              nrow(alternative$scores) == nrow(null$scores))
  # Congruent scaling of information and score columns changes only the
  # chart, so Vuong's eigenvalues are unchanged. Raw inverses can otherwise
  # reject a regular model merely because an indicator's units changed.
  condition <- function(parts) {
    diagonal <- diag(parts$information)
    if (any(!is.finite(diagonal) | diagonal <= 0)) {
      stop(errorCondition("The Vuong comparison information is not positive definite.",
                          class = "latents_singular_information", call = NULL))
    }
    scale <- 1 / sqrt(diagonal)
    parts$scores <- sweep(parts$scores, 2L, scale, "*")
    parts$information <- parts$information * tcrossprod(scale)
    parts
  }
  # Preserve the exact empirical-Gram identity before rounding the chart.
  # When supplied information is the computed S'S, an orthogonal score
  # basis realizes its whitening without ill-conditioned normal equations.
  alternative$score_gram <- identical(unname(alternative$information),
                                       unname(crossprod(alternative$scores)))
  null$score_gram <- identical(unname(null$information), unname(crossprod(null$scores)))
  alternative <- condition(alternative)
  null <- condition(null)
  unresolved <- function() {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "The Vuong reference weights cannot be resolved reliably in these coordinates;",
      "the comparison probability cannot be reported."),
      class = "latents_inaccurate_probability", call = NULL))
  }
  whiten <- function(parts) {
    tryCatch({
      if (isTRUE(parts$score_gram)) {
        decomposition <- svd(parts$scores, nv = 0L)
        epsilon <- .Machine$double.eps
        rank_error <- max(dim(parts$scores)) * epsilon * max(decomposition$d)
        if (length(decomposition$d) < ncol(parts$scores) ||
            min(decomposition$d) <= rank_error) unresolved()
        span_error <- rank_error / min(decomposition$d)
        return(list(scores = decomposition$u,
                    weight_error = 2 * span_error / (1 - span_error)))
      }
      root <- chol(parts$information)
      inverse <- backsolve(root, diag(ncol(root)))
      scores <- t(backsolve(root, t(parts$scores), transpose = TRUE))
      columns <- ncol(root)
      epsilon <- .Machine$double.eps
      gamma <- columns * epsilon / (1 - columns * epsilon)
      chol_gamma <- (columns + 1) * epsilon / (1 - (columns + 1) * epsilon)
      # Cholesky has componentwise backward error gamma[p+1] |R'| |R|.
      # Include the preceding diagonal congruence's two rounded products,
      # then propagate that information error through R^-1. Near-collinear
      # charts amplify it even though the final score matrix has unit scale.
      information_error <- chol_gamma * crossprod(abs(root)) +
        (2 * epsilon / (1 - 2 * epsilon)) * abs(parts$information)
      relative_error <- norm(crossprod(abs(inverse),
        information_error %*% abs(inverse)), "2")
      if (!is.finite(relative_error) || relative_error >= 1) {
        stop("Information whitening cannot resolve the fitted coordinates.")
      }
      score_norm <- norm(scores, "2")
      # Triangular solves and the initial score scaling have componentwise
      # error bounds too. Bound the resulting perturbation of S S' by
      # 2 ||S|| ||dS|| + ||dS||^2; Weyl then bounds every reference weight.
      score_error <- gamma * norm(abs(scores) %*% abs(root) %*% abs(inverse), "2") +
        epsilon * norm(abs(parts$scores) %*% abs(inverse), "2")
      weight_error <- score_norm^2 * relative_error / (1 - relative_error) +
        2 * score_norm * score_error + score_error^2
      if (!is.finite(weight_error)) unresolved()
      list(scores = scores, weight_error = weight_error)
    }, error = function(condition) {
      if (inherits(condition, "latents_inaccurate_probability")) stop(condition)
      stop(errorCondition("The Vuong comparison information is singular or nonpositive.",
                          class = "latents_singular_information", call = NULL))
    })
  }
  alternative_whitened <- whiten(alternative)
  null_whitened <- whiten(null)
  combined <- cbind(alternative_whitened$scores, null_whitened$scores)
  signs <- c(rep(1, ncol(alternative$scores)), rep(-1, ncol(null$scores)))
  # W is similar to J S'S for the information-whitened combined scores S.
  # Its nonzero eigenvalues equal those of S J S'. With S = U D V', use
  # the smaller symmetric D V' J V D: the unsymmetric W has defective zero
  # eigenvalues in regular nested models, and a generic eigen() can turn
  # their rounding error into spurious positive/negative weights of 1e-7.
  decomposition <- svd(combined, nu = 0L)
  signed <- crossprod(decomposition$v, signs * decomposition$v) *
    tcrossprod(decomposition$d)
  if (any(!is.finite(signed))) unresolved()
  weights <- eigen(signed, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  # Only matrix-construction roundoff identifies numerical zeros. A larger
  # whitening uncertainty does not establish zero: genuine small signed
  # weights can change probabilities materially near a zero statistic.
  rounding <- 64 * .Machine$double.eps * ncol(combined) * max(decomposition$d)^2
  uncertainty <- rounding + alternative_whitened$weight_error +
    null_whitened$weight_error
  if (!is.finite(uncertainty) || uncertainty >= max(abs(weights)) ||
      any(abs(weights) > rounding & abs(weights) <= uncertainty)) unresolved()
  weights[abs(weights) <= rounding] <- 0
  c(weights, rep(0, ncol(combined) - length(weights)))
}

.latents_imhof_upper.name: .latents_imhof_upper

before.name: .latents_imhof_upper
before.documentation:
#' Upper tail of a weighted sum of chi-square(1) variables (Imhof 1961)
#'
#' `P(sum_j lambda_j X_j > q)` for independent `X_j ~ chi-square(1)`:
#' `1/2 + (1/pi) int_0^Inf sin(theta(u)) / (u rho(u)) du`, with
#' `theta(u) = sum_j atan(lambda_j u) / 2 - q u / 2` and
#' `rho(u) = prod_j (1 + lambda_j^2 u^2)^(1/4)`. Weights that are
#' exactly zero contribute nothing and are dropped. Small nonzero weights
#' are retained: their relative size does not bound the probability error
#' near a statistic of zero. Negative statistics are handled by the symmetry
#' `P(Q > q) = 1 - P(-Q > -q)` for the continuous nonzero-weight distribution.
#'
#' The integral has two regimes, and each is integrated where it is smooth.
#' Up to `u = 2 pi / q` the phase is dominated by the arctangents, which bend
#' at `u = 1 / |lambda_j|`; that lead is integrated by adaptive quadrature
#' between breakpoints at those scales and at every decade, so no segment
#' spans more than an order of magnitude. When `q = 0` there is no
#' oscillation at all and the lead is the whole integral, ended where
#' Imhof's truncation bound falls below `1e-12`: with weights of both
#' signs the integrand then decays monotonically, and extrapolating its
#' partial sums (the method this replaces) settled on wrong limits, 32% off
#' for weights `(1, -1e4, -1e4, -1e4)`. Beyond the lead, `sin(q u / 2)`
#' dominates, so the tail is integrated in half-periods aligned to it, whose
#' partial sums alternate, and accelerated by Wynn's epsilon algorithm, as
#' QUADPACK's QAWF does for Fourier integrals. The value is accepted when two
#' successive estimates agree to `1e-10`; otherwise, or when a segment cannot
#' be integrated, `latents_inaccurate_probability` is raised. The integral
#' is taken on weights normalised to unit size, which leaves the probability
#' unchanged. Against 312 exact F and chi-square probabilities and two-weight
#' convolutions, with weights from 1e-6 to 1e6, the absolute error is at most
#' 3.2e-13 when `q = 0` and 1e-15 otherwise.
#' @param q The statistic.
#' @param lambda The weights.
#' @return A probability.
#' @noRd

.latents_wynn.name: .latents_wynn

before.name: .latents_wynn
before.documentation:
#' The limit of a sequence by Wynn's epsilon algorithm
#'
#' Builds the epsilon table column by column from the partial sums `s`
#' (`e[-1] = 0`, `e[0] = s`, `e[j + 1][k] = e[j - 1][k + 1] + 1 /
#' (e[j][k + 1] - e[j][k])`) and returns the last entry of the last even
#' column, the accelerated limit. Two equal neighbours mean the sequence has
#' already settled there.
#' @param s Partial sums.
#' @return The estimated limit.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_wynn <- function(s) {
  table <- list(rep(0, length(s) + 1L), s)
  limit <- s[length(s)]
  # The table is built column by column, each from the two before it.
  while (length(table[[length(table)]]) > 2L) {
    current <- table[[length(table)]]
    before <- table[[length(table) - 1L]]
    gaps <- diff(current)
    if (any(gaps == 0)) break
    following <- before[-c(1L, length(before))][seq_along(gaps)] + 1 / gaps
    table <- c(table, list(following))
    if ((length(table) - 2L) %% 2L == 0L) limit <- following[length(following)]
  }
  limit
}

.latents_vuong_row.name: .latents_vuong_row

before.name: .latents_vuong_row
before.documentation:
#' One VLMR and adjusted LMR comparison of two fitted candidates
#'
#' The adjusted statistic divides LR by `1 + 1 / (d log n)`, with `d` the
#' difference in the number of parameters and `n` the number of independent
#' units (Lo, Mendell and Rubin 2001, eq. 15, with their three parameters per
#' added univariate normal component replaced by the models' own difference),
#' and is referred to the same distribution.
#' @param alternative,null From `.latents_vuong_parts()`.
#' @return A one-row data frame: `n_units`, `parameters_added`, `lr`,
#'   `vlmr_p`, `adjusted_lr`, `almr_p`, `reference_mean`, `reference_sd`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_vuong_row <- function(alternative, null) {
  lr <- 2 * (alternative$log_likelihood - null$log_likelihood)
  if (lr < -1e-8 * (1 + abs(null$log_likelihood))) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste("The alternative has a lower likelihood than the null;",
                              "the nested comparison needs a better-fitting alternative."),
                        class = "latents_invalid_lmr", call = NULL))
  }
  lr <- max(0, lr)
  lambda <- .latents_vuong_weights(alternative, null)
  added <- alternative$n_parameters - null$n_parameters
  n_units <- alternative$n_units %||% nrow(alternative$scores)
  stopifnot("the two models must count the same independent units" =
              n_units == (null$n_units %||% nrow(null$scores)))
  adjusted <- lr / (1 + 1 / (added * log(n_units)))
  data.frame(n_units = n_units, parameters_added = added, lr = lr,
             vlmr_p = .latents_imhof_upper(lr, lambda), adjusted_lr = adjusted,
             almr_p = .latents_imhof_upper(adjusted, lambda),
             reference_mean = sum(lambda), reference_sd = sqrt(2 * sum(lambda^2)))
}

.latents_join_pairs.name: .latents_join_pairs

before.name: .latents_join_pairs
before.documentation:
#' Add the joint indicator of each pair to a data frame
#'
#' Each joint value is the two items' values joined by a colon, missing when
#' either item is. A frame that already holds a joint indicator (the frame a
#' fit stores, or one this function has joined) is left as it is, so joining
#' is idempotent. Rows where one item of a pair is observed and the other is
#' not lose the pair, which is reported with `latents_partial_pair`.
#' @param data A data frame.
#' @param pairs From `.latents_parse_pairs()`.
#' @param min_categories Minimum observed categories of each original item;
#'   fitting requires two, prediction subsets may have none.
#' @param rebuild_existing Regenerate an existing joint column from its source
#'   items when a fitted model has already established their meaning. Initial
#'   fitting leaves this false so existing caller columns remain protected.
#' @return The data frame with one more column per pair.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_join_pairs <- function(data, pairs, min_categories = 0L,
                                 rebuild_existing = FALSE) {
  if (!is.null(pairs$kind)) pairs <- pairs[pairs$kind == "categorical", , drop = FALSE]
  joined <- Reduce(function(frame, index) {
    pair <- pairs[index, ]
    has_items <- all(c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2) %in% names(frame))
    prepared <- pair$name %in% names(frame) &&
      identical(attr(frame[[pair$name]], "latents_pair"), c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2))
    if (pair$name %in% names(frame) && !has_items &&
        (!any(c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2) %in% names(frame)) || prepared)) return(frame)
    if (!has_items) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
        "`data` needs `%s` and `%s` for the pair \"%s\" of `local_dependence`.",
        pair$item_1, pair$item_2, pair$name), class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
    }
    first <- frame[[pair$item_1]]
    second <- frame[[pair$item_2]]
    first_levels <- .multilpa_categorical_levels(first, pair$item_1, min_categories)
    second_levels <- .multilpa_categorical_levels(second, pair$item_2, min_categories)
    # A joint category is written "first:second", so a category that already
    # holds a colon makes two responses one label: ("x:y", "z") and
    # ("x", "y:z") would be counted as the same response.
    colons <- Filter(function(item) {
      any(grepl(":", unique(as.character(frame[[item]])), fixed = TRUE))
    }, c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2))
    if (length(colons) > 0L) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "The categories of %s contain \":\", which joins the two items of the",
        "pair \"%s\"; recode them without a colon."),
        paste(sprintf("`%s`", colons), collapse = " and "), pair$name),
        class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
    }
    observed <- !is.na(first) & !is.na(second)
    labels <- ifelse(observed, paste(as.character(first), as.character(second), sep = ":"),
                     NA_character_)
    # Base rbind() drops custom factor attributes but keeps the first frame's
    # metadata. Trust that fallback only when the column still contains the
    # joint responses of its source items; stale metadata cannot authorize
    # replacing a newly assigned, unrelated column.
    frame_pairs <- attr(frame, "latents_pairs")
    prepared <- prepared || (pair$name %in% names(frame) &&
      identical(frame_pairs[[pair$name]], c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2)) &&
      is.factor(frame[[pair$name]]) &&
      identical(as.character(frame[[pair$name]]), labels))
    # Only columns produced by this preparation may be regenerated beside
    # their source items. A caller column with the same name is never replaced.
    if (pair$name %in% names(frame) && !prepared && !rebuild_existing) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "The generated joint indicator `%s` conflicts with an existing column;",
        "rename that column before using `local_dependence`."), pair$name),
        class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
    }
    partial <- xor(is.na(first), is.na(second))
    if (any(partial)) {
      warning(warningCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "%d rows observe only one item of the pair \"%s\"; the pair is treated",
        "as missing in those rows."), sum(partial), pair$name),
        class = "latents_partial_pair", call = NULL))
    }
    # Categories ordered by the first item's categories, then the second's.
    grid <- expand.grid(second = as.character(second_levels),
                        first = as.character(first_levels), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    combinations <- paste(grid$first, grid$second, sep = ":")
    frame[[pair$name]] <- factor(labels, levels = combinations)
    attr(frame[[pair$name]], "latents_pair") <- c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2)
    frame_pairs[[pair$name]] <- c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2)
    attr(frame, "latents_pairs") <- frame_pairs
    frame
  }, seq_len(nrow(pairs)), init = data)
  joined
}

    first <- frame[[pair$item_1]]
    second <- frame[[pair$item_2]]
    first_levels <- .multilpa_categorical_levels(first, pair$item_1, min_categories)
    second_levels <- .multilpa_categorical_levels(second, pair$item_2, min_categories)
    # A joint category is written "first:second", so a category that already
    # holds a colon makes two responses one label: ("x:y", "z") and
    # ("x", "y:z") would be counted as the same response.
    colons <- Filter(function(item) {
      any(grepl(":", unique(as.character(frame[[item]])), fixed = TRUE))
    }, c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2))
    if (length(colons) > 0L) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "The categories of %s contain \":\", which joins the two items of the",
        "pair \"%s\"; recode them without a colon."),
        paste(sprintf("`%s`", colons), collapse = " and "), pair$name),
        class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
    }
    observed <- !is.na(first) & !is.na(second)
    labels <- ifelse(observed, paste(as.character(first), as.character(second), sep = ":"),
                     NA_character_)
    # Base rbind() drops custom factor attributes but keeps the first frame's
    # metadata. Trust that fallback only when the column still contains the
    # joint responses of its source items; stale metadata cannot authorize
    # replacing a newly assigned, unrelated column.
    frame_pairs <- attr(frame, "latents_pairs")
    prepared <- prepared || (pair$name %in% names(frame) &&
      identical(frame_pairs[[pair$name]], c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2)) &&
      is.factor(frame[[pair$name]]) &&
      identical(as.character(frame[[pair$name]]), labels))
    # Only columns produced by this preparation may be regenerated beside
    # their source items. A caller column with the same name is never replaced.
    if (pair$name %in% names(frame) && !prepared && !rebuild_existing) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "The generated joint indicator `%s` conflicts with an existing column;",
        "rename that column before using `local_dependence`."), pair$name),
        class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
    }
    partial <- xor(is.na(first), is.na(second))
    if (any(partial)) {
      warning(warningCondition(sprintf(paste(
        "%d rows observe only one item of the pair \"%s\"; the pair is treated",
        "as missing in those rows."), sum(partial), pair$name),
        class = "latents_partial_pair", call = NULL))
    }
    # Categories ordered by the first item's categories, then the second's.
    grid <- expand.grid(second = as.character(second_levels),
                        first = as.character(first_levels), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    combinations <- paste(grid$first, grid$second, sep = ":")
    frame[[pair$name]] <- factor(labels, levels = combinations)
    attr(frame[[pair$name]], "latents_pair") <- c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2)
    frame_pairs[[pair$name]] <- c(pair$item_1, pair$item_2)
    attr(frame, "latents_pairs") <- frame_pairs
    frame
  }, seq_len(nrow(pairs)), init = data)
  joined
}

before.name: .latents_fit_local_dependence
before.documentation:
#' Fit a model whose `local_dependence` pairs are joined first
#'
#' Called by [multilpa()] when `local_dependence` is given: the pairs are
#' joined in `data`, `vars` and `categorical`, and the model is fitted on the
#' joint indicators, with the caller's own arguments otherwise unchanged.
#' @param call The caller's `match.call()`.
#' @param env The calling function's environment, holding the matched values.
#' @param local_dependence The caller's pairs.
#' @return The fit, carrying `local_dependence` (the pairs) and the caller's
#'   `call`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_fit_local_dependence <- function(call, env, local_dependence) {
  pairs <- .latents_parse_pairs(local_dependence)
  arguments <- mget(setdiff(names(call)[-1L], "local_dependence"), envir = env)
  if (!is.null(arguments$family) && !identical(arguments$family, "profiles")) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "`local_dependence` pairs the indicators of a profile or class model;",
      "the group-class families have no categorical items to pair."),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  items <- c(pairs$item_1, pairs$item_2)
  categorical <- arguments$categorical %||% character()
  # Joining removes original item names and deduplicates the new name list;
  # preserve the ordinary identity checks before either transformation.
  if (anyNA(arguments$vars) || anyDuplicated(arguments$vars) ||
      !all(arguments$vars %in% names(arguments$data)) ||
      any(arguments$id %in% arguments$vars)) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "Supply unique existing indicators and a distinct group column.",
      class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(categorical) || !all(categorical %in% arguments$vars)) {
    stop(errorCondition("`categorical` must name distinct indicators listed in `vars`.",
                        class = "latents_bad_categorical", call = NULL))
  }
  absent <- setdiff(items, arguments$vars)
  if (length(absent) > 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
      "`local_dependence` names %s, which %s not among `vars`.",
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", absent), collapse = ", "),
      if (length(absent) > 1L) "are" else "is"), class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  pairs <- .latents_classify_pairs(pairs, categorical)
  # Once joined, a paired item is no longer among `vars`, so the checks that
  # keep an indicator from also being a covariate cannot see it; they are made
  # here, with the classes those checks raise.
  covariates <- c(arguments$profile_covariates, arguments$group_covariates,
                  if (length(arguments$direct_effects) > 0L)
                    .latents_parse_direct_effects(arguments$direct_effects)$covariate)
  reused <- intersect(covariates, items)
  if (length(reused) > 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
      "%s %s an indicator of a `local_dependence` pair, so it cannot also be a covariate.",
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", reused), collapse = ", "),
      if (length(reused) > 1L) "are" else "is"),
      class = c("multilpa_indicator_reused", "latents_bad_covariate"), call = NULL))
  }
  joined_pairs <- pairs[pairs$kind == "categorical", , drop = FALSE]
  continuous_pairs <- pairs[pairs$kind == "continuous", , drop = FALSE]
  arguments$local_dependence <- if (nrow(continuous_pairs) > 0L) continuous_pairs$name
  # Apply the same native-value and variation requirements as unpaired items.
  # The join itself permits constant/single-row subsets used by prediction.
  arguments$data <- .latents_join_pairs(arguments$data, joined_pairs, min_categories = 2L)
  # Each joint category's two levels, read from the data rather than parsed
  # back out of the label.
  categories <- lapply(stats::setNames(seq_len(nrow(joined_pairs)), joined_pairs$name),
                       function(index) {
    first <- as.character(arguments$data[[joined_pairs$item_1[index]]])
    second <- as.character(arguments$data[[joined_pairs$item_2[index]]])
    label <- as.character(arguments$data[[joined_pairs$name[index]]])
    unique(data.frame(label = label, level_1 = first, level_2 = second,
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[!is.na(label), , drop = FALSE])
  })
  original <- list(vars = arguments$vars, categorical = categorical)
  arguments$vars <- .latents_joined_names(arguments$vars, joined_pairs)
  arguments$categorical <- .latents_joined_names(categorical, joined_pairs)
  fit <- do.call(multilpa, arguments)
  fit$local_dependence <- pairs
  fit$local_dependence_categories <- categories
  # The caller's own indicators, so the fit compares with one of the same data
  # whose items were not paired.
  fit$original_vars <- original$vars
  fit$original_categorical <- original$categorical
  fit$call <- call
  fit
}

before.name: .latents_local_dependence_table
before.documentation:
#' The joint and independent probabilities of each locally dependent pair
#'
#' For every pair and profile, every combination of the two items'
#' categories: its probability under the fitted joint distribution, the
#' product of the two marginal probabilities it would have if the items were
#' independent within the profile, and their ratio. A ratio far from one in a
#' profile is the dependence the joint indicator captures.
#' @param x A fitted model with `local_dependence`.
#' @return A data frame, one row per pair, profile and combination: `pair`,
#'   `profile`, `item_1`, `category_1`, `item_2`, `category_2`,
#'   `probability`, `independent` and `ratio`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_local_dependence_table <- function(x) {
  pairs <- x$local_dependence
  if (is.null(pairs) || nrow(pairs) == 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "This fit has no locally dependent pairs; fit with",
      "`local_dependence = \"item1:item2\"` to model one."),
      class = "latents_no_local_dependence", call = NULL))
  }
  kinds <- pairs$kind %||% rep("categorical", nrow(pairs))
  rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(index) {
    pair <- pairs[index, ]
    if (identical(kinds[index], "continuous")) {
      # The pair's covariance in each profile, and the correlation it implies.
      continuous <- .multilpa_continuous_names(x)
      first <- match(pair$item_1, continuous)
      second <- match(pair$item_2, continuous)
      return(do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(x$n_profiles), function(profile) {
        covariance <- matrix(x$covariances[, , profile], length(continuous))
        data.frame(pair = pair$name, kind = "continuous", profile = profile,
                   item_1 = pair$item_1, category_1 = NA_character_,
                   item_2 = pair$item_2, category_2 = NA_character_,
                   probability = NA_real_, independent = NA_real_, ratio = NA_real_,
                   covariance = covariance[first, second],
                   correlation = covariance[first, second] /
                     sqrt(covariance[first, first] * covariance[second, second]),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      })))
    }
    probabilities <- x$response_probabilities[[pair$name]]
    labels <- x$categorical_levels[[pair$name]]
    categories <- x$local_dependence_categories[[pair$name]]
    at <- match(labels, categories$label)
    first_items <- categories$level_1[at]
    second_items <- categories$level_2[at]
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(probabilities)), function(profile) {
      joint <- probabilities[profile, ]
      marginal_1 <- tapply(joint, first_items, sum)[first_items]
      marginal_2 <- tapply(joint, second_items, sum)[second_items]
      independent <- unname(marginal_1 * marginal_2)
      data.frame(pair = pair$name, kind = "categorical", profile = profile,
                 item_1 = pair$item_1, category_1 = first_items,
                 item_2 = pair$item_2, category_2 = second_items,
                 probability = unname(joint), independent = independent,
                 ratio = unname(joint) / independent, covariance = NA_real_,
                 correlation = NA_real_, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  })
  result <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(result) <- NULL
  result
}

before.name: lpa
before.documentation:
#' Fit a latent profile model
#'
#' Fits a single-level latent profile model and returns a fitted `multilpa`
#' object. The model is a finite mixture of multivariate normal distributions:
#' each observation belongs to one of `n_profiles` unobserved profiles, and each
#' profile has its own mean on every indicator. It is the model [multilpa()]
#' fits with `id = NULL`, so every accessor, plot and inference verb of the
#' package applies to the result.
#'
#' For observations nested in groups, use [multilpa()] with the grouping column
#' as `id`, which adds latent classes of groups above the profiles.
#'
#' @param data A data frame with one row per observation.
#' @param vars Names of the indicator columns. Numeric columns are continuous
#'   indicators; categorical ones are named in `categorical`.
#' @param n_profiles Number of profiles, a positive whole number.
#' @param ... Further arguments for [multilpa()]: the covariance structure
#'   (`model`, or `variance_model` and `covariance_model`, or `volume`,
#'   `shape` and `orientation`), `missing`, `categorical`, `n_starts`,
#'   `seed`, `boundary`, `prior`, `noise`, `profile_covariates` and the others
#'   it documents, except `id` and `n_group_classes`.
#' @return A fitted `multilpa` object, as [multilpa()] returns, whose `call`
#'   is the `lpa()` call.
#' @section Conditions:
#'   `latents_bad_argument` when `id` or `n_group_classes` is passed; the
#'   conditions [multilpa()] raises otherwise.
#' @references
#' Oberski, D. (2016). Mixture models: Latent profile and latent class
#' analysis. In J. Robertson & M. Kaptein (Eds.), *Modern Statistical Methods
#' for HCI* (pp. 275--287). Springer.
#' @seealso [lca()] for categorical indicators; [multilpa()] for the two-level
#'   model; [enumerate_lpa()] to compare numbers of profiles.
#' @examples
#' fit <- lpa(srl, c("cognitive_strategies", "intrinsic_value",
#'                   "self_efficacy", "self_regulation", "test_anxiety"),
#'            n_profiles = 2, variance_model = "equal",
#'            covariance_model = "full", n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
#' fit
#' plot(fit, what = "raincloud")
#' @export
before.source:
lpa <- function(data, vars, n_profiles, ...) {

#' Compare latent profile models
#'
#' Fits a single-level latent profile model for each number of profiles in
#' `n_profiles` under each covariance structure in `model`, and returns a
#' `multilpa_enumeration` object that tabulates the information criteria,
#' entropy and diagnostics of every fit. It is [enumerate_classes()] with
#' `id = NULL`.
#'
#' For observations nested in groups, use [enumerate_classes()] with the
#' grouping column as `id`, which also crosses the number of group classes.
#'
#' @param data A data frame with one row per observation.
#' @param vars Names of the indicator columns.
#' @param n_profiles Positive whole numbers of profiles to compare.
#' @param model The covariance structures: `"basic"`, the default, for the
#'   four that combine equal or varying variances with covariances absent or
#'   present (`EEI`, `VVI`, `EEE`, `VVV`); `"all"` for all 14; or their
#'   three-letter codes. See [enumerate_classes()].
#' @param ... Further arguments for [multilpa()], such as `missing`,
#'   `n_starts`, `seed`, `boundary` and `categorical`, except `id` and
#'   `n_group_classes`.
#' @return An object of class `multilpa_enumeration`, as [enumerate_classes()]
#'   returns: [as.data.frame()] gives one row per candidate, [summary()] the
#'   candidate each criterion prefers, [plot()] the criteria against the
#'   number of profiles, and [get_candidate()] one fitted candidate.
#' @section Conditions:
#'   `latents_bad_argument` when `id` or `n_group_classes` is passed, or when
#'   `model` names an unknown structure.
#' @references
#' Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (1995). Gaussian parsimonious clustering models.
#' *Pattern Recognition*, 28(5), 781--793.
#' @seealso [lpa()] to fit one model; [enumerate_lca()] for categorical
#'   indicators; [bootstrap_lrt()] to test one number of profiles against
#'   another.
#' @examples
#' models <- enumerate_lpa(srl, c("cognitive_strategies", "intrinsic_value",
#'                                "self_efficacy", "self_regulation",
#'                                "test_anxiety"),
#'                         n_profiles = 1:3, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#' summary(models)
#' plot(models)
#' @export
before.terminal_expression: .latents_candidate_data(.multilpa_quiet_single_level(enumerate_classes(data, vars, id = NULL, n_profiles = n_profiles, model = model, ...)), data_expression)

before.name: .lta_bootstrap_inference
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(x = , data = , level = , iter = , n_starts = , max_iter = , tol = , adjust = ))
before.documentation:
#' Percentile bootstrap inference for a transition fit
#'
#' Called by [parameter_inference()] on a `multilpa_transitions` or
#' `multilpa_lta` fit when `method = "bootstrap"`. Persons (the `id` groups)
#' are the resampled units, so dependence across a person's occasions is kept.
#' The table has the Wald path's rows and columns; `standard_error` is the
#' standard deviation of the replicates and `conf_low`/`conf_high` their
#' percentile interval, while `statistic`, `p_value` and `p_adjusted` are `NA`.
#'
#' @param x A transition fit.
#' @param data The data it was fitted to.
#' @param level Interval level.
#' @param iter,n_starts,max_iter,tol Resamples, and the controls of each refit.
#' @param adjust Kept for a frame of the same shape as the Wald path's.
#' @return A base `data.frame` with attributes `covariance`, `level`,
#'   `method`, `iter`, `n_valid`, `replicates` and `messages`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_bootstrap_inference <- function(x, data, level, iter, n_starts, max_iter, tol,
                                     adjust) {
  if (is.null(data)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "The bootstrap for a transition model needs `data`: each resample keeps",
      "its persons' occasions and covariates."),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  .lta_check_data(x, data)
  if (!isTRUE(x$converged)) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "The original fit did not converge; bootstrap it only once it has.",
      class = "latents_no_converge", call = NULL))
  }
  table <- .lta_bootstrap_frame(x)
  drawn <- .lta_bootstrap_replicates(x, data, iter, n_starts, max_iter, tol,
                                     table$name)
  valid <- stats::complete.cases(drawn$estimates)
  if (sum(valid) < 2L) {
    reasons <- drawn$messages[!is.na(drawn$messages)]
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
      "Only %d of %d resamples produced a usable fit; the first reason was: %s",
      sum(valid), iter,
      if (length(reasons) > 0L) reasons[1L] else "no reason was recorded"),
      class = "latents_bootstrap_failed", call = NULL))
  }
  if (sum(valid) < iter) {
    warning(warningCondition(sprintf(
      "%d of %d resamples did not produce a usable fit and were dropped.",
      iter - sum(valid), iter), class = "latents_bootstrap_dropped", call = NULL))
  }
  kept <- drawn$estimates[valid, , drop = FALSE]
  quantiles <- apply(kept, 2L, stats::quantile,
                     probs = c((1 - level) / 2, (1 + level) / 2), names = FALSE)
  table$standard_error <- apply(kept, 2L, stats::sd)
  # The interval is the inference: a Wald statistic would put back the normal
  # approximation the percentile interval avoids.
  table$statistic <- NA_real_
  table$p_value <- NA_real_
  table$p_adjusted <- NA_real_
  table$conf_low <- quantiles[1L, ]
  table$conf_high <- quantiles[2L, ]
  covariance <- stats::cov(kept)
  dimnames(covariance) <- list(table$name, table$name)
  columns <- setdiff(names(table), "name")
  result <- table[, columns, drop = FALSE]
  row.names(result) <- NULL
  structure(result, covariance = covariance, covariance_unconstrained = NULL,
            level = level, method = "bootstrap", iter = iter, n_valid = sum(valid),
            replicates = kept, messages = drawn$messages, adjust = adjust)
}
before.terminal_expression: structure(result, covariance = covariance, covariance_unconstrained = NULL, level = level, method = "bootstrap", iter = iter, n_valid = sum(valid), replicates = kept, messages = drawn$messages, adjust = adjust)

before.name: .lta_bootstrap_frame
before.documentation:
#' The rows a transition bootstrap reports, with their estimates
#'
#' The same rows, labels and column order as the Wald table of the fit's
#' class, plus `name`, the coefficient each row is matched on.
#'
#' @param x A transition fit.
#' @return A base `data.frame`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_bootstrap_frame <- function(x) {
  estimates <- .lta_bootstrap_estimates(x)
  if (inherits(x, "multilpa_transitions")) {
    labels <- .multilpa_transition_labels(names(estimates), .multilpa_transition_view(x))
    return(data.frame(labels, estimate = unname(estimates), standard_error = NA_real_,
                      statistic = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, p_adjusted = NA_real_,
                      conf_low = NA_real_, conf_high = NA_real_, name = names(estimates),
                      row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  }
  pieces <- strsplit(names(estimates), ".", fixed = TRUE)
  block <- vapply(pieces, `[`, character(1), 1L)
  moves <- strsplit(vapply(pieces, `[`, character(1), 3L), "->", fixed = TRUE)
  second <- block == "transition2"
  frame <- data.frame(
    block = block,
    group_class = vapply(pieces, `[`, character(1), 2L),
    # An initial logit names one profile, a move names its origin before it.
    from = vapply(moves, function(m) if (length(m) < 2L) NA_character_ else
      m[length(m) - 1L], character(1)),
    to = vapply(moves, function(m) m[length(m)], character(1)),
    term = vapply(pieces, function(p) paste(p[-(1:3)], collapse = "."), character(1)),
    estimate = unname(estimates), standard_error = NA_real_, statistic = NA_real_,
    p_value = NA_real_, p_adjusted = NA_real_, conf_low = NA_real_,
    conf_high = NA_real_, name = names(estimates), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (any(second)) {
    frame$previous <- ifelse(second, vapply(moves, `[`, character(1), 1L), NA_character_)
  }
  # The Wald table's block order: transitions, initial, then second order.
  frame[order(match(frame$block, c("transition", "initial", "transition2")),
              seq_len(nrow(frame))), , drop = FALSE]
}

before.name: .lta_align_estimates
before.documentation:
#' A replicate's reported estimates, in the original fit's labels
#'
#' Profiles are matched on the measurement, then group classes on what the
#' matched profiles make of them.
#'
#' @param replicate A transition fit from a resample.
#' @param reference The original fit.
#' @return The replicate's estimates, named as the original's.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_align_estimates <- function(replicate, reference) {
  profile_order <- .multilpa_match_order(.lta_profile_signature(reference, reference),
                                         .lta_profile_signature(replicate, reference))
  if (inherits(reference, "multilpa_transitions")) {
    permuted <- .lta_permute_transitions(replicate, profile_order,
                                         seq_len(replicate$n_group_classes))
    class_order <- .multilpa_match_order(.lta_class_signature(reference),
                                         .lta_class_signature(permuted))
    return(.multilpa_transition_encode(
      .lta_permute_transitions(permuted, seq_len(permuted$n_profiles), class_order),
      "natural"))
  }
  relabelled <- .lta_relabel_profiles(.lta_bootstrap_estimates(replicate), profile_order)
  classes <- names(reference$group_probabilities)
  class_order <- .multilpa_match_order(
    .lta_class_signature(reference, .lta_bootstrap_estimates(reference)),
    .lta_class_signature(replicate, relabelled))
  .lta_relabel_classes(relabelled, class_order, classes)
}

.lta_relabel_profiles.name: .lta_relabel_profiles

before.name: .lta_relabel_profiles
before.documentation:
#' Rename profiles in general-fit logits, rebasing the initial logits
#'
#' Transitions and second-order transitions are logits against staying, which
#' a relabelling maps to staying, so their names move and their values do not.
#' Initial logits are against the last profile: when another profile becomes
#' last, every initial logit is shifted by the new reference's.
#'
#' @param estimates Named logits of one fit.
#' @param order Integer permutation: new profile `j` is old profile `order[j]`.
#' @return The logits, named in the new labels.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_relabel_profiles <- function(estimates, order) {
  n_profiles <- length(order)
  new_of_old <- match(seq_len(n_profiles), order)
  pieces <- strsplit(names(estimates), ".", fixed = TRUE)
  block <- vapply(pieces, `[`, character(1), 1L)
  rename <- function(profiles) {
    numbers <- as.integer(sub("^profile_", "", strsplit(profiles, "->", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]))
    paste(paste0("profile_", new_of_old[numbers]), collapse = "->")
  }
  moved <- vapply(seq_along(pieces), function(i) {
    p <- pieces[[i]]
    paste(c(p[1L], p[2L], rename(p[3L]), p[-(1:3)]), collapse = ".")
  }, character(1))
  result <- stats::setNames(unname(estimates), moved)
  initial <- block == "initial"
  if (!any(initial)) return(result)
  # One baseline-category logit vector per group class and term.
  owner <- vapply(pieces[initial], function(p) paste(c(p[2L], p[-(1:3)]), collapse = "\r"),
                  character(1))
  old_profile <- as.integer(sub("^profile_", "", vapply(pieces[initial], `[`,
                                                        character(1), 3L)))
  rebased <- unlist(unname(lapply(split(seq_along(owner), owner), function(rows) {
    eta <- numeric(n_profiles)
    eta[old_profile[rows]] <- estimates[initial][rows]
    shifted <- .latents_rebase_logits(matrix(eta, 1L), order)[1L, ]
    p <- pieces[initial][[rows[1L]]]
    stats::setNames(shifted[-n_profiles],
                    paste(p[1L], p[2L], paste0("profile_", seq_len(n_profiles - 1L)),
                          paste(p[-(1:3)], collapse = "."), sep = "."))
  })))
  c(result[!initial], rebased)
}

before.name: .lta_check_data
before.documentation:
#' Verify original indicators, occasions and covariate designs of an LTA fit
#' @param fit A fitted transition model.
#' @param data Its original data frame.
#' @return `NULL`, invisibly; refuses mismatched fitting data.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_check_data <- function(fit, data) {
  a <- .lta_arguments(fit)
  required <- c(a$vars, a$id, a$time, a$transition_covariates, a$initial_covariates)
  refuse <- function() stop(errorCondition(
    "`data` must reproduce the indicators, groups, occasions and covariates of both fits.",
    class = "latents_bad_inference_data", call = NULL))
  if (!is.data.frame(data) || nrow(data) != fit$n_observations ||
      !all(required %in% names(data))) refuse()
  if (!inherits(fit, "multilpa_lta")) {
    .multilpa_check_transition_data(fit, data)
    if (length(fit$categorical) &&
        !identical(.multilpa_encode_categorical(data[fit$categorical])$levels,
                   fit$categorical_levels)) refuse()
    if (!identical(.multilpa_time_values(data, a$time, a$id, a$vars),
                   fit$time_values)) refuse()
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  groups <- .multilpa_prepare_groups(data[[a$id]])
  time_values <- .multilpa_time_values(data, a$time, a$id, a$vars)
  layout <- .multilpa_sequence_layout(groups$index, time_values, groups$n, a$occasions)
  designs <- .lta_designs(layout, .lta_covariate_matrix(data, a$transition_covariates),
                         .lta_covariate_matrix(data, a$initial_covariates), a$transitions)
  x <- sweep(as.matrix(data[fit$continuous]), 2L, fit$centers, "-")
  encoded <- if (!length(fit$categorical)) NULL else
    .multilpa_encode_categorical(data[fit$categorical])
  codes <- encoded$codes
  extra <- .latents_prepare_extra(data, fit$ordinal, fit$count, a$missing)
  same <- function(left, right) isTRUE(all.equal(left, right, check.attributes = FALSE,
                                                tolerance = 1e-12))
  if (!identical(groups$ids, fit$group_ids) || !identical(groups$index, fit$group_index) ||
      !identical(time_values, fit$time_values) || !identical(layout, fit$layout) ||
      !identical(encoded$levels, fit$categorical_levels) || !same(designs, fit$designs) ||
      !same(x, fit$x) || !same(codes, fit$codes) ||
      !identical(extra$ordinal_levels, fit$extra_data$ordinal_levels) ||
      !same(extra$ordinal, fit$extra_data$ordinal) ||
      !same(extra$count, fit$extra_data$count)) refuse()
  invisible(NULL)
}

#' Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test between nested transition fits
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_bootstrap_lrt <- function(null_model, alternative_model, data, iter, n_starts,
                               max_iter, tol, seed, call) {
  positive_integer <- function(value) is.numeric(value) && length(value) == 1L &&
    is.finite(value) && value >= 1 && value <= .Machine$integer.max && value == floor(value)
  stopifnot("`iter` must be a positive integer" = positive_integer(iter),
            "`n_starts` must be a positive integer" =
              is.null(n_starts) || positive_integer(n_starts),
            "`max_iter` must be a nonnegative integer" =
              is.null(max_iter) || positive_integer(max_iter + 1),
            "`tol` must be a positive finite number" = is.null(tol) ||
              (is.numeric(tol) && length(tol) == 1L && is.finite(tol) && tol > 0))
  if (is.null(data)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "bootstrap_lrt() for transition models needs `data`: the simulation keeps",
      "its groups, occasions and covariates."), class = "latents_bad_argument",
      call = NULL))
  }
  if (!.lta_nested(null_model, alternative_model)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "The null transition model must be nested in the alternative: same",
      "indicators, groups and occasions, and every option at most as free."),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  if (!isTRUE(null_model$converged) || !isTRUE(alternative_model$converged)) {
    stop(errorCondition("Both fits must have converged.",
                        class = "latents_no_converge", call = NULL))
  }
  lapply(list(null_model, alternative_model), .lta_check_data, data = data)
  # Whether the null can be simulated from is a property of the fit, not of a
  # replicate: refuse here, or every replicate fails and the classed refusal
  # surfaces only as a generic failed-replicates warning.
  .lta_general_view(null_model, data)
  .multilpa_check_seed(seed)
  .latents_local_seed(seed)
  # Each model is refitted as it was fitted (see `.latents_refit_controls()`).
  refit_tol <- max(.latents_refit_controls(null_model, n_starts, max_iter, tol)$tol,
                   .latents_refit_controls(alternative_model, n_starts, max_iter, tol)$tol)
  reversal_window <- 100 * refit_tol * (1 + abs(null_model$log_likelihood))
  observed <- 2 * (alternative_model$log_likelihood - null_model$log_likelihood)
  if (observed < -reversal_window) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "Alternative has lower likelihood by %.3g; improve its optimization first."),
      -observed), class = "latents_reversed_likelihood", call = NULL))
  }
  observed <- max(0, observed)
  replicates <- .latents_blrt_replicates(iter, function(i) {
    simulated <- .lta_simulate(null_model, data)
    models <- lapply(list(null_model, alternative_model), .lta_refit, simulated,
                     n_starts, max_iter, tol)
    statistic <- 2 * (models[[2L]]$log_likelihood - models[[1L]]$log_likelihood)
    list(statistic = statistic,
         valid = all(vapply(models, function(m) isTRUE(m$converged), logical(1))) &&
           statistic >= -reversal_window,
         boundary = any(vapply(models, function(m) isTRUE(m$boundary), logical(1))),
         logits_settled = NA, null_replications = NA_integer_,
         alternative_replications = NA_integer_)
  }, muffle_warnings = TRUE)
  tally <- .latents_blrt_p_value(replicates, observed, iter)
  describe <- function(fit) {
    a <- .lta_arguments(fit)
    paste(c(sprintf("lta with %d profiles", a$n_profiles),
            if (isTRUE(a$mover_stayer)) "stayer class",
            if (a$order >= 2L) "second order",
            if (!identical(a$transitions, "homogeneous")) "occasion transitions",
            if (length(a$transition_covariates)) paste("transitions on",
                                                        paste(a$transition_covariates, collapse = "+")),
            if (length(a$initial_covariates)) paste("initial on",
                                                     paste(a$initial_covariates, collapse = "+")),
            if (!identical(a$measurement, "invariant")) "occasion measurement"),
          collapse = ", ")
  }
  result <- list(statistic = observed, p_value = tally$p_value,
                 monte_carlo_se = tally$monte_carlo_se,
                 iter = iter, n_valid = tally$n_valid, replicates = replicates,
                 fixed = character(),
                 null_profiles = .lta_arguments(null_model)$n_profiles,
                 null_group_classes = .lta_arguments(null_model)$n_group_classes,
                 alternative_profiles = .lta_arguments(alternative_model)$n_profiles,
                 alternative_group_classes = .lta_arguments(alternative_model)$n_group_classes,
                 null_family = describe(null_model),
                 alternative_family = describe(alternative_model), call = call)
  class(result) <- "multilpa_bootstrap_lrt"
  result
}

before.name: .lta_enumerate
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(data = , vars = , id = , time = , n_profiles = , n_group_classes = , model = , seed = , extra = , call = , cores = 1L, verbose = FALSE))
before.documentation:
#' Enumerate transition models over numbers of profiles and group classes
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_enumerate <- function(data, vars, id, time, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                           model, seed, extra, call, cores = 1L,
                           verbose = FALSE) {
  # These arguments also travel in the candidate closure on socket workers.
  force(data)
  force(vars)
  force(id)
  force(time)
  force(n_profiles)
  force(n_group_classes)
  force(model)
  force(seed)
  force(extra)
  force(call)
  force(cores)
  worker_report <- .latents_worker_reporter()
  on.exit(worker_report$signal(), add = TRUE)
  unknown <- setdiff(names(extra), setdiff(names(formals(lta)),
                                           c("data", "vars", "id", "time", "n_profiles",
                                             "n_group_classes", "seed", "model")))
  if (length(unknown) > 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf("%s %s not an argument of lta().",
                                paste(sprintf("`%s`", unknown), collapse = ", "),
                                if (length(unknown) == 1L) "is" else "are"),
                        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  if (any(n_profiles < 2)) {
    stop(errorCondition("Transition models need at least two profiles.",
                        class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
  }
  models <- if (is.null(model)) NA_character_ else model
  grid <- expand.grid(n_profiles = unique(n_profiles),
                      n_group_classes = unique(n_group_classes), model = models,
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  indices <- seq_len(nrow(grid))
  costs <- grid$n_group_classes * grid$n_profiles^2
  started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  # Each candidate seeds its own draws, so its setup gives the same plan on a
  # worker as here. Only forced EM inputs and one start travel to a worker
  # for fitting, never a finaliser.
  setup_tasks <- lapply(indices, function(i) {
    model_i <- if (is.na(grid$model[i])) NULL else grid$model[i]
    fit_call <- .latents_candidate_call("lta", call$data, c(
      list(vars = vars, id = id, time = time, n_profiles = grid$n_profiles[i],
           n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes[i], seed = seed,
           model = model_i), extra))
    list(candidate = i, arguments = c(
      list(data = data, vars = vars, id = id, time = time,
           n_profiles = grid$n_profiles[i], n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes[i],
           seed = seed, model = model_i, call = fit_call), extra))
  })
  .latents_pool_progress(verbose, "Preparing %s on %s.",
                         .latents_count(length(indices), "candidate"),
                         .latents_count(min(cores, length(indices)), "worker"))
  candidates <- worker_report$collect(function() .latents_pool_setup(
    setup_tasks, .lta_setup_task, costs, cores, distribute = !is.null(seed)))
  # emEM has two flat, dynamically balanced phases. The protected first
  # start and likelihood ranking use the same helpers as a direct lta fit.
  screen_tasks <- .lta_start_tasks(candidates, "screen")
  if (length(screen_tasks)) {
    .latents_pool_progress(verbose, "Screening %s on %s.",
                           .latents_count(length(screen_tasks), "start"),
                           .latents_count(min(cores, length(screen_tasks)), "worker"))
  }
  screened <- worker_report$collect(function() .lta_pool_phase(
    screen_tasks, costs, cores, nrow(grid)))
  ranked <- lapply(indices, function(i) {
    plan <- candidates[[i]]$value
    .latents_collect_conditions(function() tryCatch({
      if (inherits(plan, "error") || is.null(plan$screen)) NULL else
        .latents_rank_screened(lapply(screened[[i]], `[[`, "value"),
                                plan$n_starts, plan$screen)
    }, error = .lta_candidate_error))
  })
  final_tasks <- .lta_start_tasks(candidates, "final", screened, ranked)
  .latents_pool_progress(verbose, "Fitting %s on %s.",
                         .latents_count(length(final_tasks), "start"),
                         .latents_count(min(cores, max(1L, length(final_tasks))), "worker"))
  finished <- worker_report$collect(function() .lta_pool_phase(
    final_tasks, costs, cores, nrow(grid)))
  on.exit(.latents_pool_progress(verbose, "Done in %s.", .latents_format_duration(
    proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - started)), add = TRUE)
  runs <- lapply(indices, function(i) {
    plan <- candidates[[i]]$value
    final <- .latents_collect_conditions(function() tryCatch({
      if (inherits(plan, "error")) stop(plan)
      if (inherits(ranked[[i]]$value, "error")) stop(ranked[[i]]$value)
      attempts <- lapply(finished[[i]], `[[`, "value")
      found <- if (is.null(plan$screen)) {
        .latents_select_starts(attempts, plan$select_start)
      } else {
        .latents_select_screened(lapply(screened[[i]], `[[`, "value"),
                                  attempts, ranked[[i]]$value$finalists,
                                  ranked[[i]]$value$screened_scores,
                                  plan$select_start)
      }
      .lta_finish_plan(plan, found)
    }, error = function(error) {
      if (!inherits(plan, "error")) .lta_report_failed_plan(plan, error)
      .lta_candidate_error(error)
    }))
    conditions <- c(candidates[[i]]$conditions,
                    unlist(lapply(screened[[i]], `[[`, "conditions"), recursive = FALSE),
                    ranked[[i]]$conditions,
                    unlist(lapply(finished[[i]], `[[`, "conditions"), recursive = FALSE),
                    final$conditions)
    .latents_signal_conditions(conditions)
    warnings <- vapply(Filter(function(condition) inherits(condition, "warning"),
                               conditions), conditionMessage, character(1))
    failed <- inherits(final$value, "error")
    fit <- if (failed) NULL else final$value
    error_text <- if (failed) conditionMessage(final$value) else NA_character_
    entropy <- if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else
      .multilpa_relative_entropy(.multilpa_classified_posteriors(fit))
    row <- data.frame(
      n_profiles = grid$n_profiles[i], n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes[i],
      model = grid$model[i],
      log_likelihood = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else fit$log_likelihood,
      n_parameters = if (is.null(fit)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(fit$n_parameters),
      aic = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else fit$aic,
      bic = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else fit$bic,
      bic_individual = if (is.null(fit)) NA_real_ else fit$bic_individual,
      entropy = entropy,
      converged = !is.null(fit) && isTRUE(fit$converged),
      boundary = if (is.null(fit)) NA else isTRUE(fit$boundary),
      n_best_replicated = if (is.null(fit)) NA_integer_ else fit$n_best_replicated,
      warnings = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = "; "), error = error_text,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    list(fit = fit, row = row)
  })
  table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(runs, `[[`, "row"))
  rownames(table) <- NULL
  result <- structure(list(table = table, fits = lapply(runs, `[[`, "fit"),
                           call = call), class = "latents_transition_enumeration")
  names(result$fits) <- .latents_candidate_names(result)
  result
}

      entropy = entropy,
      converged = !is.null(fit) && isTRUE(fit$converged),
      boundary = if (is.null(fit)) NA else isTRUE(fit$boundary),
      n_best_replicated = if (is.null(fit)) NA_integer_ else fit$n_best_replicated,
      warnings = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = "; "), error = error_text,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    list(fit = fit, row = row)
  })
  table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(runs, `[[`, "row"))
  rownames(table) <- NULL
  result <- structure(list(table = table, fits = lapply(runs, `[[`, "fit"),
                           call = call), class = "latents_transition_enumeration")
  names(result$fits) <- .latents_candidate_names(result)
  result
}

before.documentation:
#' EM for the general transition model from one start
#'
#' `pause` and `resume` are as for `.latents_em()`; with either, the result
#' also carries the `checkpoint`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_em <- function(x, codes, layout, designs, parameters, occasion_of_row,
                    variance_model, min_variance, n_categories, min_probability,
                    max_iter, tol, covariance_model = "diagonal", structure = NULL,
                    sampling_weights = NULL, extra = NULL, pause = Inf,
                    resume = NULL, acceleration = "squarem") {
  # The inner logit Newton steps of the transition M-step leave more rounding
  # in the likelihood than a closed-form step, hence the looser guard.
  fit <- .latents_em(
    parameters,
    evaluate = function(point) {
      .lta_expectation(x, codes, layout, designs, point, occasion_of_row,
                       sampling_weights, extra)
    },
    maximize = function(point, expectation) {
      .lta_maximization(x, codes, layout, designs, expectation, point,
                        occasion_of_row, variance_model, min_variance,
                        n_categories, min_probability, covariance_model,
                        structure, extra)
    },
    max_iter = max_iter, tol = tol,
    settings = .latents_em_settings(
      decrease_tolerance = 1e-8, accelerate = .lta_accelerator(acceleration, general = TRUE)),
    pause = pause, resume = resume)
  result <- list(parameters = fit$state, expectation = fit$expectation,
                 converged = fit$converged, iterations = fit$iterations,
                 history = fit$history)
  if (!is.null(fit$checkpoint)) result$checkpoint <- fit$checkpoint
  result
}

before.name: .lta_initialize
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(x = , group_index = , layout = , designs = , n_profiles = , n_types = , variance_model = , min_variance = , start_index = , codes = , n_categories = , min_probability = , n_measurement = , order = 1L, mover_stayer = 0L, covariance_model = "diagonal", structure = NULL, extra = NULL, kind = "kmeans", row_weights = NULL))
before.documentation:
#' Starting values: the homogeneous initializer, converted to logit
#' coefficients with zero covariate effects
#' @param row_weights Optional sampling weights in observation order, as for
#'   `.multilpa_initialize()`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_initialize <- function(x, group_index, layout, designs, n_profiles, n_types,
                            variance_model, min_variance, start_index, codes,
                            n_categories, min_probability, n_measurement,
                            order = 1L, mover_stayer = 0L,
                            covariance_model = "diagonal", structure = NULL,
                            extra = NULL, kind = "kmeans", row_weights = NULL) {
  start <- .multilpa_transition_initialize(x, group_index, n_profiles, n_types,
                                           variance_model, min_variance, start_index,
                                           covariance_model, codes, n_categories,
                                           min_probability, extra, kind = kind,
                                           row_weights = row_weights)
  if (!is.null(structure)) {
    start <- .multilpa_project_start(start, structure, nrow(x), min_variance)
  }
  block <- start[intersect(c("means", "variances", "covariances",
                             "response_probabilities", "ordinal_intercepts",
                             "ordinal_locations", "count_means", "count_dispersion"),
                           names(start))]
  p0 <- ncol(designs$initial)
  p <- ncol(designs$transition[[1L]])
  initial <- array(0, c(p0, n_profiles - 1L, n_types))
  transition <- array(0, c(p, n_profiles - 1L, n_profiles, n_types),
                      dimnames = list(colnames(designs$transition[[1L]]), NULL, NULL, NULL))
  attr(transition, "n_occasion_intercepts") <- layout$n_occasions - 1L
  # Intercept columns carry the starting logits; covariate columns start at 0.
  intercepts_initial <- which(colnames(designs$initial) == "(Intercept)")
  intercepts_transition <- if (identical(colnames(designs$transition[[1L]])[1L],
                                        "(Intercept)")) 1L else
    seq_len(layout$n_occasions - 1L)
  invisible(lapply(seq_len(n_types), function(h) {
    shares <- start$initial_probabilities[h, ]
    initial[intercepts_initial, , h] <<- log(shares[-n_profiles] / shares[n_profiles])
    tp <- matrix(start$transition_probabilities[, , h], n_profiles)
    lapply(seq_len(n_profiles), function(k) {
      others <- setdiff(seq_len(n_profiles), k)
      logits <- log(tp[k, others] / tp[k, k])
      transition[intercepts_transition, , k, h] <<-
        matrix(logits, length(intercepts_transition), length(others), byrow = TRUE)
    })
  }))
  # Second order starts as the first-order chain: each origin pair (i, j)
  # takes the first-order logits of its current profile j.
  transition2 <- if (order < 2L) NULL else {
    array(vapply(seq_len(n_types), function(h) {
      vapply(seq_len(n_profiles^2), function(pair) {
        as.vector(transition[, , (pair - 1L) %% n_profiles + 1L, h])
      }, numeric(p * (n_profiles - 1L)))
    }, numeric(p * (n_profiles - 1L) * n_profiles^2)),
    c(p, n_profiles - 1L, n_profiles^2, n_types))
  }
  c(list(measurement = rep(list(block), n_measurement), initial = initial,
         transition = transition),
    if (order >= 2L) list(transition2 = transition2),
    list(group_probabilities = start$group_probabilities,
         stayer = c(rep(FALSE, n_types - mover_stayer), rep(TRUE, mover_stayer))))
}

before.documentation:
#' Prepare the general transition model
#'
#' Called by `lta()` when transitions vary by occasion or covariate, the
#' initial distribution depends on covariates, or measurement varies by
#' occasion.
#' @return A prepared start plan for the general transition engine.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(data, vars, id, time, n_profiles, n_group_classes, variance_model, n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance, seed, categorical, min_probability, occasions, transitions, transition_covariates, initial_covariates, measurement_model, select_start, call, order = 1L, mover_stayer = FALSE, missing = "error", covariance_model = "diagonal", structure = NULL, weights = NULL, ordinal = character(), count = character(), count_model = "poisson", count_dispersion = "varying", drop_empty = TRUE, search = "kmeans", 
    n_screen = NULL, acceleration = "squarem", cores = 1L) {
    n_movers <- as.integer(n_group_classes)
    n_group_classes <- n_movers + as.integer(mover_stayer)
    measurement <- .multilpa_prepare_indicators(data, vars, categorical, missing, min_probability, other = c(ordinal, count))
    extra <- .latents_set_count_model(.latents_prepare_extra(data, ordinal, count, missing), count_model, count_dispersion)
    x <- measurement$x
    codes <- measurement$codes
    n_categories <- measurement$n_categories
    time_values <- .multilpa_time_values(data, time, id, vars)
    groups <- .multilpa_prepare_groups(data[[id]])
    layout <- .multilpa_sequence_layout(groups$index, time_values, groups$n, occasions)
    if (layout$n_occasions < 2L) {
        stop(errorCondition("No group is observed at two occasions, so no transition can be estimated.", class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
    }
    if (order >= 2L && layout$n_occasions < 3L) {
        stop(errorCondition("Second-order transitions require at least three occasions.", class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
    }
    distinct_rows <- nrow(unique(cbind(x, codes, extra$ordinal, extra$count)))
    if (n_profiles > distinct_rows || n_group_classes > groups$n) {
        stop(errorCondition(paste("Profiles cannot exceed the distinct observed indicator rows, and group", "classes (including stayers) cannot exceed the number of groups."), class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
    }
    .lta_check_covariate_gaps(layout, groups, time_values, transition_covariates)

#' Finalise a general transition fit from its selected starts
#' @param starts The shared start-selection result.
#' @param context Forced setup inputs.
#' @return A fitted multilpa_lta object.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(starts, context) {
    with(context, {
        found <- starts
        attempts <- starts$attempts
        valid <- starts$valid
        scores <- starts$scores
        converged <- starts$converged
        best_start <- starts$best_start
        best <- attempts[[best_start]]
        weighted_expectation <- best$expectation
        if (!is.null(sampling_weights)) {
            best$expectation <- .lta_expectation(x, codes, layout, designs, best$parameters, occasion_of_row, extra = extra)
            best$expectation$log_likelihood <- weighted_expectation$log_likelihood
        }
        result <- .lta_result(best, attempts, scores, valid, converged, best_start, centers, data, vars, id, time, groups, layout, designs, x, codes, measurement, occasion_of_row, n_profiles, n_group_classes, variance_model, transitions, transition_covariates, initial_covariates, measurement_model, min_variance, min_probability, call, order, mover_stayer, missing, covariance_model, structure, final_stage = .latents_final_stage(found))
        result$starts <- .latents_search_columns(result$starts, found, n_starts)
        record <- .latents_search_record(search, n_starts, screen, select_start, "allow")
        result[names(record)] <- record
        result$max_iter <- as.integer(max_iter)
        result$tol <- tol
        result$arguments$search <- search
        result$arguments$n_screen <- n_screen
        result$acceleration <- acceleration
        result$arguments$acceleration <- acceleration
        if (!is.null(sampling_weights)) {
            result$weights <- weights
            result$sampling_weights <- stats::setNames(sampling_weights, groups$ids)
            result$arguments$weights <- weights
        }
        result$ordinal <- ordinal
        result$count <- count
        result$arguments$ordinal <- ordinal
        result$arguments$count <- count
        result$arguments$count_model <- count_model
        result$arguments$count_dispersion <- count_dispersion
        if (!is.null(extra)) {
            result$extra_data <- extra
            profile_names <- paste0("profile_", seq_len(n_profiles))
            result$measurement <- lapply(result$measurement, .latents_label_extra, extra = extra, profile_names = profile_names)
            result$n_parameters <- result$n_parameters + n_measurement * .latents_extra_n_parameters(extra, n_profiles)
            result$aic <- -2 * result$log_likelihood + 2 * result$n_parameters
            result$informative <- result$informative | rowSums(!is.na(.latents_extra_matrix(extra))) > 0L
            result$n_informative <- sum(result$informative)
            result$n_informative_groups <- length(unique(groups$index[result$informative]))
            result$bic <- -2 * result$log_likelihood + log(result$n_informative_groups) * result$n_parameters
            result$bic_individual <- -2 * result$log_likelihood + log(result$n_informative) * result$n_parameters
            .latents_warn_poisson_limit(do.call(cbind, lapply(result$measurement, `[[`, "count_dispersion")))
        }
        result$drop_empty <- drop_empty
        result$arguments$drop_empty <- drop_empty
        if (isFALSE(drop_empty)) {
            result$n_informative <- result$n_observations
            result$bic <- -2 * result$log_likelihood + log(groups$n) * result$n_parameters
            result$bic_individual <- -2 * result$log_likelihood + log(result$n_observations) * result$n_parameters
        }
        gaussian_rows <- rowSums(!is.na(x)) > 0L
        profile_parameters <- .latents_profile_parameters(length(measurement$continuous), variance_model, covariance_model, structure)
        invisible(lapply(seq_len(n_measurement), function(index) {
            rows <- gaussian_rows & (n_measurement == 1L | occasion_of_row == index)
            .latents_warn_thin_profiles(colSums(weighted_expectation$subject_posteriors[rows, , drop = FALSE]), profile_parameters, context = if (n_measurement > 1L) sprintf("at occasion %s", index) else NULL)
        }))
        result$gaussian_diagnostics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_measurement), function(index) {
            rows <- n_measurement == 1L | occasion_of_row == index
            .latents_gaussian_diagnostics(result$measurement[[index]], x[rows, , drop = FALSE], result$subject_posteriors[rows, , drop = FALSE], weights = if (is.null(sampling_weights)) 
                NULL
            else sampling_weights[groups$index[rows]], min_variance = min_variance, context = if (n_measurement == 1L) 
                "profiles"
            else sprintf("occasion %s", index))
        }))

    })

#' Free parameters of the general transition model
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_count_parameters <- function(n_profiles, n_types, d, n_categories,
                                  variance_model, n_measurement, p0, p, order = 1L,
                                  n_stayers = 0L, covariance_model = "diagonal",
                                  structure = NULL, p_second = p) {
  n_movers <- n_types - n_stayers
  # One measurement block as the cross-sectional counter counts it, without
  # its group-class and profile-share terms (one class: K - 1 shares).
  per_measurement <- .multilpa_count_parameters(
    n_profiles, 1L, d, n_categories, variance_model, covariance_model, structure) -
    (n_profiles - 1L)
  as.integer(n_measurement * per_measurement + (n_types - 1L) +
               n_types * p0 * (n_profiles - 1L) +
               n_movers * p * (n_profiles - 1L) * n_profiles +
               if (order >= 2L) n_movers * p_second * (n_profiles - 1L) * n_profiles^2 else 0L)
}

  # One measurement block as the cross-sectional counter counts it, without
  # its group-class and profile-share terms (one class: K - 1 shares).

    n_profiles, 1L, d, n_categories, variance_model, covariance_model, structure) -
    (n_profiles - 1L)
  as.integer(n_measurement * per_measurement + (n_types - 1L) +
               n_types * p0 * (n_profiles - 1L) +
               n_movers * p * (n_profiles - 1L) * n_profiles +
               if (order >= 2L) n_movers * p_second * (n_profiles - 1L) * n_profiles^2 else 0L)
}
