before.source:
.gg_view_enumeration <- function(x, criteria, labels, mark_minimum, main,
                                 subtitle) {
  grid <- .latents_grid_table(x)
  views <- .latents_grid_views(x)
  # A grid over group classes at one number of profiles would stack every
  # candidate in one column; the group classes then go on the x-axis, as they
  # always do for a family grid, whose candidates have no profiles.
  on_group_axis <- identical(views$axis, "n_group_classes")
  by_classes <- on_group_axis || (length(unique(grid$n_profiles)) == 1L &&
    length(unique(grid$n_group_classes)) > 1L)
  # A profile or class grid keeps the axis words it has always had.
  count_word <- if (identical(views$kind, "profiles")) "profiles" else views$word
  long <- .gg_enumeration_frame(grid, criteria, by_classes)
  long$title <- factor(long$title, levels = names(criteria))
  series_levels <- unique(long$series[order(grid$n_group_classes, grid$model)])
  long$series <- factor(long$series, levels = series_levels)
  ok <- long[long$eligible, , drop = FALSE]
  # A failed candidate is marked on its panel's floor, so a gap in a line reads
  # as a failure and not as a candidate that was never fitted.
  floors <- tapply(ok$value, ok$title, \(v) min(v) - 0.08 * max(diff(range(v)),
                                                                1e-8))
  failed <- long[!long$eligible, , drop = FALSE]
  failed$failed_y <- floors[as.character(failed$title)]
  minimum <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ok, ok$title, drop = TRUE),
                                   \(panel) panel[which.min(panel$value), ]))
  ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ok, list(ok$title, ok$series),
                                      drop = TRUE),
                                \(s) s[which.max(s$n_profiles), ]))
  ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ends, ends$title, drop = TRUE), \(p) {
    span <- diff(range(ok$value[ok$title == p$title[1L]]))
    p$y <- .gg_spread(p$value, gap = 0.1 * max(span, 1e-8))
    p
  }))
  ends$x <- max(ok$n_profiles) + 0.28
  n_series <- nlevels(long$series)
  colours <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_okabe_ito, n_series), series_levels)
  shapes <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_shapes, n_series), series_levels)
  # Direct labels while they fit beside the lines; past five series they
  # collide, and a legend keeps every series identifiable. They sit past the
  # end of each line, which only a single panel has room for: beside a second
  # panel they run off the edge and repeat in every panel, so several panels
  # share one legend, keyed by colour and shape.
  labelled <- isTRUE(labels) && n_series > 1L && n_series <= 5L &&
    length(criteria) == 1L
  legend <- n_series > 1L && !labelled
  guide <- if (legend) "legend" else "none"
  failures <- sum(!grid$converged)
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(ok, ggplot2::aes(n_profiles, value, colour = series,
                                           group = series)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape = series, fill = series),
                        size = 2.3, colour = "white", stroke = 0.6)
  if (nrow(failed) > 0L) {
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = failed, ggplot2::aes(x = n_profiles, y = failed_y,
                                  colour = series),
      shape = 4, size = 2.6, stroke = 1.1, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  if (isTRUE(mark_minimum)) {
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = minimum, ggplot2::aes(x = n_profiles, y = value), shape = 21,
      size = 5.2, stroke = 0.8, colour = "grey10", fill = NA,
      inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  if (labelled) {
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = ends, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = series, colour = series),
      hjust = 0, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  several <- length(criteria) > 1L
  plot +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(title), scales = "free_y",
                        nrow = if (length(criteria) <= 3L) 1L else NULL,
                        ncol = if (length(criteria) > 3L) 2L else NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = sort(unique(long$n_profiles)),
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(0.3, if (labelled) 1.1 else 0.3))) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = colours, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = shapes, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    .gg_titles(main, subtitle,
               if (several) "Information criteria by candidate model" else
                 sprintf("%s by candidate model", names(criteria)),
               sprintf(paste("%d candidates%s; lower is preferred%s;",
                             "no candidate is selected automatically"),
                       nrow(grid),
                       if (failures == 0L) "" else
                         sprintf(", %d did not converge (x)", failures),
                       if (isTRUE(mark_minimum)) ", ring = lowest" else "")) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = if (on_group_axis) "Number of group classes" else
                    if (by_classes) {
                      sprintf("Number of group classes (%d %s)",
                              grid$n_profiles[[1L]], count_word)
                    } else sprintf("Number of %s", count_word),
                  y = if (several) NULL else names(criteria)) +
    .gg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.spacing = ggplot2::unit(1.6, "lines"),
                   strip.text = if (several) ggplot2::element_text(
                     face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = ggplot2::rel(0.95)) else
                     ggplot2::element_blank(),
                   legend.position = if (legend) "bottom" else "none",
                   legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank())
}

.gg_view_enumeration <- function(x, criteria, labels, mark_minimum, main,
                                 subtitle) {
  grid <- .latents_grid_table(x)
  views <- .latents_grid_views(x)
  # A grid over group classes at one number of profiles would stack every
  # candidate in one column; the group classes then go on the x-axis, as they
  # always do for a family grid, whose candidates have no profiles.
  on_group_axis <- identical(views$axis, "n_group_classes")
  by_classes <- on_group_axis || (length(unique(grid$n_profiles)) == 1L &&
    length(unique(grid$n_group_classes)) > 1L)
  # A profile or class grid keeps the axis words it has always had.
  count_word <- if (identical(views$kind, "profiles")) "profiles" else views$word
  long <- .gg_enumeration_frame(grid, criteria, by_classes)
  long$title <- factor(long$title, levels = names(criteria))
  series_levels <- unique(long$series[order(grid$n_group_classes, grid$model)])
  long$series <- factor(long$series, levels = series_levels)
  ok <- long[long$eligible, , drop = FALSE]
  # A failed candidate is marked on its panel's floor, so a gap in a line reads
  # as a failure and not as a candidate that was never fitted.
  floors <- tapply(ok$value, ok$title, \(v) min(v) - 0.08 * max(diff(range(v)),
                                                                1e-8))
  failed <- long[!long$eligible, , drop = FALSE]
  failed$failed_y <- floors[as.character(failed$title)]
  minimum <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ok, ok$title, drop = TRUE),
                                   \(panel) panel[which.min(panel$value), ]))
  ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ok, list(ok$title, ok$series),
                                      drop = TRUE),
                                \(s) s[which.max(s$n_profiles), ]))
  ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ends, ends$title, drop = TRUE), \(p) {
    span <- diff(range(ok$value[ok$title == p$title[1L]]))
    p$y <- .gg_spread(p$value, gap = 0.1 * max(span, 1e-8))
    p
  }))
  ends$x <- max(ok$n_profiles) + 0.28
  n_series <- nlevels(long$series)
  colours <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_okabe_ito, n_series), series_levels)
  shapes <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_shapes, n_series), series_levels)
  # Direct labels while they fit beside the lines; past five series they
  # collide, and a legend keeps every series identifiable. They sit past the
  # end of each line, which only a single panel has room for: beside a second
  # panel they run off the edge and repeat in every panel, so several panels
  # share one legend, keyed by colour and shape.
  labelled <- isTRUE(labels) && n_series > 1L && n_series <= 5L &&
    length(criteria) == 1L
  legend <- n_series > 1L && !labelled
  guide <- if (legend) "legend" else "none"
  failures <- sum(!grid$converged)
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(ok, ggplot2::aes(n_profiles, value, colour = series,
                                           group = series)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape = series, fill = series),
                        size = 2.3, colour = "white", stroke = 0.6)
  if (nrow(failed) > 0L) {
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = failed, ggplot2::aes(x = n_profiles, y = failed_y,
                                  colour = series),
      shape = 4, size = 2.6, stroke = 1.1, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  if (isTRUE(mark_minimum)) {
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = minimum, ggplot2::aes(x = n_profiles, y = value), shape = 21,
      size = 5.2, stroke = 0.8, colour = "grey10", fill = NA,
      inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  if (labelled) {
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = ends, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = series, colour = series),
      hjust = 0, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  several <- length(criteria) > 1L
  plot +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(title), scales = "free_y",
                        nrow = if (length(criteria) <= 3L) 1L else NULL,
                        ncol = if (length(criteria) > 3L) 2L else NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = sort(unique(long$n_profiles)),
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(0.3, if (labelled) 1.1 else 0.3))) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = colours, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = shapes, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    .gg_titles(main, subtitle,
               if (several) "Information criteria by candidate model" else
                 sprintf("%s by candidate model", names(criteria)),
               sprintf(paste("%d candidates%s; lower is preferred%s;",
                             "no candidate is selected automatically"),
                       nrow(grid),
                       if (failures == 0L) "" else
                         sprintf(", %d did not converge (x)", failures),
                       if (isTRUE(mark_minimum)) ", ring = lowest" else "")) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = if (on_group_axis) "Number of group classes" else
                    if (by_classes) {
                      sprintf("Number of group classes (%d %s)",
                              grid$n_profiles[[1L]], count_word)
                    } else sprintf("Number of %s", count_word),
                  y = if (several) NULL else names(criteria)) +
    .gg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.spacing = ggplot2::unit(1.6, "lines"),
                   strip.text = if (several) ggplot2::element_text(
                     face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = ggplot2::rel(0.95)) else
                     ggplot2::element_blank(),
                   legend.position = if (legend) "bottom" else "none",
                   legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank())
}

.gg_view_enumeration_quality <- function(x, measures, labels, main, subtitle,
                                         cutoff) {
  grid <- .latents_grid_quality_table(x, cutoff)
  views <- .latents_grid_views(x)
  # A family grid's candidates differ in group classes only, so they go on
  # the x-axis.
  by_classes <- identical(views$axis, "n_group_classes")
  columns <- c(
    if ("entropy" %in% measures) c("Entropy, individuals" = "profile_entropy",
                                   "Entropy, groups" = "group_entropy"),
    if ("avepp" %in% measures) c("Lowest AvePP, individuals" = "avepp_min",
                                 "Lowest AvePP, groups" = "group_avepp_min"))
  present <- columns[vapply(columns, function(column) {
    any(grid$converged %in% TRUE & is.finite(grid[[column]]))
  }, logical(1))]
  if (length(present) == 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "No converged candidate has two or more classes, so there is no entropy",
      "or AvePP to plot."), class = "latents_nothing_to_plot", call = NULL))
  }
  # With no group level the panels are simply "Entropy" and "Lowest AvePP".
  if (!any(grepl("groups$", names(present)))) {
    names(present) <- sub(", individuals$", "", names(present))
  }
  long <- .gg_enumeration_frame(grid, present, by_classes)
  long$title <- factor(long$title, levels = names(present))
  series_levels <- unique(long$series[order(grid$n_group_classes, grid$model)])
  long$series <- factor(long$series, levels = series_levels)
  ok <- long[long$eligible, , drop = FALSE]
  n_series <- nlevels(long$series)
  colours <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_okabe_ito, n_series), series_levels)
  shapes <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_shapes, n_series), series_levels)
  # As in the criteria view: direct labels fit beside a single panel only.
  labelled <- isTRUE(labels) && n_series > 1L && n_series <= 5L &&
    length(present) == 1L
  legend <- n_series > 1L && !labelled
  guide <- if (legend) "legend" else "none"
  avepp_panels <- grep("AvePP", names(present), value = TRUE)
  reference <- data.frame(title = factor(avepp_panels, levels = names(present)),
                          y = rep(cutoff, length(avepp_panels)))
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(ok, ggplot2::aes(n_profiles, value, colour = series,
                                           group = series)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(shape = series, fill = series),
                        size = 2.3, colour = "white", stroke = 0.6)
  if (nrow(reference) > 0L) {
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_hline(
      data = reference, ggplot2::aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed",
      colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.5)
  }
  if (labelled) {
    ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ok, list(ok$title, ok$series),
                                        drop = TRUE),
                                  \(s) s[which.max(s$n_profiles), ]))
    ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ends, ends$title, drop = TRUE), \(p) {
      span <- diff(range(ok$value[ok$title == p$title[1L]], cutoff))
      p$y <- .gg_spread(p$value, gap = 0.1 * max(span, 1e-8))
      p
    }))
    ends$x <- max(ok$n_profiles) + 0.28
    plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = ends, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, label = series, colour = series),
      hjust = 0, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE)
  }
  failures <- sum(!grid$converged)
  plot +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(title), scales = "free_y",
                        ncol = if (length(present) > 2L) 2L else NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = sort(unique(grid[[views$axis]])),
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(0.3, if (labelled) 1.1 else 0.3))) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = colours, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = shapes, guide = guide) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    .gg_titles(main, subtitle, "Classification quality by candidate model",
               sprintf("%d candidates%s; higher is sharper%s", nrow(grid),
                       if (failures == 0L) "" else
                         sprintf(", %d did not converge", failures),
                       if (nrow(reference) == 0L) "" else
                         sprintf("; dashed line: AvePP %s", format(cutoff)))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = sprintf("Number of %s", views$word), y = NULL) +
    .gg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.spacing = ggplot2::unit(1.6, "lines"),
                   strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(
                     face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = ggplot2::rel(0.95)),
                   legend.position = if (legend) "bottom" else "none",
                   legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank())
}

#' Draw one view of a fit through its own plot method
#'
#' The named plot functions list their arguments so an editor completes them;
#' the drawing stays in the fit's `plot()` method, so a named function and
#' `plot(fit, what = )` cannot draw different things. Only the arguments the
#' caller supplied are passed on, so each method's own defaults apply. An
#' argument the fit's method does not take is refused by name rather than
#' dropped.
#'
#' @param x A fitted model.
#' @param view The `what =` value to draw, or `NA` for a method that draws a
#'   single view and takes no `what`.
#' @param arguments Named list of the arguments the caller supplied.
#' @param verb The calling function's name, for messages.
#' @param what The named function's own `what` (`""` for a function without
#'   one), for messages.
#' @return The method's ggplot object.
#' @noRd
before.terminal_expression: do.call(method, c(list(x), if (!is.na(view)) list(what = view), arguments))

before.documentation:
#' Which view of a fit's own plot() each named plot function draws
#'
#' The one table behind the named fit plot functions. Each row says that the
#' named function `verb`, given `what`, draws `plot(x, what = view)` for a
#' fit of that `kind` (see `.latents_plot_kind()`). A function, kind and
#' `what` with no row are refused with `.latents_refuse_named_plot()`; a
#' mapping is listed only where the view shows the same quantity, so most
#' kinds map few functions. Profile, class and transition models draw
#' `plot_diagnostics()` from their posteriors at both levels in that function
#' itself, so they have no `plot_diagnostics` rows.
#' @return A `data.frame`, one row per mapped function, kind and `what`:
#'   `kind`, `verb`, `what` (`""` for a function without `what`) and `view`
#'   (the plot() view; `NA` when that plot() draws a single view and takes no
#'   `what`).
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_named_plot_registry <- function() {
  rows <- function(kind, verb, what, view) {
    data.frame(kind = kind, verb = verb, what = what, view = view,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  regressions <- c("growth_mixture", "trajectory_regression",
                   "mixture_regression")
  rbind(
    rows("profile_model", "plot_profiles",
         c("lines", "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel", "pairs"),
         c("profiles", "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel", "pairs")),
    rows("profile_model", c("plot_responses", "plot_sequences",
                            "plot_prevalence", "plot_transitions"), "",
         c("responses", "sequences", "probabilities", "transitions")),
    # The class's curve of the outcome: over time for trajectories, over the
    # first numeric predictor for a regression of observations.
    rows(regressions, "plot_profiles", "lines",
         c("trajectories", "trajectories", "fitted")),
    # Each unit's posterior probability of its most likely class.
    rows(regressions, "plot_diagnostics", "posteriors", "posteriors"),
    rows("group_class_family", "plot_profiles", "lines", "means"),
    rows("cross_level", c("plot_profiles", "plot_prevalence"), c("lines", ""),
         c("profiles", "composition")),
    # The pooled profile means and variances ("measurement"), and the pooled
    # probability of each profile within each group class ("profile"): the
    # prevalence that plot_prevalence() draws for a profile model.
    rows("pooled", c("plot_profiles", "plot_prevalence"), c("lines", ""),
         c("measurement", "profile")),
    rows("general_transitions", "plot_transitions", "", NA_character_))
}

.latents_refuse_named_plot.name: .latents_refuse_named_plot

before.name: .latents_refuse_named_plot
before.documentation:
#' Refuse a named plot function a fit has no view for, naming its views
#'
#' The message lists the views of the fit's own plot() and, for the model
#' kinds other than profile, class and transition models, which named
#' functions draw them.
#' @param x A fitted model.
#' @param verb The named function.
#' @param what Its `what` (`""` for a function without one, `"all"` when no
#'   view of the function is mapped).
#' @return Does not return; raises `latents_nothing_to_plot` (also of class
#'   `latents_bad_argument`, which these refusals had before).
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_refuse_named_plot <- function(x, verb, what = "") {
  asked <- function(verb, what) {
    ifelse(nzchar(what), sprintf("%s(what = \"%s\")", verb, what),
           sprintf("%s()", verb))
  }
  offered <- .latents_plot_offered_views(x)
  offered_text <- if (length(offered) == 0L) "its plot() draws a single view" else
    sprintf("its plot() offers %s",
            paste(sprintf("\"%s\"", offered), collapse = ", "))
  kind <- .latents_plot_kind(x)
  registry <- .latents_named_plot_registry()
  mapped <- if (identical(kind, "profile_model")) registry[0L, ] else
    registry[registry$kind %in% kind, , drop = FALSE]
  named_text <- if (nrow(mapped) == 0L) "" else
    sprintf("; of the named plot functions, %s", paste(
      sprintf("%s draws %s", asked(mapped$verb, mapped$what),
              ifelse(is.na(mapped$view), "it", sprintf("\"%s\"", mapped$view))),
      collapse = " and "))
  stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
    "%s has no view of a `%s` fit: %s%s.", asked(verb, what), class(x)[1L],
    offered_text, named_text),
    class = c("latents_nothing_to_plot", "latents_bad_argument"), call = NULL))
}
before.terminal_expression: stop(errorCondition(sprintf("%s has no view of a `%s` fit: %s%s.", asked(verb, what), class(x)[1L], offered_text, named_text), class = c("latents_nothing_to_plot", "latents_bad_argument"), call = NULL))

    paste("Style the returned plot with ggplot2, for example",
          "`+ ggplot2::theme()` or `+ ggplot2::scale_colour_manual()`."))
  stopifnot(
    "`labels` must be TRUE or FALSE" = isTRUE(labels) || isFALSE(labels),
    "`intervals` must be TRUE or FALSE" =

    "`cell_labels` must be TRUE or FALSE" =

  invisible(NULL)
}

#' @rdname latents-plots
#' @export
before.source:
plot.multilpa_enumeration <- function(x, what = c("enumeration", "tree"),
                                      criterion = c("aic", "bic_groups",
                                                    "bic_individual",
                                                    "icl_individual"),
                                      combine = TRUE, labels = TRUE,
                                      mark_minimum = TRUE, main = NULL,
                                      subtitle = NULL, ..., cutoff = 0.8,
                                      using = "bic_groups") {
  stopifnot("`x` must be an `multilpa_enumeration` result" =
              inherits(x, "multilpa_enumeration"))
  # The released view names were matched with match.arg(), so their unique
  # abbreviations remain valid alongside the new criterion names.
  if (is.null(what) || identical(what, c("enumeration", "tree"))) {
    what <- "enumeration"
  }
  legacy <- if (is.character(what) && length(what) == 1L && !is.na(what)) {
    pmatch(what, c("enumeration", "tree"))
  } else NA_integer_
  if (!is.na(legacy)) what <- c("enumeration", "tree")[legacy]
  if (identical(what, "tree")) {
    # The tree takes its own arguments; any other is refused by name.
    tree_arguments <- list(...)
    .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
      tree_arguments[setdiff(names(tree_arguments), .latents_tree_arguments())],
      "plot(what = \"tree\")", paste(
        "The tree takes `n_group_classes`, `n_profiles`, `model`, `candidates`,",
        "`from`, `to`, `level`, `combine`, `main` and `subtitle`."))
    # In 0.9.21 `criterion` always had a value and the tree did not use it.
    .latents_warn_unused_arguments(
      if (missing(criterion) || is.null(criterion)) list() else
        list(criterion = criterion),
      "plot(what = \"tree\")", "The tree shows no criterion.")
    return(do.call(plot_tree, c(list(x), tree_arguments,
                                list(combine = if (missing(combine)) FALSE else combine,
                                     main = main, subtitle = subtitle))))
  }
  .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
    list(...), "plot()", .multilpa_enumeration_plot_advice())
  # 0.9.21 chose the view with `what = "enumeration"` and the criteria with
  # `criterion`; both spellings still draw the same plot.
  what <- .latents_former_argument(
    what, !missing(what) && !identical(what, "enumeration"),
    if (missing(criterion)) NULL else criterion,
    c("what", "criterion"))
  if ("tree" %in% what) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "`what = \"tree\"` draws the tree on its own; ask for criteria separately.",
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  # The view's name before criteria were chosen through `what`.
  if (identical(what, "enumeration")) what <- eval(formals(plot_enumeration)$what)
  plot_enumeration(x, what = what, combine = combine, labels = labels,
                   mark_minimum = mark_minimum, main = main,
                   subtitle = subtitle, cutoff = cutoff, using = using)
}

.multilpa_distinct_criteria.name: .multilpa_distinct_criteria

before.name: .multilpa_distinct_criteria
before.documentation:
#' The criteria worth a panel, named for display
#'
#' A single-level grid has one unit per observation, so every criterion's
#' group-level and individual-level versions are the same numbers; drawing both
#' repeats a panel. Such a pair is kept once under the criterion's plain name.
#' A grid whose every candidate has one group class classifies nothing at the
#' group level, so the group version of a classification criterion (AWE, ICL,
#' CLC) is its penalty alone, and ICL over groups equals BIC over groups. When
#' both versions are asked for, only the individual one is kept, under the
#' criterion's plain name.
#' @param grid The enumeration table.
#' @param criterion Requested criterion columns.
#' @return The criteria to draw, named by their display titles.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_distinct_criteria <- function(grid, criterion) {
  classification <- c("awe", "icl", "clc")
  # An empty table (titles alone) has no candidates to judge.
  no_group_classes <- nrow(grid) > 0L && !is.null(grid$n_group_classes) &&
    all(grid$n_group_classes %in% 1L)
  if (no_group_classes) {
    stems <- sub("_groups$", "", criterion)
    redundant <- grepl("_groups$", criterion) & stems %in% classification &
      paste0(stems, "_individual") %in% criterion
    criterion <- criterion[!redundant]
  }
  base <- sub("_(groups|individual)$", "", criterion)
  level <- ifelse(grepl("_groups$", criterion), "groups",
                  ifelse(grepl("_individual$", criterion), "individuals", ""))
  same_at_both <- vapply(base, function(stem) {
    both <- paste0(stem, c("_groups", "_individual"))
    all(both %in% names(grid)) &&
      isTRUE(all.equal(grid[[both[1L]]], grid[[both[2L]]]))
  }, logical(1))
  plain <- same_at_both | !nzchar(level) |
    (no_group_classes & base %in% classification & level == "individuals")
  keep <- !duplicated(ifelse(same_at_both, base, criterion))
  titles <- ifelse(plain, toupper(base), sprintf("%s (%s)", toupper(base), level))
  stats::setNames(criterion[keep], titles[keep])
}

#' @export
before.source:
plot.multilpa_covariates <- function(x, what = c("profiles", "bars", "heatmap",
                                                 "raincloud", "parallel",
                                                 "pairs", "responses",
                                                 "sequences", "sizes",
                                                 "entropy", "posteriors",
                                                 "avepp", "all"),
                                     data = NULL,
                                     scale = c("raw", "standardized"),
                                     category = "last", labels = TRUE,
                                     intervals = TRUE, cell_labels = TRUE,
                                     main = NULL, subtitle = NULL,
                                     ..., statistic = c("mean", "median", "mode")) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted `multilpa_covariates` model" =
              inherits(x, "multilpa_covariates"))
  .multilpa_check_plot_arguments(list(...), labels, intervals, cell_labels,
                                 category)
  # Asked for by name or by a unique abbreviation, as match.arg() would take
  # it, so "prob" gets the reason too rather than a bare match.arg() error.
  offered <- c(eval(formals(plot.multilpa_covariates)$what), "probabilities")
  asks_prevalence <- is.character(what) && length(what) == 1L && !is.na(what) &&
    identical(offered[pmatch(what, offered)], "probabilities")
  if (asks_prevalence) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      paste("A covariate model has no single profile prevalence: it varies with",
            "each unit's covariates. Use parameter_inference() for the logits."),
      class = "latents_nothing_to_plot", call = NULL))
  }
  what <- match.arg(what)
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  statistic <- match.arg(statistic)
  .multilpa_check_plot_statistic(what, statistic)
  .gg_require()
  if (identical(what, "all")) {
    return(.gg_every_view(x, match.call(), parent.frame()))
  }
  .multilpa_draw_view(x, what, data = data, scale = scale,
                      category = category, labels = labels,
                      intervals = intervals, cell_labels = cell_labels,
                      main = main, subtitle = subtitle, statistic = statistic)
}

.multilpa_mean_error_matrix.name: .multilpa_mean_error_matrix

before.name: .multilpa_mean_error_matrix
before.documentation:
#' Measurement standard errors shaped like the means matrix
#'
#' @param x A fitted model.
#' @param data The data frame the model was fitted to, or `NULL` to use the
#'   columns the fit carries.
#' @return A profiles-by-indicators matrix of standard errors; or a single
#'   string saying why there are none, for the plot's subtitle.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_mean_error_matrix <- function(x, data) {
  # A fit carries the columns it was built from, so the intervals cost the
  # caller nothing to ask for and are drawn by default. Families whose standard
  # errors are not implemented refuse by condition class; the means are still
  # worth drawing without whiskers, so the refusal is caught and reported as
  # a reason rather than propagated out of a plot call. The reason travels to
  # the subtitle, so a plot without whiskers says why.
  because <- function(reason) function(condition) reason
  errors <- tryCatch(
    .multilpa_measurement_errors(x, .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data)),
    latents_unsupported_inference = because("no intervals for this model"),
    latents_unsupported_noise = because("no intervals with a noise component"),
    latents_singular_information = because("no intervals: singular information"),
    latents_incomplete_fit = because("no intervals: incomplete fit"),
    latents_bad_inference_data = because("no intervals: data do not reproduce the fit"),
    latents_boundary_fit = because("no intervals: an estimate is at its bound"),
    latents_no_converge = because("no intervals: the fit did not converge"))
  if (is.character(errors)) return(errors)
  vars <- .multilpa_continuous_names(x)
  cells <- expand.grid(indicator = vars, profile = seq_len(x$n_profiles),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  values <- .multilpa_match_error(errors, "mean", cells$profile, cells$indicator)
  if (all(is.na(values))) return("no intervals for this model")
  matrix(values, x$n_profiles, length(vars), byrow = TRUE)
}

before.name: .multilpa_response_error_table
before.documentation:
#' Response-probability standard errors for the responses plot
#' @param x A fitted model.
#' @param data The fitting data, or `NULL` for the columns the fit carries.
#' @return The measurement rows of the inference table; or a string saying
#'   why there are none.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_response_error_table <- function(x, data) {
  because <- function(reason) function(condition) reason
  # Probabilities on their bound are held there, so every other one keeps its
  # interval instead of one bound-active probability removing them all.
  tryCatch(
    {
      inference <- parameter_inference(x, .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data),
                                       boundary = "fix")
      inference <- inference[inference$level == "measurement", , drop = FALSE]
      attr(inference, "held") <- length(attr(inference, "fixed_at_bound") %||%
                                          character()) > 0L
      inference
    },
    latents_unsupported_inference = because("no intervals for this model"),
    latents_unsupported_noise = because("no intervals with a noise component"),
    latents_singular_information = because("no intervals: singular information"),
    latents_incomplete_fit = because("no intervals: incomplete fit"),
    latents_bad_inference_data = because("no intervals: data do not reproduce the fit"),
    latents_boundary_fit = because("no intervals: a probability is at its bound"),
    latents_no_converge = because("no intervals: the fit did not converge"))
}

pool_imputations.name: pool_imputations

before.name: pool_imputations
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(imputed = , vars = , id = , n_profiles = , ... = , level = 0.95, vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg"), adjust = .multilpa_p_adjust_methods))
before.documentation:
#' Fit a model to multiply imputed data and pool it with Rubin's rules
#'
#' Fits [multilpa()] to every completed data set, aligns each fit's profile and
#' group-class labels to those of the first, and pools the estimates with
#' Rubin's rules, returning a `latents_pooled` object. Use it for missing
#' covariates, which `missing = "fiml"` cannot handle because the model
#' conditions on covariates. Impute them first (for example with the mice
#' package, with the indicators and the group identifier in the imputation
#' model) and pass the completed data.
#'
#' Pooling is on the reported (natural) scale: the pooled estimate is the mean
#' over imputations, and its variance is the mean within-imputation variance
#' plus `(1 + 1/m)` times the between-imputation variance. Degrees of freedom
#' follow Rubin (1987) with a large complete-data sample. Pooled intervals are
#' symmetric t intervals on this scale, so for probabilities and variances
#' they can extend outside the parameter space, unlike the transformed Wald
#' intervals of [parameter_inference()]. A structural constant, such as the
#' probability of one for a single class, has zero within- and
#' between-imputation variance and zero missing information. When the
#' within-imputation variance is zero and the between-imputation variance is
#' positive, `riv` is infinite and `fmi` is one.
#'
#' @section Choosing the imputation model:
#' The pooled results are only as valid as the imputations. The covariate and
#' the indicators are related through the latent classes, which an imputation
#' model linear in the indicators (mice's defaults) does not capture. In
#' `validation/pool-imputations-coverage.R` (a membership slope with 30% of
#' its covariate missing at random given the indicators, 200 replications,
#' ten imputations), 95% intervals covered 0.925 under predictive mean
#' matching and 0.935 under Bayesian linear regression, and 0.995 when the
#' covariate was drawn approximately from its conditional distribution given
#' the known generating parameters. That reference arm omits uncertainty in
#' the imputation parameters, so it does not validate proper multiple
#' imputation, and the study covers one design only. The imputation model
#' should account for the latent structure and the clustering, include the
#' indicators and relevant nonlinearities, and propagate parameter
#' uncertainty; imputing separately within assigned classes ignores
#' classification uncertainty. Complete-case analysis covered 0.955 in that
#' design, but selecting on the indicators changes their within-class
#' distributions, and the case-control argument for unbiased logistic slopes
#' does not carry over when the outcome is latent and its measurement model
#' is estimated.
#'
#' @param imputed The completed data sets: a list of at least two data frames
#'   with the same columns and rows in the same order, or a `mids` object from
#'   the mice package, which is completed here.
#' @param vars,id,n_profiles As in [multilpa()].
#' @param ... Further arguments for [multilpa()], such as `n_group_classes`,
#'   `profile_covariates`, `group_covariates`, `categorical`, `n_starts` and
#'   `seed`, used for every imputation.
#' @param level Confidence level of the pooled intervals (default 0.95).
#' @param vcov_type `"observed"` (default), `"robust"` or `"opg"`, as in
#'   [parameter_inference()], applied to every imputation's fit. For fits
#'   with sampling weights the default is `"robust"`, and the other types are
#'   refused with `latents_unsupported_weights`.
#' @param adjust Multiplicity correction applied to the pooled p-values to
#'   give `p_adjusted`, as in [parameter_inference()]: `"none"` (default) or
#'   a method of [stats::p.adjust()]. The per-imputation tables are computed
#'   without correction.
#' @return An object of class `latents_pooled`. [as.data.frame()] and
#'   `get_results(x, "estimates")` give one row per parameter, with the columns
#'   of [parameter_inference()] (`level`, `outcome`, `term`, `parameter`,
#'   `estimate`, `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`,
#'   `conf_low`, `conf_high`) plus `df` (Rubin's degrees of freedom),
#'   `within` and `between` (the two variance components), `riv` (the
#'   relative increase in variance due to missingness) and `fmi` (the fraction
#'   of missing information). `statistic` and `p_value` are `NA` where
#'   [parameter_inference()] reports no test (variances and probabilities).
#'   `get_results(x, "imputations")` gives each imputation's aligned estimates,
#'   one row per imputation and parameter, and `get_results(x, "fits")` one row
#'   per imputation with its log likelihood, convergence and the label
#'   permutation that aligned it.
#' @section Conditions:
#'   `latents_bad_data` when `imputed` is not a list of at least two data frames
#'   with identical columns and row counts; `latents_pooling_failed` when any
#'   imputation's fit or inference fails (the message names the imputation and
#'   gives the original reason); `latents_missing_package` for a `mids` object
#'   without mice installed. Warnings from the individual fits are passed on
#'   as they are raised.
#' @references
#' Rubin, D. B. (1987). *Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys*.
#' Wiley.
#'
#' Meng, X.-L. (1994). Multiple-imputation inferences with uncongenial
#' sources of input. *Statistical Science*, 9(4), 538--558.
#'
#' van Buuren, S. (2018). *Flexible Imputation of Missing Data* (2nd ed.),
#' section 5.2. Chapman & Hall/CRC.
#' @examples
#' set.seed(1)
#' # Two stand-in completed data sets. With real missing covariates, pass the
#' # `mids` object mice::mice() returns instead.
#' completed <- lapply(seq_len(2), function(i) {
#'   within(subset(course_engagement, student <= 40),
#'          previous_grade <- previous_grade + rnorm(length(previous_grade), sd = 0.1))
#' })
#' pooled <- pool_imputations(completed, c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read"),
#'                            "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1,
#'                            profile_covariates = "previous_grade",
#'                            n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#' pooled
#' get_results(pooled, "fits")
#' @export
before.source:
pool_imputations <- function(imputed, vars, id, n_profiles, ..., level = 0.95,
                             vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg"),
                             adjust = .multilpa_p_adjust_methods) {
  stopifnot(
    "`level` must be a single number in (0, 1)" =
      is.numeric(level) && length(level) == 1L && is.finite(level) &&
      level > 0 && level < 1)
  vcov_defaulted <- missing(vcov_type)

#' Fit a model to multiply imputed data and pool it with Rubin's rules
#'
#' Fits [multilpa()] to every completed data set, aligns each fit's profile and
#' group-class labels to those of the first, and pools the estimates with
#' Rubin's rules, returning a `latents_pooled` object. Use it for missing
#' covariates, which `missing = "fiml"` cannot handle because the model
#' conditions on covariates. Impute them first (for example with the mice
#' package, with the indicators and the group identifier in the imputation
#' model) and pass the completed data.
#'
#' Pooling is on the reported (natural) scale: the pooled estimate is the mean
#' over imputations, and its variance is the mean within-imputation variance
#' plus `(1 + 1/m)` times the between-imputation variance. Degrees of freedom
#' follow Rubin (1987) with a large complete-data sample. Pooled intervals are
#' symmetric t intervals on this scale, so for probabilities and variances
#' they can extend outside the parameter space, unlike the transformed Wald
#' intervals of [parameter_inference()]. A structural constant, such as the
#' probability of one for a single class, has zero within- and
#' between-imputation variance and zero missing information. When the
#' within-imputation variance is zero and the between-imputation variance is
#' positive, `riv` is infinite and `fmi` is one.
#'
#' @section Choosing the imputation model:
#' The pooled results are only as valid as the imputations. The covariate and
#' the indicators are related through the latent classes, which an imputation
#' model linear in the indicators (mice's defaults) does not capture. In
#' `validation/pool-imputations-coverage.R` (a membership slope with 30% of
#' its covariate missing at random given the indicators, 200 replications,
#' ten imputations), 95% intervals covered 0.925 under predictive mean
#' matching and 0.935 under Bayesian linear regression, and 0.995 when the
#' covariate was drawn approximately from its conditional distribution given
#' the known generating parameters. That reference arm omits uncertainty in
#' the imputation parameters, so it does not validate proper multiple
#' imputation, and the study covers one design only. The imputation model
#' should account for the latent structure and the clustering, include the
#' indicators and relevant nonlinearities, and propagate parameter
#' uncertainty; imputing separately within assigned classes ignores
#' classification uncertainty. Complete-case analysis covered 0.955 in that
#' design, but selecting on the indicators changes their within-class
#' distributions, and the case-control argument for unbiased logistic slopes
#' does not carry over when the outcome is latent and its measurement model
#' is estimated.
#'
#' @param imputed The completed data sets: a list of at least two data frames
#'   with the same columns and rows in the same order, or a `mids` object from
#'   the mice package, which is completed here.
#' @param vars,id,n_profiles As in [multilpa()].
#' @param ... Further arguments for [multilpa()], such as `n_group_classes`,
#'   `profile_covariates`, `group_covariates`, `categorical`, `n_starts` and
#'   `seed`, used for every imputation.
#' @param level Confidence level of the pooled intervals (default 0.95).
#' @param vcov_type `"observed"` (default), `"robust"` or `"opg"`, as in
#'   [parameter_inference()], applied to every imputation's fit. For fits
#'   with sampling weights the default is `"robust"`, and the other types are
#'   refused with `latents_unsupported_weights`.
#' @param adjust Multiplicity correction applied to the pooled p-values to
#'   give `p_adjusted`, as in [parameter_inference()]: `"none"` (default) or
#'   a method of [stats::p.adjust()]. The per-imputation tables are computed
#'   without correction.
#' @return An object of class `latents_pooled`. [as.data.frame()] and
#'   `get_results(x, "estimates")` give one row per parameter, with the columns
#'   of [parameter_inference()] (`level`, `outcome`, `term`, `parameter`,
#'   `estimate`, `standard_error`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `p_adjusted`,
#'   `conf_low`, `conf_high`) plus `df` (Rubin's degrees of freedom),
#'   `within` and `between` (the two variance components), `riv` (the
#'   relative increase in variance due to missingness) and `fmi` (the fraction
#'   of missing information). `statistic` and `p_value` are `NA` where
#'   [parameter_inference()] reports no test (variances and probabilities).
#'   `get_results(x, "imputations")` gives each imputation's aligned estimates,
#'   one row per imputation and parameter, and `get_results(x, "fits")` one row
#'   per imputation with its log likelihood, convergence and the label
#'   permutation that aligned it.
#' @section Conditions:
#'   `latents_bad_data` when `imputed` is not a list of at least two data frames
#'   with identical columns and row counts; `latents_pooling_failed` when any
#'   imputation's fit or inference fails (the message names the imputation and
#'   gives the original reason); `latents_missing_package` for a `mids` object
#'   without mice installed. Warnings from the individual fits are passed on
#'   as they are raised.
#' @references
#' Rubin, D. B. (1987). *Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys*.
#' Wiley.
#'
#' Meng, X.-L. (1994). Multiple-imputation inferences with uncongenial
#' sources of input. *Statistical Science*, 9(4), 538--558.
#'
#' van Buuren, S. (2018). *Flexible Imputation of Missing Data* (2nd ed.),
#' section 5.2. Chapman & Hall/CRC.
#' @examples
#' set.seed(1)
#' # Two stand-in completed data sets. With real missing covariates, pass the
#' # `mids` object mice::mice() returns instead.
#' completed <- lapply(seq_len(2), function(i) {
#'   within(subset(course_engagement, student <= 40),
#'          previous_grade <- previous_grade + rnorm(length(previous_grade), sd = 0.1))
#' })
#' pooled <- pool_imputations(completed, c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read"),
#'                            "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1,
#'                            profile_covariates = "previous_grade",
#'                            n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#' pooled
#' get_results(pooled, "fits")
#' @export

                                      vcov_defaulted)

    .multilpa_pool_step(index, "inference", {

                          adjust = "none")
    })

  if (!all(vapply(keys, identical, logical(1), keys[[1L]]))) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(

#' Pool inference tables with Rubin's rules
#'
#' Rubin (1987): the pooled estimate is the mean `Q`, the total variance
#' `T = U + (1 + 1/m) B` with `U` the mean within-imputation variance and `B`
#' the between-imputation variance, `r=(1 + 1/m) * B / U`, degrees of freedom
#' `(m - 1)(1 + 1/r)^2` (infinite when `B` is zero), and the fraction of
#' missing information `(r + 2 / (df + 3)) / (r + 1)`.
#'
#' @param tables Aligned [parameter_inference()] tables, one per imputation.
#' @param level Interval level.
#' @param adjust A [stats::p.adjust()] method for `p_adjusted`.
#' @return A data frame, one row per parameter.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(tables, level, adjust = "none") {
    m <- length(tables)
    estimates <- vapply(tables, `[[`, numeric(nrow(tables[[1L]])), "estimate")
    variances <- vapply(tables, function(table) table$standard_error^2, numeric(nrow(tables[[1L]])))
    estimates <- matrix(estimates, ncol = m)
    variances <- matrix(variances, ncol = m)
    pooled <- rowMeans(estimates)
    within <- rowMeans(variances)
    between <- apply(estimates, 1L, stats::var)
    total <- within + (1 + 1/m) * between
    riv <- (1 + 1/m) * between/within
    riv[!is.na(within) & !is.na(between) & within == 0 & between == 0] <- 0
    df <- ifelse(between > 0, (m - 1) * (1 + 1/riv)^2, Inf)
    fmi <- ifelse(is.infinite(riv), 1, (riv + 2/(df + 3))/(riv + 1))
    standard_error <- sqrt(total)
    tested <- !is.na(tables[[1L]]$statistic)
    statistic <- ifelse(tested, pooled/standard_error, NA_real_)
    p_value <- ifelse(tested, 2 * stats::pt(-abs(statistic), df), NA_real_)
    critical <- stats::qt((1 + level)/2, df)
    data.frame(tables[[1L]][c("level", "outcome", "term", "parameter")], estimate = pooled, standard_error = standard_error, statistic = statistic, p_value = p_value, p_adjusted = stats::p.adjust(p_value, method = adjust), conf_low = pooled - critical * standard_error, conf_high = pooled + critical * standard_error, df = df, within = within, between = between, riv = riv, fmi = fmi, row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

  estimates <- vapply(tables, `[[`, numeric(nrow(tables[[1L]])), "estimate")
  variances <- vapply(tables, function(table) table$standard_error^2,

  within <- rowMeans(variances)

  df <- ifelse(between > 0, (m - 1) * (1 + 1 / riv)^2, Inf)

  tested <- !is.na(tables[[1L]]$statistic)

  data.frame(
    tables[[1L]][c("level", "outcome", "term", "parameter")],
    estimate = pooled, standard_error = standard_error,
    statistic = statistic, p_value = p_value,
    p_adjusted = stats::p.adjust(p_value, method = adjust),
    conf_low = pooled - critical * standard_error,
    conf_high = pooled + critical * standard_error,
    df = df, within = within, between = between, riv = riv, fmi = fmi,
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

print.latents_pooled <- function(x, digits = 4L, rows = 20L, ...) {
  cat(sprintf(paste(
    "Pooled over %d imputations (Rubin's rules): %s, %d profiles,",
    "%d group classes\n"), x$m, x$model, x$n_profiles, x$n_group_classes))
  cat(sprintf("Largest fraction of missing information: %.3f\n",
              max(x$estimates$fmi)))
  shown <- utils::head(x$estimates[c("level", "outcome", "term", "parameter",
                                     "estimate", "standard_error", "conf_low",
                                     "conf_high", "fmi")], rows)
  print(shown, digits = digits, row.names = FALSE)
  if (nrow(x$estimates) > rows) {
    cat(sprintf("... %d more rows: as.data.frame(x)\n",
                nrow(x$estimates) - rows))
  }
  invisible(x)
}

  estimates <- x$estimates[x$estimates$level %in% what, , drop = FALSE]
  imputations <- x$imputations[x$imputations$level %in% what, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(estimates) == 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf("This fit has no `%s` parameters to plot.", what),
                        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  .gg_require()
  label <- function(table) paste(table$outcome, table$term, table$parameter)
  sources <- c("Pooled", "One imputation")
  rows <- rbind(
    data.frame(label = label(imputations), estimate = imputations$estimate,
               conf_low = NA_real_, conf_high = NA_real_, source = sources[2L]),
    data.frame(label = label(estimates), estimate = estimates$estimate,
               conf_low = estimates$conf_low, conf_high = estimates$conf_high,
               source = sources[1L]))
  # The first parameter at the top, as the tables list them.
  rows$label <- factor(rows$label, levels = rev(unique(label(estimates))))
  rows$source <- factor(rows$source, levels = sources)
  pooled <- rows[rows$source == sources[1L], , drop = FALSE]
  colours <- stats::setNames(.gg_okabe_ito[c(1L, 2L)], sources)
  drawn <- ggplot2::ggplot(rows, ggplot2::aes(estimate, label, colour = source,
                                     shape = source)) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = pooled,
                          ggplot2::aes(x = conf_low, xend = conf_high,
                                       y = label, yend = label),
                          linewidth = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.6, stroke = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = stats::setNames(c(16L, 1L), sources)) +
    .gg_theme() + .gg_top_legend() +
    ggplot2::labs(x = sprintf("Estimate with pooled %g%% interval", 100 * x$level),
                  y = NULL) +
    .gg_titles(main, subtitle, sprintf("Pooled over %d imputations", x$m),
               sprintf("%s%s parameters; open circles are the single imputations",
                       toupper(substr(what, 1L, 1L)), substring(what, 2L)))
  .gg_draw_on_call(drawn)
}

before.name: predict.multilpa
before.documentation:
#' @rdname latents-predict
#' @importFrom stats predict
#' @export
before.source:
predict.multilpa <- function(object, newdata = NULL,
                             type = c("class", "posterior", "density"), ...) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  prepared <- if (is.null(newdata)) .multilpa_training_rows(object) else
    .multilpa_prediction_rows(object, newdata)
  parameters <- object[intersect(c("means", "variances", "covariances",
                                   "profile_probabilities",
                                   "group_probabilities",
                                   "response_probabilities", "ordinal_intercepts",
                                   "ordinal_locations", "count_means",
                                   "count_dispersion", "direct_effects"),
                                 names(object))]
  if (isTRUE(object$noise)) {
    # The fit reports the noise share apart from the Gaussian profiles' shares
    # (together they sum to one); the E-step takes it as a last column.
    parameters$profile_probabilities <- cbind(parameters$profile_probabilities,
                                              noise = object$noise_probability)
    parameters$noise_log_density <- rep(-log(object$hypervolume),
                                        nrow(prepared$x))
  }
  if (identical(type, "density")) {
    return(data.frame(row = prepared$rows,
                      log_density = .multilpa_row_log_density(
                        prepared, parameters)))
  }
  expectation <- .multilpa_expectation(prepared$x, prepared$group_index,
                                       parameters, prepared$codes,
                                       extra = prepared$extra)
  .multilpa_prediction_table(object, prepared, expectation,
                             posteriors = identical(type, "posterior"))
}

.multilpa_prediction_table.name: .multilpa_prediction_table

before.name: .multilpa_prediction_table
before.documentation:
#' Tidy prediction table
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_prediction_table <- function(object, prepared, expectation,
                                       posteriors) {
  posterior <- expectation$subject_posteriors
  noisy <- isTRUE(object$noise)
  modal <- max.col(posterior, ties.method = "first")
  n_profiles <- object$n_profiles
  table <- data.frame(row = prepared$rows)
  if (prepared$two_level) table[[object$id]] <- prepared$groups
  table$profile <- ifelse(noisy & modal == ncol(posterior), 0L, modal)
  table$posterior <- posterior[cbind(seq_len(nrow(posterior)), modal)]
  if (prepared$two_level && object$n_group_classes > 1L) {
    group_modal <- max.col(expectation$group_posteriors, ties.method = "first")
    table$group_class <- group_modal[prepared$group_index]
    table$group_posterior <- expectation$group_posteriors[
      cbind(prepared$group_index, table$group_class)]
  }
  if (posteriors) {
    columns <- paste0("probability_profile_", seq_len(n_profiles))
    if (noisy) columns <- c(columns, "probability_noise")
    probability <- as.data.frame(posterior)
    names(probability) <- columns
    table <- cbind(table, probability)
  }
  table
}

prior_control.name: prior_control

before.name: prior_control
before.formal_defaults: pairlist(shrinkage = 0.01, mean = NULL, dof = NULL, scale = NULL)
before.documentation:
#' Specify a conjugate prior for Gaussian mixture estimation
#'
#' Returns a `latents_prior` object requesting maximum a posteriori (MAP)
#' estimation of the Gaussian profile means and covariances under the
#' conjugate prior of Fraley and Raftery (2007), as `mclust::priorControl()`
#' does for `mclust::Mclust()`. Pass the result as `multilpa(prior = )`. The
#' prior keeps the covariance estimates away from singularity.
#'
#' Every argument left `NULL` takes `mclust::defaultPrior()`'s value, computed
#' from the indicators being fitted: the prior mean is their column means, the
#' degrees of freedom are `d + 2` for `d` indicators, and the scale is
#' `(1/G)^(2/d)` times the sample covariance (ellipsoidal structures) or times
#' the average sample variance (axis-parallel and spherical structures), for
#' `G` profiles.
#'
#' The updates follow mclust's fitted-model convention, including its
#' structure-specific departures from a textbook conjugate update, so the
#' controls have different effects across covariance structures. For `EII`,
#' `scale` does not enter the variance update. For `EEI`, `shrinkage` and
#' `mean` enter the variance calculation but do not shrink the fitted means.
#' For `VEV`, `dof` does not enter the update. `EEI`, `EVI` and `EEV` count the
#' mean-prior contribution once rather than once per profile.
#'
#' @param shrinkage Non-negative prior precision factor for the means, `kappa`
#'   (default `0.01`, as in mclust). Zero leaves the means unshrunk.
#' @param mean Optional prior mean, one value per continuous indicator, on the
#'   scale the profile means are estimated on: the indicators' own units, or
#'   their centred values under [multilpa()]'s `centering`. Requires a positive
#'   `shrinkage`.
#' @param dof Optional prior degrees of freedom, a single positive number.
#' @param scale Optional prior scale: a single positive number for an
#'   axis-parallel or spherical structure, or a positive-definite `d` by `d`
#'   matrix for an ellipsoidal one.
#' @return An object of class `latents_prior`: a list with `shrinkage`, `mean`,
#'   `dof` and `scale`, the last three `NULL` where the default is to be
#'   computed from the data.
#' @section Conditions:
#'   `latents_bad_argument` for a negative or non-finite `shrinkage`, a
#'   non-finite `mean`, a `mean` with a zero `shrinkage`, a non-positive or
#'   non-finite `dof`, or a `scale` that is neither a positive number nor a
#'   square, symmetric, positive-definite matrix.
#' @references Fraley, C., & Raftery, A. E. (2007). Bayesian regularization for
#'   normal mixture estimation and model-based clustering. *Journal of
#'   Classification*, 24, 155--181. \doi{10.1007/s00357-007-0004-5}
#' @seealso [multilpa()], whose `prior` argument takes this.
#' @examples
#' prior_control()
#' prior_control(shrinkage = 0)
#' @export
before.terminal_expression: structure(list(shrinkage = shrinkage, mean = mean, dof = dof, scale = scale), class = "latents_prior")

before.name: .multilpa_positive_scale
before.documentation:
#' Is a prior scale a positive number or a positive-definite matrix?
#'
#' A matrix is checked as one: square, symmetric to a relative `1e-10` and
#' with a positive smallest eigenvalue. Positive diagonal entries alone admit
#' indefinite matrices, which only failed later, at fit time.
#'
#' @param scale A finite numeric scalar, vector or matrix.
#' @return A single logical.
#' @noRd
before.terminal_expression: max(abs(scale - t(scale))) <= 1e-10 * max(abs(scale)) && min(eigen((scale + t(scale))/2, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values) > 0

before.name: diagnostics
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(x = , data = NULL, plots = TRUE, by = c("profile", "overall"), ... = ))
before.documentation:
#' Classification diagnostics of a fitted model
#'
#' Gathers the four classification tables of [get_results()] (`"entropy"`,
#' `"classification"`, `"average_posteriors"` and `"residuals"`) for a fitted
#' model, prints one line per diagnostic, and by default draws the
#' classification plots. The diagnostics are relative entropy, estimated class
#' sizes, average posterior probabilities of the assigned classes, and the
#' bivariate residuals that check the within-profile independence the model
#' assumes.
#'
#' @param x A fitted model of this package.
#' @param data Optional. The data the model was fitted to. A fit carries the
#'   columns it was built from, so this is only needed to override them.
#' @param plots `TRUE` (the default) also draws the four classification plots:
#'   effective profile sizes, posterior probabilities of the assigned
#'   profiles, case entropy, and the average posterior probability matrix.
#'   Without the ggplot2 package a message says so and the tables are still
#'   returned. `FALSE` returns the tables only.
#' @param by `"profile"` (the default) assesses each profile's bivariate
#'   residuals separately; `"overall"` pools them. It is the only argument
#'   forwarded to the gathered tables. The `level` of the classification
#'   tables is set from whether the fit has discrete group classes.
#' @param ... Not used. For `diagnostics()` and `plot()`, any further argument
#'   raises `latents_bad_argument`; style the returned plots with ggplot2.
#' @return An object of class `multilpa_diagnostics`. Its tables are read with
#'   `get_results(result, what = )`, where `what` is `"entropy"`,
#'   `"classification"`, `"average_posteriors"`, `"residuals"` or `"all"`. A
#'   model family without bivariate residuals leaves that table out of
#'   `"all"`, and asking for it by name raises `latents_no_group_classes`; a
#'   fit with a noise component has none either, and raises
#'   `latents_unsupported_noise`.
#'
#'   `print()` prints one line per diagnostic (relative entropy, smallest
#'   class, lowest average posterior and largest residual, at each level the
#'   fit has) and returns the object invisibly. `plot()` returns the four
#'   classification plots as a `latents_plots` list of ggplot objects, which
#'   draws all four when printed. `as.data.frame()` returns the entropy table.
#' @seealso [get_results()] for these and the other tables, [descriptives()]
#'   for the variables before fitting, and [summary()] for the estimates.
#' @examples
#' fit <- multilpa(
#'   course_engagement,
#'   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
#'   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
#'   seed = 1
#' )
#' quality <- diagnostics(fit)
#' quality
#' get_results(quality, what = "classification")
#' get_results(diagnostics(fit, by = "overall"), what = "residuals")
#' @export
before.definition_AST:
function(x, data = NULL, plots = TRUE, by = c("profile", "overall"), ...) {
    stopifnot(`\`x\` must be a fitted model of this package` = .multilpa_any_fit(x), `\`plots\` must be TRUE or FALSE` = isTRUE(plots) || isFALSE(plots))
    .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(list(...), "diagnostics()", paste("The only argument of a gathered table it forwards is `by`;", "ask get_results() for that table directly for anything else."))
    by <- match.arg(by)
    data <- .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data)
    has_groups <- !is.null(x$group_posteriors)
    level <- if (has_groups) 
        "both"
    else "individuals"
    result <- list(entropy = .multilpa_entropy_table(x), classification = .multilpa_classification_table(x, level = level), average_posteriors = .multilpa_average_posteriors(x, level = level), residuals = tryCatch(.multilpa_bivariate_residuals(x, data, by = by), latents_no_group_classes = function(condition) NULL, latents_unsupported_noise = function(condition) NULL), fit = x)
    class(result) <- "multilpa_diagnostics"
    if (isTRUE(plots) && .gg_available()) 
        print(plot(result))
    result
}

diagnostics <- function(x, data = NULL, plots = TRUE,
                        by = c("profile", "overall"), ...) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x),
            "`plots` must be TRUE or FALSE" = isTRUE(plots) || isFALSE(plots))
  .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
    list(...), "diagnostics()",
    paste("The only argument of a gathered table it forwards is `by`;",
          "ask get_results() for that table directly for anything else."))
  by <- match.arg(by)
  data <- .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data)
  has_groups <- !is.null(x$group_posteriors)
  level <- if (has_groups) "both" else "individuals"
  result <- list(
    entropy = .multilpa_entropy_table(x),
    classification = .multilpa_classification_table(x, level = level),
    average_posteriors = .multilpa_average_posteriors(x, level = level),
    # Residuals need a discrete group-class model and no noise component; a
    # fit without them has no such table, as `get_results(x, "all")` says, and
    # the other three diagnostics are still reported.
    residuals = tryCatch(.multilpa_bivariate_residuals(x, data, by = by),
                         latents_no_group_classes = function(condition) NULL,
                         latents_unsupported_noise = function(condition) NULL),
    fit = x)
  class(result) <- "multilpa_diagnostics"
  if (isTRUE(plots) && .gg_available()) print(plot(result))
  result
}

The diagnostics are relative entropy, estimated class sizes, average posterior probabilities of the assigned classes, and the bivariate residuals that check the within-profile independence the model assumes.  @param x A fitted model of this package. @param data Optional. The data the model was fitted to. A fit carries the   columns it was built from, so this is only needed to override them. @param plots `TRUE` (the default) also draws the four classification plots:   effective profile sizes, posterior probabilities of the assigned   profiles, case entropy, and the average posterior probability matrix.   Without the ggplot2 package a message says so and the tables are still   returned. `FALSE` returns the tables only. @param by `"profile"` (the default) assesses each profile's bivariate   residuals separately; `"overall"` pools them. It is the only argument   forwarded to the gathered tables. The `level` of the classification   tables is set from whether the fit has discrete group classes. @param ... Not used. For `diagnostics()` and `plot()`, any further argument   raises `latents_bad_argument`; style the returned plots with ggplot2. @return An object of class `multilpa_diagnostics`. Its tables are read with   `get_results(result, what = )`, where `what` is `"entropy"`,   `"classification"`, `"average_posteriors"`, `"residuals"` or `"all"`. A   model family without bivariate residuals leaves that table out of   `"all"`, and asking for it by name raises `latents_no_group_classes`; a   fit with a noise component has none either, and raises   `latents_unsupported_noise`.    `print()` prints one line per diagnostic (relative entropy, smallest   class, lowest average posterior and largest residual, at each level the   fit has) and returns the object invisibly. `plot()` returns the four   classification plots as a `latents_plots` list of ggplot objects, which   draws all four when printed. `as.data.frame()` returns the entropy table. @seealso [get_results()] for these and the other tables, [descriptives()]   for the variables before fitting, and [summary()] for the estimates. @examples fit <- multilpa(   course_engagement,   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,   seed = 1 ) quality <- diagnostics(fit) quality get_results(quality, what = "classification") get_results(diagnostics(fit, by = "overall"), what = "residuals") @export

report.name: report

before.name: report
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(x = , data = NULL, plots = TRUE, by = c("profile", "overall"), rows = 10L, ... = ))
before.documentation:
#' Print a full report of a fitted model
#'
#' Prints the model summary, the descriptive statistics of its variables and
#' the classification diagnostics, then draws every plot view the fit
#' supports.
#'
#' @param x A fitted model of this package.
#' @param data Optional. The data the model was fitted to; a fit carries the
#'   columns it was built from.
#' @param plots `TRUE` (the default) draws the plots. `FALSE` prints only.
#' @param rows Number of rows of each summary table to print, passed to
#'   `print(summary(x))`. Default 10.
#' @param by Passed to [diagnostics()] for the bivariate residuals:
#'   `"profile"` (the default) assesses each profile separately, `"overall"`
#'   pools them.
#' @param ... Not used. Any further argument raises `latents_bad_argument`
#'   before anything is printed.
#' @section What it prints: `summary()`, then `descriptives()`, then the
#'   one-line-per-diagnostic reading of `diagnostics()`, then every plot view
#'   the fit supports. Views that the plot method declines for this model are
#'   listed after the plots as not drawn. The tables themselves are obtained
#'   from [get_results()], [summary()], [descriptives()] and [diagnostics()].
#' @return The fitted model, invisibly. Called for its printed and plotted
#'   output.
#' @seealso [summary()], [diagnostics()], [descriptives()],
#'   [plot_views()].
#' @examples
#' fit <- multilpa(
#'   course_engagement,
#'   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
#'   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
#'   seed = 1
#' )
#' report(fit, plots = FALSE)
#' @export
before.source:
report <- function(x, data = NULL, plots = TRUE,
                   by = c("profile", "overall"), rows = 10L, ...) {
  stopifnot("`x` must be a fitted model of this package" = .multilpa_any_fit(x),
            "`plots` must be TRUE or FALSE" = isTRUE(plots) || isFALSE(plots))
  # Checked here as well as in diagnostics(), so a refused argument is refused
  # before three sections have already been printed.
  .multilpa_reject_extra_arguments(
    list(...), "report()",
    "It forwards `by` to diagnostics() and `rows` to print(summary(x)).")
  by <- match.arg(by)
  data <- .multilpa_resolve_data(x, data)
  print(summary(x), rows = rows)
  cat("\n")
  print(descriptives(x))
  cat("\n")
  quality <- diagnostics(x, data = data, plots = FALSE, by = by)
  print(quality)
  if (isTRUE(plots) && .gg_available()) {
    views <- .multilpa_supported_views(x)
    # A view can still refuse for a reason only the method knows -- a family
    # with no plot at all, a panel with nothing in it. `report()` is a first
    # look, so it moves on; it says which views it could not draw rather than
    # dropping them silently.
    refused <- unlist(lapply(views, function(view) {
      drawn <- tryCatch({
        print(if (is.na(view)) plot(x) else plot(x, what = view))
        NULL
      },
      latents_no_plot = function(condition) view,
      latents_nothing_to_plot = function(condition) view,
      latents_no_time = function(condition) view,
      latents_no_categorical = function(condition) view,
      latents_no_continuous = function(condition) view,
      latents_no_indicator_data = function(condition) view)
      drawn
    }))
    if (length(refused) > 0L) {
      cat(sprintf("\nNot drawn for this model: %s\n",
                  paste(ifelse(is.na(refused), "the default plot", refused),
                        collapse = ", ")))
    }
  }
  invisible(x)
}

.multilpa_group_scores.name: .multilpa_group_scores

before.name: .multilpa_group_scores
before.documentation:
#' Per-group scores of the observed-data log likelihood
#'
#' Decomposes the gradient into one row per independent group. The groups are
#' the independent sampling units of the two-level likelihood, so these rows are
#' the contributions the robust cross-product matrix accumulates.
#'
#' @param theta Unconstrained parameter vector.
#' @param x Centered numeric indicator matrix, possibly containing NA.
#' @param object Fitted model defining dimensions and groups.
#' @return A groups-by-parameters matrix whose column sums equal the gradient of
#'   the positive observed-data log likelihood, that is `-.multilpa_score()`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_group_scores <- function(theta, x, object, codes = NULL) {
  stopifnot("`theta` must be numeric" = is.numeric(theta),
            "`x` must be a numeric matrix" = is.matrix(x) && is.numeric(x),
            "`object` must be an `multilpa` fit" = inherits(object, "multilpa"))
  parameters <- .multilpa_decode(theta, object)
  group_index <- object$group_index
  expectation <- .multilpa_expectation(x, group_index, parameters, codes,
                                       unname(object$sampling_weights),
                                       object$extra_data)
  n_profiles <- object$n_profiles
  n_types <- object$n_group_classes
  measurement <- if (.multilpa_uses_chart(object)) {
    .multilpa_chart_scores(
      parameters, expectation, x, object,
      theta[length(parameters$means) +
              seq_len(.multilpa_coordinate_widths(object, "unconstrained")[["variances"]])],
      group_index)
  } else if (identical(object$covariance_model, "full")) {
    .multilpa_full_measurement_group_score(parameters, expectation, object)
  } else {
    shifted <- .latents_direct_shift(x, object$extra_data, parameters)
    observed <- !is.na(x)
    blocks <- lapply(seq_len(n_profiles), function(profile) {
      residuals <- sweep(shifted, 2L, parameters$means[profile, ], "-")
      residuals[!observed] <- 0
      weights <- expectation$subject_posteriors[, profile]
      list(
        means = rowsum(sweep(residuals, 2L, parameters$variances[profile, ], "/") *
                         weights, group_index, reorder = FALSE),
        variances = rowsum(0.5 * (sweep(residuals^2, 2L,
          parameters$variances[profile, ], "/") - observed) * weights,
          group_index, reorder = FALSE))
    })
    variances <- if (object$variance_model == "equal") {
      Reduce(`+`, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "variances"))
    } else do.call(cbind, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "variances"))
    list(means = do.call(cbind, lapply(blocks, `[[`, "means")),
         covariances = variances)
  }
  # Each group class contributes its own multinomial score for the profile
  # proportions, with the final profile as the omitted reference category.
  profile_scores <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(n_types), function(group_type) {
    counts <- rowsum(expectation$joint[[group_type]], group_index, reorder = FALSE)
    expected <- outer(rowSums(counts), parameters$profile_probabilities[group_type, ])
    (counts - expected)[, seq_len(n_profiles - 1L), drop = FALSE]
  }))
  # A weighted posterior row sums to its unit's weight, so the expected count
  # is that weight times the class probabilities; unweighted, it is one.
  group_scores <- (expectation$group_posteriors -
    outer(rowSums(expectation$group_posteriors),
          parameters$group_probabilities))[, seq_len(n_types - 1L), drop = FALSE]
  response_scores <- .multilpa_response_scores(
    codes, expectation$subject_posteriors, parameters$response_probabilities,
    group_index)
  extra_scores <- .latents_extra_scores(object$extra_data,
                                        expectation$subject_posteriors,
                                        parameters, group_index, x = x)
  scores <- cbind(measurement$means, measurement$covariances, response_scores,
                  extra_scores, profile_scores, group_scores)
  dimnames(scores) <- list(object$group_ids, names(theta))
  scores
}

.multilpa_design_scale.name: .multilpa_design_scale

before.name: .multilpa_design_scale
before.documentation:
#' Column scales that make an optimization coordinate unit-free
#'
#' A multinomial logit is a parameterization of the same model under any linear
#' rescaling of a predictor: multiplying a covariate by `c` and its coefficient
#' by `1/c` leaves every fitted probability alone. A quasi-Newton search is not
#' invariant in that way, because it stops on a relative tolerance measured in
#' the coordinates it was handed. A column whose units are `1e-7` times those of
#' the rest therefore stalls the search while the score is still large, and the
#' optimizer still reports success.
#'
#' The root-mean-square of a column is exactly proportional to that column's
#' units, so dividing each column by it gives a design matrix that does not
#' change when a predictor is rescaled. Fitting in those coordinates and
#' dividing the coefficients back by the same scales returns estimates in the
#' user's units while making the search itself unit-free.
#'
#' @param design A numeric design matrix with finite entries.
#' @return A positive numeric vector with one entry per column of `design`. A
#'   column that is exactly zero, or whose root-mean-square is not finite, gets
#'   `1`, so the scaling is never itself a source of `NaN`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_design_scale <- function(design) {
  stopifnot(
    "`design` must be a numeric matrix" =
      is.matrix(design) && is.numeric(design),
    "`design` must be finite" = all(is.finite(design)))
  if (ncol(design) == 0L) return(numeric(0))
  ## The peak comes out first so that squaring a column held in very large
  ## units cannot overflow to `Inf` before the mean is taken.
  peak <- apply(abs(design), 2L, max)
  safe <- ifelse(is.finite(peak) & peak > 0, peak, 1)
  scale <- safe * sqrt(colMeans(sweep(design, 2L, safe, "/")^2))
  unname(ifelse(is.finite(scale) & scale > 0, scale, 1))
}
