.multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale.name: .multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale

before.name: .multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale
before.documentation:
#' Scales for the log-Cholesky coordinates of a residual covariance
#'
#' The unrestricted residual covariance is estimated through the lower triangle
#' of its Cholesky factor, with the diagonal logged. Those coordinates do not
#' share one unit: a logged diagonal entry is dimensionless, while an
#' off-diagonal entry `L[i, j]` carries the units of indicator `i`. Handing them
#' to a finite-difference Hessian unscaled makes the information matrix's
#' condition number grow with the square of the indicator units, and it is then
#' declared singular for no reason but the units the data arrived in.
#'
#' This is the general form of the scaling [parameter_inference()] already
#' applies to a covariate-free `multilpa` fit (R/inference.R), written so that
#' the covariate path can share it instead of rediscovering it.
#'
#' @param variances A profiles-by-indicators matrix of residual variances, the
#'   diagonal of each profile's residual covariance.
#' @param dimension Number of continuous indicators.
#' @param rows Integer indices of the rows of `variances` whose spread block is
#'   estimated separately: every profile under a varying spread, `1L` when one
#'   block is shared.
#' @return A positive numeric vector of length
#'   `length(rows) * dimension * (dimension + 1) / 2`, ordered as the
#'   coordinates themselves are: one block per entry of `rows`, and within a
#'   block the lower triangle including the diagonal, in column-major order.
#'   Diagonal entries get `1` because they are logged.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_covariance_coordinate_scale <- function(variances, dimension, rows) {
  stopifnot(
    "`variances` must be a numeric matrix" =
      is.matrix(variances) && is.numeric(variances),
    "`dimension` must be a single non-negative whole number" =
      is.numeric(dimension) && length(dimension) == 1L && is.finite(dimension) &&
      dimension >= 0 && dimension == as.integer(dimension),
    "`variances` must have at least `dimension` columns" =
      ncol(variances) >= dimension,
    "`rows` must index rows of `variances`" =
      is.numeric(rows) && length(rows) >= 1L && all(is.finite(rows)) &&
      all(rows >= 1L) && all(rows <= nrow(variances)),
    "`variances` must be positive" = all(variances > 0))
  if (dimension == 0L) return(numeric(0))
  positions <- which(lower.tri(matrix(0, dimension, dimension), diag = TRUE),
                     arr.ind = TRUE)
  unlist(lapply(rows, function(profile) {
    ifelse(positions[, 1L] == positions[, 2L], 1,
           sqrt(variances[profile, positions[, 1L]]))
  }), use.names = FALSE)
}

#'
#' When every profile shares one covariance matrix (EII, EEI, EEE), the
#' likelihood is bounded: no profile can collapse onto a point without
#' lowering the density of every other (McLachlan & Peel, 2000, section 3.8).
#' A higher maximum is then a better estimate, never a degenerate one, so the
#' screened emEM search, which reaches more of them, is the default. With
#' profile-specific covariances a higher maximum can be such a collapse, and
#' the kmeans search stays the default.

.latents_refit_controls.name: .latents_refit_controls

before.name: .latents_refit_controls
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(model = , n_starts = NULL, max_iter = NULL, tol = NULL))
before.documentation:
#' The fitting controls a bootstrap refit of a model uses
#'
#' A refit repeats the search and the stopping rule the model was fitted
#' with, so the statistic and its reference distribution come from the same
#' procedure; an explicit `n_starts`, `max_iter` or `tol` overrides them for
#' every model. A fit made before these controls were recorded falls back to
#' the values `bootstrap_lrt()` used to apply to every refit (10 starts, 1000
#' iterations, `1e-8`, the default search, selection and acceleration).
#'
#' @param model A fitted model.
#' @param n_starts,max_iter,tol `NULL` to inherit, or an override.
#' @return A named list of `search`, `n_starts`, `n_screen`, `max_iter`,
#'   `tol`, `acceleration`, `select_start` and `boundary`.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(model, n_starts = NULL, max_iter = NULL, tol = NULL) {
    recorded <- !is.null(model$search)
    starts <- as.integer(n_starts %||% (if (recorded) model$n_starts) %||% 10L)
    search <- model$search %||% "kmeans"
    n_screen <- if (identical(search, "emEM") && identical(starts, as.integer(model$n_starts))) 
        model$n_screen
    list(search = search, n_starts = starts, n_screen = n_screen, max_iter = as.integer(max_iter %||% (if (recorded) model$max_iter) %||% 1000L), tol = tol %||% (if (recorded) model$tol) %||% 1e-08, acceleration = model$acceleration %||% "squarem", select_start = model$select_start %||% "likelihood", boundary = model$boundary_policy %||% "allow")
}
before.source:
.latents_refit_controls <- function(model, n_starts = NULL, max_iter = NULL,
                                    tol = NULL) {
  recorded <- !is.null(model$search)
  starts <- as.integer(n_starts %||% (if (recorded) model$n_starts) %||% 10L)
  search <- model$search %||% "kmeans"
  # A changed number of starts takes the default pool for that number.
  n_screen <- if (identical(search, "emEM") &&
                  identical(starts, as.integer(model$n_starts))) model$n_screen
  list(search = search, n_starts = starts, n_screen = n_screen,
       max_iter = as.integer(max_iter %||% (if (recorded) model$max_iter) %||% 1000L),
       tol = tol %||% (if (recorded) model$tol) %||% 1e-8,
       acceleration = model$acceleration %||% "squarem",
       select_start = model$select_start %||% "likelihood",
       boundary = model$boundary_policy %||% "allow")
}

.latents_selection_frame.name: .latents_selection_frame

before.name: .latents_selection_frame
before.documentation:
#' One row per candidate with the criterion the views read
#'
#' @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`.
#' @param using The criterion column.
#' @return A data frame: `candidate`, `n_profiles`, `n_group_classes`,
#'   `model`, `n_parameters`, `value`, and `usable` (converged with a finite
#'   value).
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_selection_frame <- function(x, using) {
  criteria <- unname(.latents_grid_views(x, "The selection view")$criteria)
  if (!is.character(using) || length(using) != 1L || !using %in% criteria) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf(
      "`using` must name one information criterion of the grid: %s.",
      paste(sprintf("\"%s\"", criteria), collapse = ", ")),
      class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
  }
  # The criteria and diagnostics are stored; the AvePP columns, which need
  # every fit's posteriors, are not needed here.
  grid <- .latents_grid_table(x)
  value <- grid[[using]]
  data.frame(candidate = grid$candidate, n_profiles = grid$n_profiles,
             n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes, model = grid$model,
             n_parameters = grid$n_parameters, value = value,
             usable = grid$converged %in% TRUE & is.finite(value),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
before.terminal_expression: data.frame(candidate = grid$candidate, n_profiles = grid$n_profiles, n_group_classes = grid$n_group_classes, model = grid$model, n_parameters = grid$n_parameters, value = value, usable = grid$converged %in% TRUE & is.finite(value), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

before.name: .latents_kneedle
before.documentation:
#' The maximum perpendicular chord-distance knee of one curve
#'
#' Both axes are rescaled to 0-1, and the knee is the point furthest below
#' the straight line from the first point to the last,
#' measured perpendicular to that line. This simplified Kneedle-inspired
#' statistic omits smoothing, local-maxima thresholds and sensitivity; a tiny
#' positive distance may therefore still name a knee.
#'
#' @param x,y The curve, ordered by `x`.
#' The curve is a criterion that should fall as the model grows; a line
#' whose last value is not below its first has no knee, because a bend in a
#' criterion that only rises marks no diminishing return.
#'
#' @return A list: `at` (the index of the knee, `NA` without one), `distance`
#'   (each point's perpendicular distance below the line, in the rescaled
#'   units) and `rising` (`TRUE` when the criterion does not fall along the
#'   line).
#' @noRd
before.terminal_expression: list(at = if (distance[at] > sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)) at else NA_integer_, distance = distance, rising = FALSE)

.latents_knees_table.name: .latents_knees_table

before.name: .latents_knees_table
before.documentation:
#' The knee of every line of the grid, in each direction
#'
#' @param x A `multilpa_enumeration`.
#' @param using The criterion.
#' @return One row per line: `direction` (`"profiles"`: along the number of
#'   profiles at fixed group classes; `"group_classes"`: along the group
#'   classes at fixed profiles; `"parameters"`: every candidate, by number of
#'   parameters), `line` (what is held fixed), `criterion`, `from`, `to`,
#'   `n_points`, `knee_candidate`, `distance`, `knee_without_largest`,
#'   `stable` and `note`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_knees_table <- function(x, using = "bic_groups") {
  frame <- .latents_selection_frame(x, using)
  usable <- frame[frame$usable, , drop = FALSE]
  structure_text <- function(rows) {
    if (all(is.na(rows$model)) || length(unique(stats::na.omit(frame$model))) < 2L) "" else
      paste0(", ", rows$model[1L])
  }
  one_line <- function(rows, along, direction, line) {
    rows <- rows[order(rows[[along]]), , drop = FALSE]
    n <- nrow(rows)
    knee <- .latents_kneedle(rows[[along]], rows$value)
    shorter <- if (n >= 4L) .latents_kneedle(rows[[along]][-n], rows$value[-n])$at else
      NA_integer_
    found <- !is.na(knee$at)
    without <- if (is.na(shorter)) NA_character_ else rows$candidate[shorter]
    knee_name <- if (found) rows$candidate[knee$at] else NA_character_
    note <- if (n < 3L) "fewer than three candidates" else
      if (isTRUE(knee$rising)) "the criterion does not fall along this line" else
        if (!found) "the curve does not bend below the line" else
        if (n < 4L) "three candidates: stability not assessed" else
          if (is.na(without)) "no knee when the largest is left out" else
            if (identical(without, knee_name)) "" else
              "moves when the largest is left out"
    data.frame(direction = direction, line = line, criterion = using,
               from = rows$candidate[1L], to = rows$candidate[n], n_points = n,
               knee_candidate = knee_name,
               distance = if (found) knee$distance[knee$at] else NA_real_,
               knee_without_largest = without,
               stable = if (found && n >= 4L) identical(without, knee_name) else NA,
               note = note, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  model_key <- ifelse(is.na(usable$model), "", usable$model)
  along_profiles <- lapply(split(usable, list(usable$n_group_classes, model_key),
                                 drop = TRUE), function(rows) {
    one_line(rows, "n_profiles", "profiles",
             sprintf("%d group class%s%s", rows$n_group_classes[1L],
                     if (rows$n_group_classes[1L] == 1L) "" else "es",
                     structure_text(rows)))
  })
  several_groups <- length(unique(usable$n_group_classes)) > 1L
  along_groups <- if (several_groups) {
    lapply(split(usable, list(usable$n_profiles, model_key), drop = TRUE),
           function(rows) {
             one_line(rows, "n_group_classes", "group_classes",
                      sprintf("%d profile%s%s", rows$n_profiles[1L],
                              if (rows$n_profiles[1L] == 1L) "" else "s",
                              structure_text(rows)))
           })
  } else list()
  by_parameters <- lapply(split(usable, model_key, drop = TRUE), function(rows) {
    one_line(rows, "n_parameters", "parameters",
             paste0("all candidates", structure_text(rows)))
  })
  result <- do.call(rbind, c(along_profiles, along_groups, by_parameters))
  if (is.null(result)) {
    return(data.frame(direction = character(), line = character(),
                      criterion = character(), from = character(),
                      to = character(), n_points = integer(),
                      knee_candidate = character(), distance = numeric(),
                      knee_without_largest = character(), stable = logical(),
                      note = character()))
  }
  result <- result[order(match(result$direction,
                               c("profiles", "group_classes", "parameters"))), ,
                   drop = FALSE]
  row.names(result) <- NULL
  result
}

before.name: .gg_selection_deltas
before.documentation:
#' Deltas view: what each added profile and group class buys
#'
#' Two panels. In each, a line holds the other count fixed, and every point
#' is the criterion's decrease from the neighbour one step smaller. Each line
#' is named at its end.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(x, using, main, subtitle) {
    deltas <- .latents_deltas_table(x, using)
    word <- .latents_grid_views(x)$word
    singular <- .latents_singular(word)
    several_models <- length(unique(deltas$model[!is.na(deltas$model)])) > 1L
    structure_suffix <- if (several_models) 
        paste0(", ", deltas$model)
    else ""
    panel_profile <- sprintf("Adding a %s", singular)
    panel_group <- "Adding a group class"
    long <- rbind(data.frame(panel = panel_profile, candidate = deltas$candidate, x = deltas$n_profiles, delta = deltas$delta_profile, line = sprintf("%d group class%s%s", deltas$n_group_classes, ifelse(deltas$n_group_classes == 1L, "", "es"), structure_suffix), stringsAsFactors = FALSE), data.frame(panel = panel_group, candidate = deltas$candidate, x = deltas$n_group_classes, delta = deltas$delta_group_class, line = sprintf("%d %s%s", deltas$n_profiles, ifelse(deltas$n_profiles == 1L, singular, 
        word), structure_suffix), stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    long <- long[is.finite(long$delta), , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(long) == 0L) {
        stop(errorCondition("No converged candidate has a converged neighbour one step smaller.", class = "latents_nothing_to_plot", call = NULL))
    }
    long$panel <- factor(long$panel, levels = c(panel_profile, panel_group))
    long$key <- paste(long$panel, long$line)
    keys <- unique(long$key)
    colours <- stats::setNames(rep_len(.gg_okabe_ito, length(keys)), keys)
    ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(long, long$key), function(s) s[which.max(s$x), ]))
    ends <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ends, ends$panel, drop = TRUE), function(p) {
        span <- diff(range(long$delta[long$panel == p$panel[1L]]))
        p$y <- .gg_spread(p$delta, gap = 0.06 * max(span, 1e-08))
        p
    }))
    plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(long, ggplot2::aes(x, delta, colour = key, group = key)) + ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) + ggplot2::geom_line(data = long[stats::ave(long$x, long$key, FUN = length) > 1L, , drop = FALSE], linewidth = 0.8) + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.8) + ggplot2::geom_text(data = ends, ggplot2::aes(x = x + 0.15, y = y, label = line), hjust = 0, size = 3, fontface = "bold") + ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = colours) + ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = function(limits) {

#' Heatmap view: the criterion over profiles and group classes
#' @noRd
before.source:
.gg_selection_heatmap <- function(x, using, main, subtitle) {
  frame <- .latents_selection_frame(x, using)
  if (!any(frame$usable)) {
    stop(errorCondition(sprintf("No converged candidate has a finite %s.", using),
                        class = "latents_nothing_to_plot", call = NULL))
  }
  lowest <- min(frame$value[frame$usable])
  frame$delta <- ifelse(frame$usable, frame$value - lowest, NA_real_)
  frame$tile_label <- ifelse(!frame$usable, "x", sprintf("+%.0f", frame$delta))
  frame$tile_label[which.min(frame$delta)] <- "lowest"
  frame$n_group_label <- factor(frame$n_group_classes,
                                levels = sort(unique(frame$n_group_classes)))
  several_models <- length(unique(frame$model[!is.na(frame$model)])) > 1L
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(frame, ggplot2::aes(n_profiles, n_group_label, fill = delta)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = tile_label), size = 3.2) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#4A6FE3", high = "white", na.value = "grey85",
                                 name = sprintf("%s above the lowest", using)) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(frame$n_profiles))) +
    ggplot2::labs(y = "Number of group classes")
  if (several_models) plot <- plot + ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(model))
  .latents_selection_look(
    plot, main, subtitle, sprintf("%s over the whole grid", using),
    "Each tile: the criterion above the lowest candidate; x = not fitted or not converged",
    sprintf("Number of %s", .latents_grid_views(x)$word)) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right", panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank())
}

.gg_selection_smallest <- function(x, main, subtitle) {
  views <- .latents_grid_views(x)
  frame <- .latents_selection_frame(x, views$using)
  shares <- .latents_grid_smallest_shares(x)
  word <- views$word
  singular <- .latents_singular(word)
  long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(shares), function(level) {
    values <- shares[[level]]
    data.frame(frame[c("candidate", "n_profiles", "n_group_classes", "model")],
               panel = if (identical(level, "individuals"))
                 sprintf("Smallest %s", singular) else "Smallest group class",
               smallest_share = values,
               keep = frame$usable & is.finite(values), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  long <- long[long$keep, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(long) == 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition("No converged candidate has two or more classes.",
                        class = "latents_nothing_to_plot", call = NULL))
  }
  long$panel <- factor(long$panel, levels = c(sprintf("Smallest %s", singular),
                                              "Smallest group class"))
  several_models <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(long$model))) > 1L
  long$line <- sprintf("%d group class%s%s", long$n_group_classes,
                       ifelse(long$n_group_classes == 1L, "", "es"),
                       if (several_models) paste0(", ", long$model) else "")

#' Trust view: whether each candidate's estimate can be believed
#' @noRd
before.source:
.gg_selection_trust <- function(x, main, subtitle) {
  grid <- .latents_grid_table(x)
  status <- ifelse(is.na(grid$log_likelihood), "not fitted",
                   ifelse(!(grid$converged %in% TRUE), "not converged",
                          ifelse(grid$boundary %in% TRUE, "on a boundary",
                                 ifelse(grid$n_best_replicated %in% 1L,
                                        "best found once", "best replicated"))))
  frame <- data.frame(candidate = grid$candidate, n_profiles = grid$n_profiles,
                      n_group_label = factor(grid$n_group_classes,
                                             levels = sort(unique(grid$n_group_classes))),
                      model = grid$model,
                      status = factor(status, levels = c("best replicated", "best found once",
                                                         "on a boundary", "not converged",
                                                         "not fitted")),
                      tile_label = ifelse(is.na(grid$log_likelihood), "x",
                                          ifelse(is.na(grid$n_best_replicated), "",
                                                 sprintf("%dx", grid$n_best_replicated))),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  several_models <- length(unique(frame$model[!is.na(frame$model)])) > 1L
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(frame, ggplot2::aes(n_profiles, n_group_label, fill = status)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = tile_label), size = 3.2) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("best replicated" = "#009E73",
                                          "best found once" = "#F0E442",
                                          "on a boundary" = "#E69F00",
                                          "not converged" = "#D55E00",
                                          "not fitted" = "#999999"),
                               drop = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(frame$n_profiles))) +
    ggplot2::labs(y = "Number of group classes")
  if (several_models) plot <- plot + ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(model))
  .latents_selection_look(
    plot, main, subtitle, "Can each candidate be trusted?",
    "Label: how many random starts reached the best log likelihood; x = not fitted",
    sprintf("Number of %s", .latents_grid_views(x)$word), legend = TRUE) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank())
}

before.documentation:
#' Refit a model under several seeds
#'
#' Refits the model under each of several random seeds and returns one row
#' per seed with the maximised log likelihood, convergence, which distinct
#' optimum the refit reached, and the proportion of observations assigned to
#' the same profile as in the reference fit. Profile labels of each refit are
#' matched to the reference fit's before agreement is computed.
#'
#' A fit's own replication count describes only the starts within one seed's
#' random-number stream; refitting under other seeds shows whether other
#' streams reach the same maximum and the same classification.
#'
#' A seed whose refit fails gives a row with `NA` estimates, and a
#' `latents_sensitivity_dropped` warning reports how many seeds failed.
#'
#' @param x The reference fit: a [multilpa()] model, an [lta()] model, or a
#'   growth mixture ([mixture_regression()] with `random`). A [fit_staged()]
#'   result varies the second-stage starts while holding its first-stage
#'   measurement solution fixed. A directly fitted model with measurement
#'   blocks held fixed is refused (`latents_unsupported_sensitivity`), because
#'   its original free starting values are not retained. A
#'   membership-covariate fit is refused with
#'   `latents_unsupported_sensitivity`. For an [lta()] fit, `agreement` is the
#'   share of occasions given the same profile, after matching the refit's
#'   profiles on the measurement; for a growth mixture it is the share of
#'   persons given the same class, after matching the refit's classes by
#'   their posterior memberships of the fitted persons.
#' @param data Optional for a [multilpa()] fit or a growth mixture, which
#'   carry the columns they were built from. Required for an [lta()] fit
#'   (`latents_bad_argument` otherwise). It must be the data the model was
#'   fitted to, in its original row order; shared identifier and indicator
#'   columns are checked against the fit (`latents_bad_inference_data`).
#' @param seeds Seeds to refit under: at least two distinct whole numbers
#'   that `set.seed()` accepts. Default `1:10`. Anything else raises
#'   `latents_bad_argument`. If the reference fit's own seed is included, that
#'   row reproduces the reference fit.
#' @param n_starts Starts per refit. Defaults to the number the reference fit
#'   used.
#' @param max_iter,tol Passed to each refit. Default to the reference fit's
#'   (for an [lta()] fit, to the defaults of [lta()]).
#' @param tolerance Two log likelihoods within this of each other count as
#'   the same optimum. Defaults to the reference fit's replication tolerance
#'   (for a growth mixture, `1e-6 * (1 + abs(logLik))`).
#' @return A base `data.frame`, one row per seed, with columns `seed`,
#'   `log_likelihood`, `converged`, `iterations`, `optimum` (1 for the best
#'   maximum found across the seeds, 2 for the next distinct one, and so on),
#'   `best` (whether this seed reached optimum 1) and `agreement` (the
#'   proportion of observations given the same profile as the reference fit,
#'   after label matching). A failed refit has `NA` in every column except
#'   `seed`.
#' @seealso [enumerate_classes()] to vary the number of classes, and
#'   [parameter_inference()] for uncertainty about the parameters of a single
#'   solution.
#' @references Hipp, J. R., & Bauer, D. J. (2006). Local solutions in the
#'   estimation of growth mixture models. *Psychological Methods, 11*, 36--53.
#' @examples
#' set.seed(7)
#' example_data <- data.frame(
#'   school = rep(seq_len(12), each = 10),
#'   score_a = c(rnorm(60, -1.5), rnorm(60, 1.5)),
#'   score_b = c(rnorm(60, -1), rnorm(60, 1))
#' )
#' fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
#'                 n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
#' sensitivity(fit, seeds = 1:3, n_starts = 3)
#'
#' # Growth mixtures are known for local solutions (Hipp and Bauer 2006).
#' growth <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, data = subset(growth_scores, student <= 60),
#'                              n_classes = 2, id = "student", class_level = "group",
#'                              random = ~ 1, n_starts = 1, seed = 1)
#' sensitivity(growth, seeds = 1:2)
#' @export
before.terminal_expression: data.frame(seed = as.integer(seeds), log_likelihood = likelihood, converged = converged, iterations = iterations, optimum = optimum, best = optimum == 1L, agreement = agreement, row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

before.documentation:
#' How sensitivity() refits a growth mixture and compares its assignments
#'
#' Persons' modal classes are compared after the refit's classes are matched
#' to the reference's by their posterior memberships of the fitted persons.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.sensitivity_growth <- function(x, data, n_starts, max_iter, tol) {
  if (!is.null(data)) .trajectory_check_data(x, data)
  spec <- x$spec
  frame <- spec$model_data
  weight_column <- NULL
  if (.latents_is_weighted(x)) {
    weight_column <- ".latents_sensitivity_weight"
    frame[[weight_column]] <- spec$sampling_weights[spec$group_index]
  }
  arguments <- c(.growth_refit_arguments(x, weight_column),
                 list(n_starts = as.integer(n_starts %||% x$settings$n_starts),
                      max_iter = max_iter %||% x$settings$max_iter,
                      tol = tol %||% x$settings$tol))
  reference <- max.col(x$expectation$posterior, ties.method = "first")
  list(
    refit = function(seed) do.call(mixture_regression,
                                   c(list(data = frame), arguments, list(seed = seed))),
    agreement = function(fit) {
      matched <- .growth_match_classes(x, fit)
      mean(match(max.col(matched$posterior, ties.method = "first"), matched$order) ==
             reference)
    },
    tolerance = 1e-6 * (1 + abs(x$log_likelihood)))
}

.multilpa_optimum_index.name: .multilpa_optimum_index

before.name: .multilpa_optimum_index
before.documentation:
#' Number the distinct maxima a set of log likelihoods reached
#'
#' Sorted from the best downwards, a new optimum begins wherever the drop from
#' the previous one exceeds `tolerance`. Comparing the likelihoods pairwise
#' would not do: `==` on doubles is never right here, and a chain of values each
#' within tolerance of the last is one basin, not several.
#'
#' @param likelihood Maximised log likelihoods, possibly with `NA`.
#' @param tolerance Two values within this count as the same optimum.
#' @return An integer vector the same length as `likelihood`; `1` is the best
#'   maximum, and a failed fit is `NA`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_optimum_index <- function(likelihood, tolerance) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(likelihood),
            length(tolerance) == 1L, is.finite(tolerance), tolerance > 0)
  index <- rep(NA_integer_, length(likelihood))
  observed <- which(!is.na(likelihood))
  if (length(observed) == 0L) return(index)
  ranked <- observed[order(likelihood[observed], decreasing = TRUE)]
  values <- likelihood[ranked]
  index[ranked] <- cumsum(c(1L, as.integer(diff(values) < -tolerance)))
  index
}

before.name: .multilpa_sequences
before.documentation:
#' Profile assignments in occasion order
#'
#' Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.
#'
#' @param x A fitted model of this package, fitted with `time =`.
#' @param format `"long"` for one row per observation, `"wide"` for one row per
#'   group with one column per occasion.
#' @return A base `data.frame`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_sequences <- function(x, format = c("long", "wide")) {
  time_values <- .multilpa_require_time(x)
  format <- match.arg(format)
  long <- data.frame(
    group = x$group_values[x$group_index],
    group_class = x$group_classes[x$group_index],
    time = time_values,
    profile = x$subject_profiles,
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  long <- long[order(long$group, long$time), , drop = FALSE]
  row.names(long) <- NULL
  if (identical(format, "long")) return(long)

  cells <- .multilpa_sequence_matrix(x, long)
  groups <- unique(long$group)
  occasions <- as.data.frame(lapply(seq_len(ncol(cells)), function(column) {
    factor(cells[, column], levels = c(if (isTRUE(x$noise)) 0L,
                                      seq_len(x$n_profiles)))
  }), optional = TRUE)
  names(occasions) <- colnames(cells)
  # The group identifier is a column, not a row name: row names coerce to
  # character and would silently merge two groups that print alike.
  data.frame(
    group = groups,
    group_class = x$group_classes[match(groups, x$group_values)],
    occasions,
    row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
}

.multilpa_sequence_summary.name: .multilpa_sequence_summary

before.name: .multilpa_sequence_summary
before.documentation:
#' How much data each group class contributes
#'
#' Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.
#'
#' @param x A fitted model of this package, fitted with `time =`.
#' @return A base `data.frame`, one row per group class, including any class no
#'   group was assigned to.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_sequence_summary <- function(x) {
  time_values <- .multilpa_require_time(x)
  positions <- sort(unique(time_values))
  n_positions <- length(positions)
  # Native integer indices avoid unused factor levels and character rounding of
  # distinct numeric group identifiers in tapply().
  lengths_by_group <- tabulate(x$group_index, nbins = x$n_groups)
  position_index <- match(time_values, positions)
  first <- as.integer(tapply(position_index, x$group_index, min))
  last <- as.integer(tapply(position_index, x$group_index, max))
  # A group whose observations fall short of its own span skipped a position
  # inside it; a group that simply stopped early does not count as a gap.
  has_gap <- lengths_by_group < (last - first + 1L)
  class_by_group <- x$group_classes
  classes <- seq_len(x$n_group_classes)
  summarize <- function(class) {
    in_class <- class_by_group == class
    taken <- lengths_by_group[in_class]
    data.frame(
      group_class = class,
      groups = length(taken),
      observations = sum(taken),
      mean_length = if (length(taken)) mean(taken) else NA_real_,
      median_length = if (length(taken)) stats::median(taken) else NA_real_,
      shortest = if (length(taken)) min(taken) else NA_integer_,
      longest = if (length(taken)) max(taken) else NA_integer_,
      complete = sum(taken == n_positions),
      gaps = sum(has_gap[in_class]),

after.documentation:
#' How much data each group class contributes
#'
#' Documented on `?get_results`, which is where a caller reaches this table from.
#'
#' @param x A fitted model of this package, fitted with `time =`.
#' @return A base `data.frame`, one row per group class, including any class no
#'   group was assigned to.
#' @noRd
after.source:
.multilpa_sequence_summary <- function(x) {
  time_values <- .multilpa_require_time(x)
  positions <- sort(unique(time_values))
  n_positions <- length(positions)
  # Native integer indices avoid unused factor levels and character rounding of
  # distinct numeric group identifiers in tapply().
  lengths_by_group <- tabulate(x$group_index, nbins = x$n_groups)
  position_index <- match(time_values, positions)
  first <- as.integer(tapply(position_index, x$group_index, min))
  last <- as.integer(tapply(position_index, x$group_index, max))
  # A group whose observations fall short of its own span skipped a position
  # inside it; a group that simply stopped early does not count as a gap.
  has_gap <- lengths_by_group < (last - first + 1L)
  class_by_group <- x$group_classes
  classes <- seq_len(x$n_group_classes)
  summarize <- function(class) {
    in_class <- class_by_group == class
    taken <- lengths_by_group[in_class]
    data.frame(
      group_class = class,
      groups = length(taken),
      observations = sum(taken),
      mean_length = if (length(taken)) mean(taken) else NA_real_,
      median_length = if (length(taken)) stats::median(taken) else NA_real_,
      shortest = if (length(taken)) min(taken) else NA_integer_,
      longest = if (length(taken)) max(taken) else NA_integer_,
      complete = sum(taken == n_positions),
      gaps = sum(has_gap[in_class]),
      row.names = NULL
    )
  }
  do.call(rbind, lapply(classes, summarize))
}

#' Set a seed for the calling function and restore the random state on its
#' exit
#'
#' Seeded verbs must not leave the caller's random stream changed: a user who

#' get the draw they would have got without the fit. The previous

#' by an error; when there was none, the one `set.seed()` created is removed,

#' same point as before.

#' Draw one category per row from a matrix of row-wise probabilities
#'
#' Inverse-CDF sampling in one pass, one uniform per row: the category is the
#' first whose cumulative probability reaches the uniform. The last cumulative
#' probability is set to exactly one, so that a rounding shortfall (a row
#' summing to slightly less than one, as exponentiated log probabilities do)
#' cannot leave a uniform above every cumulative total; it falls in the last
#' category, not past it, and not back to the first.
#'
#' A one-column matrix still consumes one uniform per row, so a model with a
#' single class draws the same stream as one with several.
#'
#' @param probabilities Matrix whose rows each sum to one.

before.documentation:
#' One resample of the groups, as a data frame
#'
#' A group drawn twice has to become two groups, or the refit would pool the two
#' copies into one unit and the resample would carry fewer groups than it drew.
#'
#' @param data The fitting data.
#' @param rows_by_group Row indices of each group, in group order.
#' @param id The group column's name.
#' @param drawn Which groups were drawn, with replacement.
#' @return A data frame with one relabelled group per draw.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(data, rows_by_group, id, drawn) {
    stopifnot(is.data.frame(data), is.list(rows_by_group), is.character(id), length(id) == 1L)
    taken <- rows_by_group[drawn]
    resampled <- data[unlist(taken, use.names = FALSE), , drop = FALSE]
    resampled[[id]] <- rep(seq_along(drawn), lengths(taken))
    row.names(resampled) <- NULL
    resampled
}

.latents_pool_phase <- function(tasks, costs, cores, n_candidates,
                                  execute, on_lost = NULL) {
  candidate <- vapply(tasks, `[[`, integer(1), "candidate")
  results <- if (length(tasks)) .latents_map_candidates(
    tasks, execute, cores, costs = costs[candidate], signal = FALSE,
    on_lost = on_lost) else list()
  lapply(seq_len(n_candidates), function(i) results[candidate == i])

.multilpa_chart <- function(structure, k, d) {
  stopifnot(
    "`structure` must be a constrained structure" =
      length(structure) == 1L && structure %in% .multilpa_structures() &&
      !structure %in% .multilpa_separable_structures(),
    "`k` must be a positive whole number" = length(k) == 1L && k >= 1,
    "`d` must be a positive whole number" = length(d) == 1L && d >= 1)
  second <- substr(structure, 2L, 2L)
  third <- substr(structure, 3L, 3L)
  form <- if (structure %in% c("EII", "VII")) "spherical" else
    if (third == "I") "diagonal" else
      if (second == third) "cholesky" else "rotation"
  volume_shared <- startsWith(structure, "E")
  shape_shared <- second == "E"
  rotation_shared <- third == "E"
  map <- function(shared) if (shared) rep(1L, k) else seq_len(k)
  shape_rows <- if (form == "spherical") 0L else if (shape_shared) 1L else k
  rotation_rows <- if (form == "rotation") {
    if (rotation_shared) 1L else k
  } else 0L
  per_shape <- switch(form, spherical = 0L, diagonal = d - 1L, rotation = d - 1L,
                      cholesky = d * (d + 1L) / 2L - 1L)
  per_rotation <- d * (d - 1L) / 2L
  widths <- c(volume = if (volume_shared) 1L else k,
              shape = shape_rows * per_shape,
              rotation = rotation_rows * per_rotation)
  list(structure = structure, form = form, k = k, d = d,
       volume_shared = volume_shared, shape_shared = shape_shared,
       rotation_shared = rotation_shared,
       volume_of = map(volume_shared), shape_of = map(shape_shared),
       rotation_of = map(rotation_shared),
       shape_rows = shape_rows, rotation_rows = rotation_rows,
       per_shape = as.integer(per_shape), per_rotation = as.integer(per_rotation),
       widths = widths,
       offsets = stats::setNames(cumsum(c(0L, widths))[seq_len(3L)], names(widths)),
       width = as.integer(sum(widths)))
}

.multilpa_profile_gradients.name: .multilpa_profile_gradients

before.name: .multilpa_profile_gradients
before.documentation:
#' Gradients of the log likelihood with respect to each profile's covariance
#'
#' By Fisher's identity the observed-data score is the conditional expectation
#' of the complete-data score, so with missing indicators the scatter carries
#' the conditional covariance of what was not observed. The gradient with
#' respect to an unconstrained symmetric `Sigma_k` is `(P S P - w P) / 2`.
#'
#' @param parameters Decoded parameters.
#' @param expectation The expectation step at those parameters.
#' @param x The centred indicator matrix.
#' @param group_index Group indices, or `NULL` for pooled totals.
#' @return A list with `means` (groups, or one row, by profiles-times-indicators)
#'   and `covariance`, one groups-by-`d^2` matrix per profile.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_profile_gradients <- function(parameters, expectation, x,
                                        group_index = NULL) {
  d <- ncol(x)
  k <- nrow(parameters$means)
  index <- group_index %||% rep(1L, nrow(x))
  pairs <- expand.grid(row = seq_len(d), column = seq_len(d))
  pieces <- lapply(seq_len(k), function(profile) {
    covariance <- if (is.null(parameters$covariances)) {
      diag(parameters$variances[profile, ], d)
    } else matrix(parameters$covariances[, , profile], d, d)
    precision <- chol2inv(chol(covariance))
    weights <- expectation$subject_posteriors[, profile]
    moments <- expectation$gaussian_moments[[profile]]
    expected <- if (is.null(moments)) x else moments$expected
    residuals <- sweep(expected, 2L, parameters$means[profile, ], "-")
    weighted <- residuals * weights
    scatter <- rowsum(residuals[, pairs$row, drop = FALSE] *
                        weighted[, pairs$column, drop = FALSE],
                      index, reorder = FALSE)
    adjustments <- if (is.null(moments)) list() else moments$adjustments
    if (length(adjustments) > 0L) {
      scatter <- scatter + Reduce(`+`, lapply(adjustments, function(adjustment) {
        share <- numeric(length(weights))
        share[adjustment$rows] <- weights[adjustment$rows]
        outer(as.vector(rowsum(share, index, reorder = FALSE)),
              as.vector(adjustment$covariance))
      }))
    }
    group_weight <- as.vector(rowsum(weights, index, reorder = FALSE))
    list(means = rowsum(weighted, index, reorder = FALSE) %*% precision,
         covariance = 0.5 * (scatter %*% kronecker(precision, precision) -
                               outer(group_weight, as.vector(precision))))
  })
  list(means = do.call(cbind, lapply(pieces, `[[`, "means")),
       covariance = lapply(pieces, `[[`, "covariance"))
}

.multilpa_step_ml_fit.name: .multilpa_step_ml_fit

before.name: .multilpa_step_ml_fit
before.documentation:
#' Fit the step-three model of a continuous distal outcome
#'
#' @param pieces The list from `.multilpa_level_assignments()` (or the
#'   trajectory equivalent): `posteriors`, `modal`, `n_classes`.
#' @param values The outcome, one value per unit.
#' @param variance `"varying"` (a variance per class) or `"equal"`.
#' @param tol Relative change in the log likelihood at which EM stops.
#' @param max_iter Maximum number of EM iterations.
#' @return A list: `means`, `variances` (one per class), `responsibilities`
#'   (units by classes), `log_likelihood`, `converged`, `iterations`, and the
#'   fixed `weights` (units by classes: the prior times the probability of the
#'   unit's assigned class).
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_step_ml_fit <- function(pieces, values, variance, tol = 1e-12,
                                  max_iter = 5000L) {
  stopifnot("`variance` must be \"varying\" or \"equal\"" =
              variance %in% c("varying", "equal"))
  if (stats::var(values) <= 0) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "The outcome takes one value, so it has no distribution to estimate by class.",
      class = "latents_bad_outcome", call = NULL))
  }
  # Fit and differentiate in a chart whose origin and units are determined
  # by the outcome spread. A finite-difference step around a raw mean near
  # 1e12 can round to zero even though the outcome varies by whole units.
  outcome_center <- mean(values)
  outcome_scale <- stats::sd(values)
  values <- (values - outcome_center) / outcome_scale
  errors <- .multilpa_error_matrix(pieces)
  prior <- colMeans(pieces$posteriors)
  # Each unit's fixed weight on each class: the class's share times the
  # probability that a unit of that class is assigned where this one was.
  weights <- t(errors[, pieces$modal, drop = FALSE]) *
    matrix(prior, length(values), pieces$n_classes, byrow = TRUE)
  log_weights <- log(weights)
  smallest <- 1e-10 * stats::var(values)
  moments <- function(responsibilities, means) {
    squares <- (values - matrix(means, length(values), length(means), byrow = TRUE))^2
    by_class <- colSums(responsibilities * squares)
    if (identical(variance, "equal")) {
      rep(sum(by_class) / length(values), length(means))
    } else by_class / colSums(responsibilities)
  }
  e_step <- function(means, variances) {
    log_density <- vapply(seq_along(means), function(class) {
      stats::dnorm(values, means[class], sqrt(variances[class]), log = TRUE)
    }, numeric(length(values)))
    joint <- log_weights + log_density
    largest <- apply(joint, 1L, max)
    log_marginal <- largest + log(rowSums(exp(joint - largest)))
    list(responsibilities = exp(joint - log_marginal),
         log_likelihood = sum(log_marginal))
  }
  run <- function(means, variances) {
    state <- e_step(means, variances)
    converged <- FALSE
    failed <- FALSE
    iterations <- 0L
    # EM is iterative by nature: each step needs the previous one's estimates,
    # so this loop cannot be vectorised.
    while (iterations < max_iter) {
      iterations <- iterations + 1L
      responsibilities <- state$responsibilities
      # A start that leaves a class with no weight has no estimate for it;
      # the start is dropped rather than carried on with an undefined mean.
      if (!all(colSums(responsibilities) > 0)) {
        failed <- TRUE
        break
      }
      means <- as.vector(crossprod(responsibilities, values)) / colSums(responsibilities)
      variances <- pmax(moments(responsibilities, means), smallest)
      updated <- e_step(means, variances)
      if (!is.finite(updated$log_likelihood)) {
        failed <- TRUE
        break
      }
      change <- abs(updated$log_likelihood - state$log_likelihood)
      state <- updated
      if (change <= tol * (1 + abs(state$log_likelihood))) {
        converged <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
    list(means = unname(means), variances = unname(variances),
         responsibilities = state$responsibilities,
         log_likelihood = state$log_likelihood, converged = converged,
         iterations = iterations, weights = weights, failed = failed,
         at_floor = !failed && any(variances <= smallest * (1 + 1e-8)))
  }
  # The step-three likelihood can have several maxima (a heavy-tailed or
  # skewed outcome lets one class absorb the tail), so EM runs from a fixed,
  # non-random set of starts: the proportional (posterior-weighted) moments,
  # Latent GOLD's start, first; then the modal-class means; then the class
  # means at the outcome's quantiles in every order (every cyclic order, both
  # ways, above five classes), from the outcome's own variance and from the
  # proportional spread; then the seeded draws below.
  proportional <- as.vector(crossprod(pieces$posteriors, values)) / colSums(pieces$posteriors)
  spread <- pmax(moments(pieces$posteriors, proportional), smallest)
  modal <- vapply(seq_len(pieces$n_classes), function(class) {
    members <- pieces$modal == class
    if (any(members)) mean(values[members]) else proportional[class]
  }, numeric(1))
  k <- pieces$n_classes
  quantiles <- stats::quantile(values, (seq_len(k) - 0.5) / k, names = FALSE)
  orders <- if (k <= 5L) .multilpa_permutations(k) else {
    shifts <- t(vapply(seq_len(k) - 1L, function(shift) (seq_len(k) + shift - 1L) %% k + 1L,
                       integer(k)))
    rbind(shifts, shifts[, rev(seq_len(k)), drop = FALSE])
  }
  placed <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(orders)), function(row) quantiles[orders[row, ]])
  # A heavy tail can be the likelihood's best class: each class in turn starts
  # at the mean of the outcome's top and bottom 2%, the others proportional.
  tails <- c(mean(values[values >= stats::quantile(values, 0.98)]),
             mean(values[values <= stats::quantile(values, 0.02)]))
  tailed <- do.call(c, lapply(tails, function(tail) lapply(seq_len(k), function(class) {
    replace(proportional, class, tail)
  })))
  # Twenty more starts at random quantiles with random standard deviations
  # (0.3 to 1 of the outcome's) reach basins the ordered placements miss.
  # They are drawn from a fixed seed in a local stream, so the result is the
  # same whatever the caller's seed and the caller's stream is untouched.
  drawn <- (function() {
    .latents_local_seed(20261021L)
    lapply(seq_len(20L), function(draw) {
      sds <- if (identical(variance, "equal")) rep(stats::runif(1L, 0.3, 1), k) else
        stats::runif(k, 0.3, 1)
      list(means = stats::quantile(values, stats::runif(k), names = FALSE),
           variances = sds^2)
    })
  })()
  # A start keeps only its estimates, not its observations-by-classes
  # responsibilities: with five classes there are 272 starts. The winner's
  # are recomputed below from its own estimates, by the same E-step.
  slim <- function(means, variances) {
    attempt <- run(means, variances)
    attempt$responsibilities <- NULL
    attempt
  }
  runs <- c(lapply(c(list(proportional, modal), tailed), slim, variances = spread),
            lapply(placed, slim, variances = rep(1, k)),
            lapply(placed, slim, variances = spread),
            lapply(drawn, function(start) slim(start$means, start$variances)))
  failed <- vapply(runs, `[[`, logical(1), "failed")
  if (all(failed)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "Every start of the step-three model left a class without weight; the",
      "class means are not identified."),
      class = "latents_singular_information", call = NULL))
  }
  scores <- vapply(runs, function(attempt) {
    if (attempt$failed || attempt$at_floor) -Inf else attempt$log_likelihood
  }, numeric(1))
  # A later start replaces the first only when it is clearly higher, so a
  # likelihood with one maximum keeps Latent GOLD's solution exactly. When
  # every start ends at the variance floor, the first that ran is kept.
  best <- if (all(is.infinite(scores))) which(!failed)[1L] else {
    top <- max(scores)
    which(scores >= top - 1e-10 * (1 + abs(top)))[1L]
  }
  fit <- runs[[best]]
  fit$responsibilities <- e_step(fit$means, fit$variances)$responsibilities
  if (!fit$at_floor) fit <- .multilpa_step_ml_polish(fit, values, variance)
  # Keep the conditioned means for inference: subtracting the origin from
  # already rounded reported means would throw away the precision just saved.
  fit$outcome_coordinates <- list(center = outcome_center, scale = outcome_scale,
                                  means = fit$means)
  fit$means <- outcome_center + outcome_scale * fit$means
  fit$variances <- outcome_scale^2 * fit$variances
  fit$log_likelihood <- fit$log_likelihood - length(values) * log(outcome_scale)
  fit
}

#' Fit the step-three model of a continuous distal outcome
#'
#' @param pieces The list from `.multilpa_level_assignments()` (or the
#'   trajectory equivalent): `posteriors`, `modal`, `n_classes`.
#' @param values The outcome, one value per unit.
#' @param variance `"varying"` (a variance per class) or `"equal"`.
#' @param tol Relative change in the log likelihood at which EM stops.
#' @param max_iter Maximum number of EM iterations.
#' @return A list: `means`, `variances` (one per class), `responsibilities`
#'   (units by classes), `log_likelihood`, `converged`, `iterations`, and the
#'   fixed `weights` (units by classes: the prior times the probability of the
#'   unit's assigned class).
#' @noRd
after.source:
.multilpa_step_ml_fit <- function(pieces, values, variance, tol = 1e-12,
                                  max_iter = 5000L) {
  stopifnot("`variance` must be \"varying\" or \"equal\"" =
              variance %in% c("varying", "equal"))
  if (stats::var(values) <= 0) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "The outcome takes one value, so it has no distribution to estimate by class.",
      class = "latents_bad_outcome", call = NULL))
  }
  # Fit and differentiate in a chart whose origin and units are determined
  # by the outcome spread. A finite-difference step around a raw mean near
  # 1e12 can round to zero even though the outcome varies by whole units.
  outcome_center <- mean(values)
  outcome_scale <- stats::sd(values)
  values <- (values - outcome_center) / outcome_scale
  errors <- .multilpa_error_matrix(pieces)
  prior <- colMeans(pieces$posteriors)
  # Each unit's fixed weight on each class: the class's share times the
  # probability that a unit of that class is assigned where this one was.
  weights <- t(errors[, pieces$modal, drop = FALSE]) *
    matrix(prior, length(values), pieces$n_classes, byrow = TRUE)
  log_weights <- log(weights)
  smallest <- 1e-10 * stats::var(values)
  moments <- function(responsibilities, means) {
    squares <- (values - matrix(means, length(values), length(means), byrow = TRUE))^2
    by_class <- colSums(responsibilities * squares)
    if (identical(variance, "equal")) {
      rep(sum(by_class) / length(values), length(means))
    } else by_class / colSums(responsibilities)
  }
  e_step <- function(means, variances) {
    log_density <- vapply(seq_along(means), function(class) {
      stats::dnorm(values, means[class], sqrt(variances[class]), log = TRUE)
    }, numeric(length(values)))
    joint <- log_weights + log_density
    largest <- apply(joint, 1L, max)
    log_marginal <- largest + log(rowSums(exp(joint - largest)))
    list(responsibilities = exp(joint - log_marginal),
         log_likelihood = sum(log_marginal))
  }
  run <- function(means, variances) {
    state <- e_step(means, variances)
    converged <- FALSE
    failed <- FALSE
    iterations <- 0L
    # EM is iterative by nature: each step needs the previous one's estimates,
    # so this loop cannot be vectorised.
    while (iterations < max_iter) {
      iterations <- iterations + 1L
      responsibilities <- state$responsibilities
      # A start that leaves a class with no weight has no estimate for it;
      # the start is dropped rather than carried on with an undefined mean.
      if (!all(colSums(responsibilities) > 0)) {
        failed <- TRUE
        break
      }
      means <- as.vector(crossprod(responsibilities, values)) / colSums(responsibilities)
      variances <- pmax(moments(responsibilities, means), smallest)
      updated <- e_step(means, variances)
      if (!is.finite(updated$log_likelihood)) {
        failed <- TRUE
        break
      }
      change <- abs(updated$log_likelihood - state$log_likelihood)
      state <- updated
      if (change <= tol * (1 + abs(state$log_likelihood))) {
        converged <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
    list(means = unname(means), variances = unname(variances),
         responsibilities = state$responsibilities,
         log_likelihood = state$log_likelihood, converged = converged,
         iterations = iterations, weights = weights, failed = failed,
         at_floor = !failed && any(variances <= smallest * (1 + 1e-8)))
  }
  # The step-three likelihood can have several maxima (a heavy-tailed or
  # skewed outcome lets one class absorb the tail), so EM runs from a fixed,
  # reproducible set of starts: the proportional (posterior-weighted) moments,
  # Latent GOLD's start, first; then the modal-class means; then the class
  # means at the outcome's quantiles in every order (every cyclic order, both
  # ways, above five classes), from the outcome's own variance and from the
  # proportional spread; then the seeded draws below. The equal-variance
  # model also tries quasi-Newton optimization from the quantile placements.
  proportional <- as.vector(crossprod(pieces$posteriors, values)) / colSums(pieces$posteriors)
  spread <- pmax(moments(pieces$posteriors, proportional), smallest)
  modal <- vapply(seq_len(pieces$n_classes), function(class) {
    members <- pieces$modal == class
    if (any(members)) mean(values[members]) else proportional[class]
  }, numeric(1))
  k <- pieces$n_classes
  quantiles <- stats::quantile(values, (seq_len(k) - 0.5) / k, names = FALSE)
  orders <- if (k <= 5L) .multilpa_permutations(k) else {
    shifts <- t(vapply(seq_len(k) - 1L, function(shift) (seq_len(k) + shift - 1L) %% k + 1L,
                       integer(k)))
    rbind(shifts, shifts[, rev(seq_len(k)), drop = FALSE])
  }
  placed <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(orders)), function(row) quantiles[orders[row, ]])
  # A heavy tail can be the likelihood's best class: each class in turn starts
  # at the mean of the outcome's top and bottom 2%, the others proportional.
  tails <- c(mean(values[values >= stats::quantile(values, 0.98)]),
             mean(values[values <= stats::quantile(values, 0.02)]))
  tailed <- do.call(c, lapply(tails, function(tail) lapply(seq_len(k), function(class) {
    replace(proportional, class, tail)
  })))
  # Twenty more starts at random quantiles with random standard deviations
  # (0.3 to 1 of the outcome's) reach basins the ordered placements miss.
  # They are drawn from a fixed seed in a local stream, so the result is the
  # same whatever the caller's seed and the caller's .Random.seed is restored
  # (with the Box-Muller cache limitation documented by the seed service).
  drawn <- (function() {
    .latents_local_seed(20261021L)
    lapply(seq_len(20L), function(draw) {
      sds <- if (identical(variance, "equal")) rep(stats::runif(1L, 0.3, 1), k) else
        stats::runif(k, 0.3, 1)
      list(means = stats::quantile(values, stats::runif(k), names = FALSE),
           variances = sds^2)
    })
  })()
  # A start keeps only its estimates, not its observations-by-classes
  # responsibilities: with five classes there are 272 starts. The winner's
  # are recomputed below from its own estimates, by the same E-step.
  slim <- function(means, variances) {
    attempt <- run(means, variances)
    attempt$responsibilities <- NULL
    attempt
  }
  runs <- c(lapply(c(list(proportional, modal), tailed), slim, variances = spread),
            lapply(placed, slim, variances = rep(1, k)),
            lapply(placed, slim, variances = spread),
            lapply(drawn, function(start) slim(start$means, start$variances)))
  if (identical(variance, "equal")) {
    # EM and quasi-Newton iterations can enter different basins from the
    # same mean placement. For the shared-variance model, also optimize the
    # existing quantile starts directly. The chart variance = floor + exp(2a)
    # enforces the same lower bound as EM without changing the likelihood.
    template <- list(means = numeric(k), variances = rep(1, k), weights = weights)
    log_floor <- log(smallest)
    decode <- function(point) {
      log_excess <- 2 * point[k + 1L]
      log_variance <- max(log_floor, log_excess) +
        log1p(exp(-abs(log_floor - log_excess)))
      c(point[seq_len(k)], log_variance / 2)
    }
    objective <- function(point) {
      -.multilpa_step_ml_log_likelihood(template, values, variance, decode(point))
    }
    gradient <- function(point) {
      decoded <- decode(point)
      score <- -colSums(.multilpa_step_ml_scores(template, values, variance, decoded))
      score[k + 1L] <- score[k + 1L] * exp(2 * point[k + 1L] - 2 * decoded[k + 1L])
      score
    }
    optimized <- lapply(placed, function(means) tryCatch({
      start <- c(means, log(1 - smallest) / 2)
      found <- stats::optim(start, objective, gradient, method = "BFGS",
                            control = list(maxit = max_iter, reltol = 1e-15))
      if (!identical(found$convergence, 0L) || !is.finite(found$value) ||
          any(!is.finite(found$par))) return(NULL)
      point <- decode(found$par)
      candidate <- template
      candidate$means <- point[seq_len(k)]
      candidate$variances <- rep(exp(2 * point[k + 1L]), k)
      if (any(candidate$variances <= smallest * (1 + 1e-8))) return(NULL)
      scale <- .multilpa_step_ml_scale(candidate, variance)
      score <- colSums(.multilpa_step_ml_scores(candidate, values, variance, point))
      if (any(!is.finite(score)) || max(abs(score * scale)) >
          sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) * (1 + length(values))) return(NULL)
      information <- .multilpa_step_ml_hessian(function(theta) {
        -colSums(.multilpa_step_ml_scores(candidate, values, variance, theta))
      }, point, scale)
      chol(information * tcrossprod(scale))
      slim(candidate$means, candidate$variances)
    }, error = function(condition) NULL))
    # Appending preserves the original EM winner whenever the likelihoods
    # are tied under the existing selection rule below.
    runs <- c(runs, Filter(Negate(is.null), optimized))
  }
  failed <- vapply(runs, `[[`, logical(1), "failed")
  if (all(failed)) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "Every start of the step-three model left a class without weight; the",
      "class means are not identified."),
      class = "latents_singular_information", call = NULL))
  }
  scores <- vapply(runs, function(attempt) {
    if (attempt$failed || attempt$at_floor) -Inf else attempt$log_likelihood
  }, numeric(1))
  # A later start replaces the first only when it is clearly higher, so a
  # likelihood with one maximum keeps Latent GOLD's solution exactly. When
  # every start ends at the variance floor, the first that ran is kept.
  best <- if (all(is.infinite(scores))) which(!failed)[1L] else {
    top <- max(scores)
    which(scores >= top - 1e-10 * (1 + abs(top)))[1L]
  }
  fit <- runs[[best]]
  fit$responsibilities <- e_step(fit$means, fit$variances)$responsibilities
  if (!fit$at_floor) fit <- .multilpa_step_ml_polish(fit, values, variance)
  # Keep the conditioned means for inference: subtracting the origin from
  # already rounded reported means would throw away the precision just saved.
  fit$outcome_coordinates <- list(center = outcome_center, scale = outcome_scale,
                                  means = fit$means)
  fit$means <- outcome_center + outcome_scale * fit$means
  fit$variances <- outcome_scale^2 * fit$variances
  fit$log_likelihood <- fit$log_likelihood - length(values) * log(outcome_scale)
  fit
}

#' Coordinates: the class means, then the log standard deviations (one per
#' class, or one shared).
#' @param fit From `.multilpa_step_ml_fit()`.
#' @param values The outcome.
#' @param variance `"varying"` or `"equal"`.
#' @param parameters Optional coordinates at which to evaluate; the fit's own
#'   by default.
#' @return A units-by-coordinates matrix.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(fit, values, variance, parameters = NULL) {
    classes <- length(fit$means)
    parameters <- parameters %||% .multilpa_step_ml_coordinates(fit, variance)
    means <- parameters[seq_len(classes)]
    sds <- exp(parameters[-seq_len(classes)])
    sds <- if (identical(variance, "equal")) 
        rep(sds, classes)
    else sds
    log_density <- vapply(seq_len(classes), function(class) {
        stats::dnorm(values, means[class], sds[class], log = TRUE)
    }, numeric(length(values)))
    joint <- log(fit$weights) + log_density
    largest <- apply(joint, 1L, max)
    responsibilities <- exp(joint - largest - log(rowSums(exp(joint - largest))))
    residuals <- values - matrix(means, length(values), classes, byrow = TRUE)
    scaled <- residuals/matrix(sds, length(values), classes, byrow = TRUE)
    mean_scores <- responsibilities * scaled/matrix(sds, length(values), classes, byrow = TRUE)
    sd_scores <- responsibilities * (scaled^2 - 1)
    if (identical(variance, "equal")) 
        sd_scores <- matrix(rowSums(sd_scores), ncol = 1L)
    unname(cbind(mean_scores, sd_scores))
}

before.name: .multilpa_step_ml_hessian
before.documentation:
#' The Hessian of the step-three objective from its analytic gradient
#'
#' Central differences of the gradient, each coordinate stepped by a fixed
#' fraction of its own scale, then symmetrized. `stats::optimHess()` steps by
#' 1e-3 in the coordinates' units, which on an outcome measured in units of
#' 1e-4 is wider than the curvature it measures (an information of 0.15 for
#' 365, and standard errors 3000 times too large); with `parscale` it was
#' still wrong.

before.name: .multilpa_three_step_ml
before.formal_defaults: as.pairlist(alist(pieces = , values = , level = , variance = , ci_level = , contrast = , adjust = , vcov_type = ))
before.documentation:
#' The ML three-step table of a distal outcome
#'
#' @param pieces,values The units' assignments and outcome values.
#' @param level,variance,ci_level,contrast,adjust,vcov_type As in
#'   [three_step()].
#' @return The table [three_step()] returns.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.multilpa_three_step_ml <- function(pieces, values, level, variance, ci_level,
                                    contrast, adjust, vcov_type) {
  fit <- .multilpa_step_ml_fit(pieces, values, variance)
  if (!fit$converged) {
    warning(warningCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "The step-three model did not converge in %d iterations, so its class",
      "means are not a maximum."), fit$iterations),
      class = "latents_unconverged", call = NULL))
  }
  if (fit$at_floor) {
    warning(warningCondition(paste(
      "A class variance of the outcome reached its lower bound: the class has",
      "almost no spread in the outcome, and its standard error is unreliable."),
      class = "latents_boundary", call = NULL))
  }
  quantile <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - ci_level) / 2)
  clustered <- .multilpa_step_clusters(.multilpa_step_ml_influence(fit, values, variance),
                                       pieces, vcov_type)
  # A sandwich for a class carried by a single unit is built from that unit's
  # score, which is zero at its own mean: it would report a standard error of
  # 0 rather than none. The units carrying a class are counted by Kish's
  # effective number, (sum r)^2 / sum r^2: 1 for one unit, 2 for two equal.
  # The units are those the sandwich sums over: groups under "cluster".
  responsibilities <- if (identical(vcov_type, "cluster")) {
    rowsum(fit$responsibilities, pieces$group_index, reorder = FALSE)
  } else fit$responsibilities
  carriers <- colSums(responsibilities)^2 / colSums(responsibilities^2)
  thin <- carriers < 1.5
  if (any(thin)) {
    warning(warningCondition(sprintf(paste(
      "Class %s of the step-three model is carried by a single unit, so its",
      "standard error cannot be estimated and is reported as NA."),
      paste(which(thin), collapse = ", ")), class = "latents_small_classes", call = NULL))
    clustered[, thin] <- NA_real_
  }
  if (identical(contrast, "pairs")) {
    # The common origin cancels from contrasts; remove it before subtraction
    # so reported rounding at a large origin cannot erase a small difference.
    means <- fit$outcome_coordinates$means * fit$outcome_coordinates$scale
    return(.multilpa_step_pairs(means, clustered, level, "ml", quantile,
                                adjust, vcov_type))
  }
  errors <- sqrt(colSums(clustered^2))
  result <- data.frame(level = level, method = "ml",
                       class = seq_len(pieces$n_classes), estimate = fit$means,
                       standard_error = errors,
                       conf_low = fit$means - quantile * errors,
                       conf_high = fit$means + quantile * errors,
                       variance = fit$variances,
                       effective_n = colSums(fit$responsibilities),
                       row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  attr(result, "vcov_type") <- vcov_type
  attr(result, "variance") <- variance
  column <- .latents_column
  .latents_table(result, ci_level,
                 sprintf("Distal outcome by class (ml, %s variances, %s%% CI)",
                         variance, format(100 * ci_level)),
                 list(column("Class", "class", "integer"), column("Mean", "estimate"),
                      column(sprintf("%s%% CI", format(100 * ci_level)),
                             c("conf_low", "conf_high"), "ci", "estimate"),
                      column("SE", "standard_error"), column("Variance", "variance"),
                      column("Effective n", "effective_n")))
}

.multilpa_classification_errors <- function(x,
