#' @param model A covariance structure as `multilpa()` takes it (`"EEI"`,
#'   `"VVI"`, `"VEI"`, ... ; mclust's codes). Standard errors are given for
#'   every structure with the extensions (covariate, occasion-varying or
#'   second-order transitions, occasion-specific measurement), and for EEI,
#'   VVI, EEE and VVV in the homogeneous model, which refuses the other ten
#'   with `latents_unsupported_inference`.
#' @return A `multilpa_transitions` object containing `means`, `variances`,
#'   optional `covariances` and `response_probabilities`,
#'   `initial_probabilities` (group classes by profiles),
#'   `transition_probabilities` (profiles by profiles by group classes, rows
#'   indexing the profile moved from), `group_probabilities`, posterior
#'   matrices, classifications, log likelihood, information criteria, restart
#'   diagnostics and convergence history. [get_results()] returns the tidy
#'   transition table and the other tables, [parameter_inference()] Wald or
#'   bootstrap standard errors, and [bootstrap_lrt()] compares nested fits.
#'   Global optimality is not guaranteed.
#'
#'   With `transitions = "occasion"`, `transition_covariates`,
#'   `initial_covariates`, `measurement = "occasion"`, `order = 2`,
#'   `mover_stayer = TRUE`, `weights`, `ordinal` or `count`, the result is a
#'   `multilpa_lta` object, read with [get_results()]: transition and initial
#'   logit coefficients with Wald standard errors (observed, robust or OPG,
#'   from analytic scores), model-implied transition probabilities per
#'   occasion, and profiles per occasion. Missing indicators
#'   (`missing = "fiml"`) and covariance structures are supported; diagonal
#'   fits are finished by a quasi-Newton search on the exact likelihood,
#'   others by EM. Agreement with Mplus (User's Guide examples 8.13, 8.14;
#'   occasion-specific thresholds), depmixS4 and LMest is recorded in
#'   `equivalence/lta-extensions/` of the source repository.
#' @details By default transitions are first order and homogeneous over
#'   occasions: the probability of moving from one profile to another does not
#'   depend on the occasion or on earlier profiles. Measurement parameters are
#'   shared across occasions and across group classes. A profile that no group
#'   occupies before its final occasion leaves its transition row without
#'   information; the row is then uniform by construction, not estimated. Such
#'   a row raises a warning when the model is fitted, is flagged by the
#'   `estimated` column of the transition table and is listed by
#'   `get_results(fit, "transitions", estimated = FALSE)`. Profile labels are
#'   arbitrary and are not comparable across fits without alignment.
#'
#'   `max_iter = 0` updates nothing: the starting values are evaluated and
#'   returned with the expectation they imply, and the fit reports
#'   `converged = FALSE` after zero iterations. Every reported quantity,
#'   including `expected_count` and the implied profile prevalence, is then
#'   read off that single expectation.
#' @references Collins, L. M., & Lanza, S. T. (2010). Latent class and latent
#'   transition analysis. Wiley.
#'
#'   Varadhan, R., & Roland, C. (2008). Simple and globally convergent methods
#'   for accelerating the convergence of any EM algorithm. Scandinavian
#'   Journal of Statistics, 35, 335--353.
#'
#'   Vermunt, J. K. (2003). Multilevel latent class models. Sociological
#'   Methodology, 33, 213--239. doi:10.1111/j.0081-1750.2003.t01-1-00131.x.
#' @seealso [get_results()] for the fitted transition probabilities and for the
#'   assignments in order, and [multilpa()] for the
#'   cross-sectional model this one shares its measurement parameters with.
#' @examples
#' # Students take their courses in their own order, which `sequence` records,
#' # so the same enrolments that fit a cross-sectional model fit a transition
#' # one. Engagement mostly persists from one course to the next.
#' fit <- lta(
#'   course_engagement,
#'   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
#'   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence", n_starts = 2, seed = 1
#' )
#' get_results(fit, what = "transitions")
#' summary(fit)
#' @export
after.source:
lta <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles, time,
                            n_group_classes = 1L,
                            variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
                            n_starts = 10L, max_iter = 5000L, tol = 1e-10,
                            min_variance = 1e-6, seed = NULL,
                            missing = c("error", "fiml"),
                            covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
                            categorical = character(), min_probability = 1e-10,
                            occasions = c("observed", "grid"),
                            select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
                            transitions = c("homogeneous", "occasion"),
                            transition_covariates = character(),
                            initial_covariates = character(),
                            measurement = c("invariant", "occasion"),
                            order = 1L, model = NULL, mover_stayer = FALSE,
                            weights = NULL, ordinal = character(),
                            count = character(),
                            count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
                            count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
                            drop_empty = TRUE, search = c("kmeans", "emEM"),
                            n_screen = NULL,
                            acceleration = c("squarem", "none"), cores = 1L) {
  # Setup forces the public arguments and draws every start in its seed frame.
  plan <- do.call(.lta_setup, c(as.list(environment()), list(call = match.call())),
                  quote = TRUE)
  .lta_run_plan(plan, cores)
}

old_inventory_record.name: lta
old_inventory_record.documentation: Fit a latent transition model  Fits latent profiles to repeated observations of the same group, estimates the probabilities of moving between profiles from one occasion to the next, and returns a `multilpa_transitions` (or `multilpa_lta`) object. The measurement model is that of [multilpa()] (Gaussian, categorical or mixed indicators) and is invariant across occasions by default, so a profile has the same meaning at every occasion. With more than one group class, each class has its own initial distribution and its own transition matrix, so the group classes are a mixture over transition patterns. [multilpa()] is the cross-sectional counterpart.  @inheritParams multilpa @param search How the starts are found: `"kmeans"` (the default) or   `"emEM"`, as described for [multilpa()]. Unlike [multilpa()], `lta()`   does not choose its default by the covariance structure. @param cores Number of processor cores for the random starts (default 1).   The starting values are drawn in order in the current process and only   the EM runs are distributed, so with `seed` given the result is identical   to `cores = 1`. Under `search = "emEM"` both screening and the final runs   are distributed. Workers are forked processes on macOS and Linux, and a   socket cluster on Windows and on macOS with Apple's Accelerate BLAS, as   in [enumerate_classes()]. Lost worker results are retried once with half   as many workers (rounded up), with one `latents_worker_lost` warning   reporting losses and recovery and suggesting fewer cores. A start still   lost is recorded as failed; the fit uses the remaining starts. If all   starts fail, the usual `latents_all_starts_failed` error is raised.   Socket workers use bounded chunks; completed tasks within a failed chunk   may also be retried. To fit many models, give `cores` to   [enumerate_classes()], which runs starts across candidates in one pool. @param id Name of the observed group identifier column. Character, factor   and numeric identifiers are supported; missing identifiers are not.   Required; `id = NULL` is not accepted. @param n_profiles Integer number of individual profiles, at least two   (`latents_bad_transition` otherwise). @param time Name of the column giving each observation's occasion within   its group. Required. Values must be complete and unique within each   group. They are ordered as [sort()] orders them: numbers numerically, a   factor by its levels, and character strings alphabetically. Numbers   stored as text whose alphabetical order is not their numeric order   (`"2"`, `"10"`) raise `latents_bad_time` (also `latents_bad_data`);   zero-padded numbers and ISO dates are accepted. @param n_group_classes Positive integer number of latent group classes   (default 1). One gives an ordinary latent transition model; more than one   fits a mixture of transition models over groups. @param select_start Which start the fit reports. `"likelihood"` (the   default) takes the highest log likelihood across starts, preferring a   converged start only among those within a relative `1e-10` of it.   `"converged"` takes the highest log likelihood among the converged starts   when at least one converged, and among all starts otherwise. The two   differ when an unconverged start exceeds a converged one by a negligible   amount, as happens when a membership logit drifts along a flat ridge of   the likelihood; only the converged start is a maximum on which standard   errors can be based. `summary()` and `get_results(fit, "starts")` show   every start. @param occasions How a group's occasions are placed on the transition grid.   `"observed"` (the default) numbers each group's own observations   consecutively, so a transition always links two adjacent observations.   `"grid"` places them on the grid of every position seen in the data, so a   group that skips a position still makes a transition across the gap and   contributes no measurement information at it. The two agree when every   group is observed at every position. Under either, a group's first   observation is its first occasion: occasion-specific transitions and   measurement count occasions from each group's own start, not from the   first position in the data. @param transitions `"homogeneous"` (the default) uses one transition matrix   for every occasion; `"occasion"` estimates a separate one for each move   (occasion 1 to 2, 2 to 3, ...). @param transition_covariates Names of columns whose values shift the   transition probabilities through a multinomial logit per origin profile:   the log odds of moving to each other profile rather than staying. A   column may change over occasions; the value at the destination occasion   is used. Factors are expanded to indicator columns. With `occasions =   "grid"`, a move into a position the group skipped has no row to read the   covariates from, and the fit raises `latents_bad_data`; use   `occasions = "observed"`, or add the skipped rows with their covariate   values (their indicators may be missing under `missing = "fiml"`). @param initial_covariates Names of columns that shift the initial profile   distribution (a multinomial logit, reference: the last profile), read at   each group's first occasion. @param measurement `"invariant"` (the default) keeps the profiles' means,   variances and response probabilities equal across occasions;   `"occasion"` estimates them separately at each occasion. @param tol Positive relative log-likelihood tolerance (default `1e-10`,   tighter than the `1e-8` of [multilpa()]). Convergence requires an   absolute change no greater than `tol * (1 + abs(previous log likelihood))`.   The group-class shares are re-estimated from posteriors one EM step   behind them; at `1e-8` the two differed by up to about `2e-4`, at `1e-10`   by about `2e-5`, for roughly 1.5 times the iterations. @param acceleration `"squarem"` (the default) accelerates EM with SQUAREM   (Varadhan & Roland, 2008), as [multilpa()] does: each cycle extrapolates   along the last two EM steps, including the initial and transition   probabilities, and ends with an ordinary EM step. An extrapolated point   that would lower the likelihood, or that leaves a probability   non-positive or a row not summing to one, is replaced by the plain EM   point, so the iteration stays monotone. Convergence is assessed over a   whole cycle, so it is never looser than plain EM's. Under the strict   default `tol` plain EM can creep along a flat likelihood for thousands of   steps; SQUAREM usually stops in far fewer, at the same or a slightly   higher maximum. `"none"` runs plain EM, which reproduces fits from   versions before this argument existed. `iterations` and `max_iter` count   EM steps under either setting. @param max_iter Nonnegative integer maximum number of EM updates per start   (default 5000, higher than the 1000 of [multilpa()] to match the tighter   `tol`). A fit that stops short warns with `latents_unconverged`.   `max_iter = 0` updates nothing and evaluates the starting values. @param order `1` (the default) or `2`. With `2`, the profile at each   occasion from the third on depends on the profiles at the two previous   occasions (a second-order Markov chain); the first move stays first   order. @param mover_stayer `FALSE` (the default), or `TRUE` to add a class of   stayers: groups that never change profile (identity transitions) and have   their own initial profile distribution (Goodman's mover-stayer model).   `n_group_classes` then counts the mover classes; the stayer class is   reported as `"stayers"`. @param weights `NULL`, or the name of a column of `data` holding one   sampling weight per `id` (constant over its occasions). As in   [multilpa()]: pseudo maximum likelihood with the weights scaled to sum to   the number of `id` units, sandwich standard errors by default, and   integer weights equal to repeating each sequence. A weighted fit uses the   general transition engine and returns a `multilpa_lta`, whose   model-implied `"transitions"` and `"initial"` tables average the groups   with their weights. @param ordinal,count,count_model,count_dispersion Ordinal and count   indicators, as in [multilpa()]; with `measurement = "occasion"` their   parameters are estimated per occasion. Read them with   `get_results(fit, "ordinal")` and `get_results(fit, "count_means")`. A   fit with them uses the general transition engine. @param model A covariance structure as `multilpa()` takes it (`"EEI"`,   `"VVI"`, `"VEI"`, ... ; mclust's codes). Standard errors are given for   every structure with the extensions (covariate, occasion-varying or   second-order transitions, occasion-specific measurement), and for EEI,   VVI, EEE and VVV in the homogeneous model, which refuses the other ten   with `latents_unsupported_inference`. @return A `multilpa_transitions` object containing `means`, `variances`,   optional `covariances` and `response_probabilities`,   `initial_probabilities` (group classes by profiles),   `transition_probabilities` (profiles by profiles by group classes, rows   indexing the profile moved from), `group_probabilities`, posterior   matrices, classifications, log likelihood, information criteria, restart   diagnostics and convergence history. [get_results()] returns the tidy   transition table and the other tables, [parameter_inference()] Wald or   bootstrap standard errors, and [bootstrap_lrt()] compares nested fits.   Global optimality is not guaranteed.    With `transitions = "occasion"`, `transition_covariates`,   `initial_covariates`, `measurement = "occasion"`, `order = 2`,   `mover_stayer = TRUE`, `weights`, `ordinal` or `count`, the result is a   `multilpa_lta` object, read with [get_results()]: transition and initial   logit coefficients with Wald standard errors (observed, robust or OPG,   from analytic scores), model-implied transition probabilities per   occasion, and profiles per occasion. Missing indicators   (`missing = "fiml"`) and covariance structures are supported; diagonal   fits are finished by a quasi-Newton search on the exact likelihood,   others by EM. Agreement with Mplus (User's Guide examples 8.13, 8.14;   occasion-specific thresholds), depmixS4 and LMest is recorded in   `equivalence/lta-extensions/` of the source repository. @details By default transitions are first order and homogeneous over   occasions: the probability of moving from one profile to another does not   depend on the occasion or on earlier profiles. Measurement parameters are   shared across occasions and across group classes. A profile that no group   occupies before its final occasion leaves its transition row without   information; the row is then uniform by construction, not estimated. Such   a row raises a warning when the model is fitted, is flagged by the   `estimated` column of the transition table and is listed by   `get_results(fit, "transitions", estimated = FALSE)`. Profile labels are   arbitrary and are not comparable across fits without alignment.    `max_iter = 0` updates nothing: the starting values are evaluated and   returned with the expectation they imply, and the fit reports   `converged = FALSE` after zero iterations. Every reported quantity,   including `expected_count` and the implied profile prevalence, is then   read off that single expectation. @references Collins, L. M., & Lanza, S. T. (2010). Latent class and latent   transition analysis. Wiley.    Varadhan, R., & Roland, C. (2008). Simple and globally convergent methods   for accelerating the convergence of any EM algorithm. Scandinavian   Journal of Statistics, 35, 335--353.    Vermunt, J. K. (2003). Multilevel latent class models. Sociological   Methodology, 33, 213--239. doi:10.1111/j.0081-1750.2003.t01-1-00131.x. @seealso [get_results()] for the fitted transition probabilities and for the   assignments in order, and [multilpa()] for the   cross-sectional model this one shares its measurement parameters with. @examples # Students take their courses in their own order, which `sequence` records, # so the same enrolments that fit a cross-sectional model fit a transition # one. Engagement mostly persists from one course to the next. fit <- lta(   course_engagement,   vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),   id = "student", n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence", n_starts = 2, seed = 1 ) get_results(fit, what = "transitions") summary(fit) @export

before.name: .lta_setup
before.formal_defaults:
as.pairlist(alist(data = , vars = , id = , n_profiles = , time = , n_group_classes = 1L, variance_model = c("varying", "equal"), n_starts = 10L, max_iter = 5000L, tol = 1e-10, min_variance = 1e-06, seed = NULL, missing = c("error", "fiml"), covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"), categorical = character(), min_probability = 1e-10, occasions = c("observed", "grid"), select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"), transitions = c("homogeneous", "occasion"), transition_covariates = character(), initial_covariates = character(), measurement = c("invariant", 
    "occasion"), order = 1L, model = NULL, mover_stayer = FALSE, weights = NULL, ordinal = character(), count = character(), count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"), count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"), drop_empty = TRUE, search = c("kmeans", "emEM"), n_screen = NULL, acceleration = c("squarem", "none"), cores = 1L, call = NULL))
before.documentation:
#' Prepare a latent transition fit without running its starts
#' @inheritParams lta
#' @param call The public fitting call to retain on the result.
#' @return A prepared start plan with a runner and a parent-side finaliser.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.lta_setup <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles, time,
                            n_group_classes = 1L,
                            variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
                            n_starts = 10L, max_iter = 5000L, tol = 1e-10,
                            min_variance = 1e-6, seed = NULL,
                            missing = c("error", "fiml"),
                            covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
                            categorical = character(), min_probability = 1e-10,
                            occasions = c("observed", "grid"),
                            select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
                            transitions = c("homogeneous", "occasion"),
                            transition_covariates = character(),
                            initial_covariates = character(),
                            measurement = c("invariant", "occasion"),
                            order = 1L, model = NULL, mover_stayer = FALSE,
                            weights = NULL, ordinal = character(),
                            count = character(),
                            count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
                            count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
                            drop_empty = TRUE, search = c("kmeans", "emEM"),
                            n_screen = NULL,
                            acceleration = c("squarem", "none"), cores = 1L, call = NULL) {
  cores <- .latents_check_cores(cores)
  acceleration <- match.arg(acceleration)
  count_model <- match.arg(count_model)
  count_dispersion <- match.arg(count_dispersion)
  .multilpa_check_drop_empty(drop_empty)
  select_start <- match.arg(select_start)
  search <- match.arg(search)
  transitions <- match.arg(transitions)
  measurement_model <- match.arg(measurement)
  if (!is.numeric(order) || length(order) != 1L || !order %in% c(1, 2)) {
    stop(errorCondition("`order` must be 1 or 2.", class = "latents_bad_argument",
                        call = NULL))
  }
  stopifnot("`mover_stayer` must be TRUE or FALSE" = isTRUE(mover_stayer) ||
              isFALSE(mover_stayer))
  general <- mover_stayer || order == 2 || !identical(transitions, "homogeneous") ||
    length(transition_covariates) > 0L || length(initial_covariates) > 0L ||
    !identical(measurement_model, "invariant") || !is.null(weights) ||
    length(ordinal) > 0L || length(count) > 0L
  .latents_check_extra_arguments(vars, categorical, ordinal, count)
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(data), is.character(vars), is.character(id),
            "`categorical` must be a character vector of indicator names" =
              is.character(categorical) && !anyNA(categorical),
            "`min_probability` must be a single number in (0, 1)" =
              is.numeric(min_probability) && length(min_probability) == 1L &&
              is.finite(min_probability) && min_probability > 0 &&
              min_probability < 1,
            "`time` must be supplied; a transition model is defined by the ordering" =
              !is.null(time))
  if (is.null(call)) call <- match.call()
  variance_model <- match.arg(variance_model)
  covariance_model <- match.arg(covariance_model)
  missing <- match.arg(missing)
  occasions <- match.arg(occasions)
  # `model` names the covariance structure in mclust's three letters, as in
  # multilpa(); NULL keeps the `variance_model` x `covariance_model` choice.
  structure <- NULL
  if (!is.null(model)) {
    if (!is.character(model) || length(model) != 1L ||
        !model %in% .multilpa_structures()) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf("`model` must be one of %s.",
        paste(sprintf("\"%s\"", .multilpa_structures()), collapse = ", ")),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    pieces <- .multilpa_structure_arguments(model)
    structure <- .multilpa_resolve_structure(variance_model, covariance_model,
                                             pieces$volume, pieces$shape,
                                             pieces$orientation)
    if (.multilpa_is_ellipsoidal(structure)) covariance_model <- "full"
    if (structure %in% c("EEI", "EEE")) variance_model <- "equal"
    if (structure %in% c("VVI", "VVV")) variance_model <- "varying"
    .multilpa_reset_structure_log()
  }
  # The data contract is checked BEFORE the ordering column. Reversed, a missing
  # group column surfaced as an internal `split()` failure ("group length is 0
  # but data length > 0") instead of this package's own classed error.
  .multilpa_check_arguments(data, vars, id, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                            n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance,
                            min_probability, seed, categorical)
  time_values <- .multilpa_time_values(data, time, id, vars)
  if (general) {
    # The general engine: transitions per occasion or covariate, covariate
    # initial distribution, or measurement per occasion.
    if (n_profiles < 2L) {
      stop(errorCondition(
        "`n_profiles` must be at least two; a single profile has nothing to move between.",
        class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
    }
    return(.lta_setup_general(data, vars, id, time, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                            variance_model, n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance,
                            seed, categorical, min_probability, occasions,
                            transitions, transition_covariates, initial_covariates,
                            measurement_model, select_start, call, as.integer(order),
                            mover_stayer, missing, covariance_model, structure,
                            weights, ordinal, count, count_model, count_dispersion,
                            drop_empty = drop_empty, search = search,
                            n_screen = n_screen, acceleration = acceleration,
                            cores = cores))
  }
  if (n_profiles < 2L) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "`n_profiles` must be at least two; a single profile has nothing to move between.",
      class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
  }
  measurement <- .multilpa_prepare_indicators(data, vars, categorical,
                                              missing, min_probability)
  continuous <- measurement$continuous
  codes <- measurement$codes
  n_categories <- measurement$n_categories
  x <- measurement$x
  groups <- .multilpa_prepare_groups(data[[id]])
  layout <- .multilpa_sequence_layout(groups$index, time_values, groups$n, occasions)
  if (layout$n_occasions < 2L) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "No group is observed at two occasions, so no transition can be estimated.",
      class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
  }
  distinct_rows <- if (is.null(codes)) nrow(unique(x)) else
    nrow(unique(cbind(x, codes)))
  if (n_profiles > distinct_rows) {
    stop(errorCondition("n_profiles cannot exceed the number of distinct observed indicator rows.",
        class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  if (n_group_classes > groups$n) {
    stop(errorCondition("n_group_classes cannot exceed the number of groups.",
        class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  if (n_group_classes > 1L && all(groups$sizes == 1L)) {
    stop(errorCondition("Multiple group classes are not identifiable with only singleton groups.",
        class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  .latents_local_seed(seed)
  # Centering is a translation of the indicators, with no density Jacobian and
  # no change of scale; the fitted means are shifted back before they are read.
  centers <- if (ncol(x) > 0L) colMeans(x, na.rm = TRUE) else numeric(0)
  x <- sweep(x, 2L, centers, "-")
  if (any(!is.finite(x[!is.na(x)]^2))) {
    stop(errorCondition("Indicator scales overflow squared residuals; rescale the data.",
        class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  # Each start runs to completion or is recorded as failed; the best is
  # chosen by the shared rule (see .latents_run_starts()).
  # Every start is prepared before any is run; EM draws no random numbers, so
  # the draws are those of preparing and running each start in turn.
  screen <- .latents_search_screen(search, n_starts, n_screen, max_iter)
  prepare <- function(start_index) {
    initial <- .multilpa_transition_initialize(
      x, groups$index, n_profiles, n_group_classes, variance_model,
      min_variance, start_index, covariance_model, codes, n_categories,
      min_probability, kind = .latents_start_kind(start_index, n_starts))
    if (!is.null(structure)) {
      initial <- .multilpa_project_start(initial, structure, nrow(x), min_variance)
    }
    initial
  }
  initial <- .latents_prepare_starts(
    if (is.null(screen)) n_starts else screen$n_pool, prepare)
  context <- as.list(environment())
  context[c("prepare", "initial")] <- NULL
  .lta_plan(context, initial, .lta_run_start, .lta_finalise,
             c("x", "layout", "variance_model", "min_variance", "max_iter", "tol",
               "covariance_model", "codes", "n_categories", "min_probability",
               "structure", "acceleration"))
}

#' Prepare a latent transition fit without running its starts
#' @inheritParams lta
#' @param call The public fitting call to retain on the result.
#' @return A prepared start plan with a runner and a parent-side finaliser.
#' @noRd
after.source:
.lta_setup <- function(data, vars, id, n_profiles, time,
                            n_group_classes = 1L,
                            variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
                            n_starts = 10L, max_iter = 5000L, tol = 1e-10,
                            min_variance = 1e-6, seed = NULL,
                            missing = c("error", "fiml"),
                            covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
                            categorical = character(), min_probability = 1e-10,
                            occasions = c("observed", "grid"),
                            select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
                            transitions = c("homogeneous", "occasion"),
                            transition_covariates = character(),
                            initial_covariates = character(),
                            measurement = c("invariant", "occasion"),
                            order = 1L, model = NULL, mover_stayer = FALSE,
                            weights = NULL, ordinal = character(),
                            count = character(),
                            count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
                            count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
                            drop_empty = TRUE, search = c("kmeans", "emEM"),
                            n_screen = NULL,
                            acceleration = c("squarem", "none"), cores = 1L, call = NULL) {
  cores <- .latents_check_cores(cores)
  acceleration <- match.arg(acceleration)
  count_model <- match.arg(count_model)
  count_dispersion <- match.arg(count_dispersion)
  .multilpa_check_drop_empty(drop_empty)
  select_start <- match.arg(select_start)
  search <- match.arg(search)
  transitions <- match.arg(transitions)
  measurement_model <- match.arg(measurement)
  if (!is.numeric(order) || length(order) != 1L || !order %in% c(1, 2)) {
    stop(errorCondition("`order` must be 1 or 2.", class = "latents_bad_argument",
                        call = NULL))
  }
  stopifnot("`mover_stayer` must be TRUE or FALSE" = isTRUE(mover_stayer) ||
              isFALSE(mover_stayer))
  general <- mover_stayer || order == 2 || !identical(transitions, "homogeneous") ||
    length(transition_covariates) > 0L || length(initial_covariates) > 0L ||
    !identical(measurement_model, "invariant") || !is.null(weights) ||
    length(ordinal) > 0L || length(count) > 0L
  .latents_check_extra_arguments(vars, categorical, ordinal, count)
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(data), is.character(vars), is.character(id),
            "`categorical` must be a character vector of indicator names" =
              is.character(categorical) && !anyNA(categorical),
            "`min_probability` must be a single number in (0, 1)" =
              is.numeric(min_probability) && length(min_probability) == 1L &&
              is.finite(min_probability) && min_probability > 0 &&
              min_probability < 1,
            "`time` must be supplied; a transition model is defined by the ordering" =
              !is.null(time))
  if (is.null(call)) call <- match.call()
  variance_model <- match.arg(variance_model)
  covariance_model <- match.arg(covariance_model)
  missing <- match.arg(missing)
  occasions <- match.arg(occasions)
  # `model` names the covariance structure in mclust's three letters, as in
  # multilpa(); NULL keeps the `variance_model` x `covariance_model` choice.
  structure <- NULL
  if (!is.null(model)) {
    if (!is.character(model) || length(model) != 1L ||
        !model %in% .multilpa_structures()) {
      stop(errorCondition(sprintf("`model` must be one of %s.",
        paste(sprintf("\"%s\"", .multilpa_structures()), collapse = ", ")),
        class = "latents_bad_argument", call = NULL))
    }
    pieces <- .multilpa_structure_arguments(model)
    structure <- .multilpa_resolve_structure(variance_model, covariance_model,
                                             pieces$volume, pieces$shape,
                                             pieces$orientation)
    if (.multilpa_is_ellipsoidal(structure)) covariance_model <- "full"
    if (structure %in% c("EEI", "EEE")) variance_model <- "equal"
    if (structure %in% c("VVI", "VVV")) variance_model <- "varying"
    .multilpa_reset_structure_log()
  }
  # The data contract is checked BEFORE the ordering column. Reversed, a missing
  # group column surfaced as an internal `split()` failure ("group length is 0
  # but data length > 0") instead of this package's own classed error.
  .multilpa_check_arguments(data, vars, id, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                            n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance,
                            min_probability, seed, categorical)
  time_values <- .multilpa_time_values(data, time, id, vars)
  if (general) {
    # The general engine: transitions per occasion or covariate, covariate
    # initial distribution, or measurement per occasion.
    if (n_profiles < 2L) {
      stop(errorCondition(
        "`n_profiles` must be at least two; a single profile has nothing to move between.",
        class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
    }
    return(.lta_setup_general(data, vars, id, time, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                            variance_model, n_starts, max_iter, tol, min_variance,
                            seed, categorical, min_probability, occasions,
                            transitions, transition_covariates, initial_covariates,
                            measurement_model, select_start, call, as.integer(order),
                            mover_stayer, missing, covariance_model, structure,
                            weights, ordinal, count, count_model, count_dispersion,
                            drop_empty = drop_empty, search = search,
                            n_screen = n_screen, acceleration = acceleration,
                            cores = cores))
  }
  if (n_profiles < 2L) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "`n_profiles` must be at least two; a single profile has nothing to move between.",
      class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
  }
  measurement <- .multilpa_prepare_indicators(data, vars, categorical,
                                              missing, min_probability)
  continuous <- measurement$continuous
  codes <- measurement$codes
  n_categories <- measurement$n_categories
  x <- measurement$x
  groups <- .multilpa_prepare_groups(data[[id]])
  layout <- .multilpa_sequence_layout(groups$index, time_values, groups$n, occasions)
  if (layout$n_occasions < 2L) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      "No group is observed at two occasions, so no transition can be estimated.",
      class = "latents_bad_transition", call = NULL))
  }
  distinct_rows <- if (is.null(codes)) nrow(unique(x)) else
    nrow(unique(cbind(x, codes)))
  if (n_profiles > distinct_rows) {
    stop(errorCondition("n_profiles cannot exceed the number of distinct observed indicator rows.",
        class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  if (n_group_classes > groups$n) {
    stop(errorCondition("n_group_classes cannot exceed the number of groups.",
        class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  if (n_group_classes > 1L && all(groups$sizes == 1L)) {
    stop(errorCondition("Multiple group classes are not identifiable with only singleton groups.",
        class = "latents_unidentified", call = NULL))
  }
  .latents_local_seed(seed)
  # Centering is a translation of the indicators, with no density Jacobian and
  # no change of scale; the fitted means are shifted back before they are read.
  centers <- if (ncol(x) > 0L) colMeans(x, na.rm = TRUE) else numeric(0)
  x <- sweep(x, 2L, centers, "-")
  if (any(!is.finite(x[!is.na(x)]^2))) {
    stop(errorCondition("Indicator scales overflow squared residuals; rescale the data.",
        class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  # Each start runs to completion or is recorded as failed; the best is
  # chosen by the shared rule (see .latents_run_starts()).
  # Every start is prepared before any is run; EM draws no random numbers, so
  # the draws are those of preparing and running each start in turn.
  screen <- .latents_search_screen(search, n_starts, n_screen, max_iter)
  prepare <- function(start_index) {
    initial <- .multilpa_transition_initialize(
      x, groups$index, n_profiles, n_group_classes, variance_model,
      min_variance, start_index, covariance_model, codes, n_categories,
      min_probability, kind = .latents_start_kind(start_index, n_starts))
    if (!is.null(structure)) {
      initial <- .multilpa_project_start(initial, structure, nrow(x), min_variance)
    }
    initial
  }
  initial <- .latents_prepare_starts(
    if (is.null(screen)) n_starts else screen$n_pool, prepare)
  context <- as.list(environment())
  context[c("prepare", "initial")] <- NULL
  .lta_plan(context, initial, .lta_run_start, .lta_finalise,
             c("x", "layout", "variance_model", "min_variance", "max_iter", "tol",
               "covariance_model", "codes", "n_categories", "min_probability",
               "structure", "acceleration"))
}

function(starts, context) {

        starts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(attempts), function(start_index) {
            attempt <- attempts[[start_index]]

        counted_groups <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty))

        group_sample_size <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty))

        small_classes <- any(colSums(subject_posteriors) < 1) || any(colSums(group_posteriors) < 1)

                ties.method = "first"), group_classes = max.col(group_posteriors, ties.method = "first"), log_likelihood = log_likelihood, group_log_likelihood = setNames(best$expectation$group_log_likelihood, groups$ids), n_parameters = n_parameters, aic = -2 * log_likelihood + 2 * n_parameters, bic = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters, bic_groups = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters, bic_individual = -2 * log_likelihood + log(n_informative) * n_parameters,

        }

            else "A variance reached min_variance; this is a bound-active constrained fit.", class = "latents_boundary", call = NULL))
        }

        }

        }

    })

.lta_finalise <- function(starts, context) {
  with(context, {
    found <- starts
    attempts <- starts$attempts
    valid <- starts$valid
    scores <- starts$scores
    best_start <- starts$best_start
    best <- attempts[[best_start]]
    parameters <- best$parameters
    parameters$means <- sweep(parameters$means, 2L, centers, "+")
    profile_names <- paste0("profile_", seq_len(n_profiles))
    type_names <- paste0("group_class_", seq_len(n_group_classes))
    parameters <- .multilpa_label_parameters(parameters, profile_names, continuous,
                                             categorical, measurement$encoded$levels)
    dimnames(parameters$initial_probabilities) <- list(type_names, profile_names)
    # Taken from the expectation that is reported rather than from the M-step,
    # which saw the previous one -- and which never runs at all when `max_iter`
    # is zero, where reading the M-step's field left the assembly setting
    # dimnames on NULL.
    parameters$profile_prevalence <- matrix(
      .multilpa_transition_prevalence(best$expectation),
      n_group_classes, n_profiles, dimnames = list(type_names, profile_names))
    dimnames(parameters$transition_probabilities) <-
      list(profile_names, profile_names, type_names)
    names(parameters$group_probabilities) <- type_names
    subject_posteriors <- best$expectation$subject_posteriors
    group_posteriors <- best$expectation$group_posteriors
    dimnames(subject_posteriors) <- list(rownames(data), profile_names)
    dimnames(group_posteriors) <- list(groups$ids, type_names)
    n_parameters <- .multilpa_count_transition_parameters(
      n_profiles, n_group_classes, ncol(x), n_categories, variance_model,
      covariance_model, structure)
    log_likelihood <- best$expectation$log_likelihood
    transition_counts <- array(
      vapply(best$expectation$sequence, `[[`, numeric(n_profiles * n_profiles),
             "transition"),
      c(n_profiles, n_profiles, n_group_classes),
      dimnames = list(profile_names, profile_names, type_names))
    # EM leaves the parameters one M-step behind the final expectation, so the
    # empty rows are re-read from the counts that are actually reported rather
    # than from the ones the last update happened to see.
    parameters$empty_transition_rows <- matrix(
      apply(transition_counts, c(1L, 3L), sum) <= 0, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
      dimnames = list(profile_names, type_names))
    starts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(attempts), function(start_index) {
      attempt <- attempts[[start_index]]
      data.frame(start = start_index, log_likelihood = scores[start_index],
                 converged = if (valid[start_index]) attempt$converged else FALSE,
                 iterations = if (valid[start_index]) attempt$iterations else NA_integer_,
                 error = if (valid[start_index]) NA_character_ else attempt$error)
    }))
    starts <- .latents_search_columns(starts, found, n_starts)
    observed_per_row <- rowSums(!is.na(x)) +
      if (is.null(codes)) 0L else rowSums(!is.na(codes))
    n_informative <- sum(observed_per_row > 0L)
    n_informative_groups <- length(unique(groups$index[observed_per_row > 0L]))
    # Under `drop_empty`, sizes and counts are of the classified rows and
    # groups, as Mplus counts them; otherwise of every row and group (0.9.37).
    counted_rows <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) observed_per_row > 0L else rep(TRUE, nrow(x))
    counted_groups <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty))
      seq_len(groups$n) %in% groups$index[observed_per_row > 0L] else rep(TRUE, groups$n)
    group_sample_size <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) n_informative_groups else groups$n
    boundary <- .multilpa_covariance_boundary(parameters, min_variance)
    empty_rows <- any(parameters$empty_transition_rows)
    small_classes <- any(colSums(subject_posteriors) < 1) ||
      any(colSums(group_posteriors) < 1)
    result <- c(parameters, list(
      call = call, vars = vars, continuous = continuous,
      continuous_types = vapply(data[continuous], typeof, character(1)),
      categorical = categorical,
      categorical_levels = measurement$encoded$levels,
      categorical_values = .multilpa_categorical_values(
        data, categorical, measurement$encoded),
      min_probability = min_probability,
      indicator_data = as.matrix(measurement$frame), categorical_data = codes,
      id = id, group_ids = groups$ids, time = time, time_values = time_values,
      group_values = groups$values, group_index = groups$index,
      group_sizes = setNames(groups$sizes, groups$ids),
      n_observations = nrow(x), n_informative = n_informative,
      informative = observed_per_row > 0L,
      n_informative_groups = n_informative_groups, drop_empty = drop_empty,
      n_groups = groups$n, n_profiles = as.integer(n_profiles),
      n_group_classes = as.integer(n_group_classes),
      n_occasions = layout$n_occasions, occasions = occasions,
      sequence_lengths = setNames(layout$span, groups$ids),
      balanced = all(layout$span == layout$n_occasions) &&
        !anyNA(layout$slot),
      variance_model = variance_model, covariance_model = covariance_model,
      covariance_structure = structure,
      missing = missing, min_variance = min_variance,
      standard_deviations = sqrt(parameters$variances),
      measurement_model = if (is.null(codes)) "gaussian" else
        if (ncol(x) == 0L) "categorical" else "mixed",
      transition_counts = transition_counts,
      subject_posteriors = subject_posteriors, group_posteriors = group_posteriors,
      subject_profiles = max.col(subject_posteriors, ties.method = "first"),
      group_classes = max.col(group_posteriors, ties.method = "first"),
      log_likelihood = log_likelihood,
      group_log_likelihood = setNames(best$expectation$group_log_likelihood,
                                      groups$ids),
      n_parameters = n_parameters, aic = -2 * log_likelihood + 2 * n_parameters,
      bic = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters,
      bic_groups = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters,

.lta_finalise <- function(starts, context) {
  with(context, {
    found <- starts
    attempts <- starts$attempts
    valid <- starts$valid
    scores <- starts$scores

    best <- attempts[[best_start]]

    parameters$means <- sweep(parameters$means, 2L, centers, "+")

    type_names <- paste0("group_class_", seq_len(n_group_classes))
    parameters <- .multilpa_label_parameters(parameters, profile_names, continuous,
                                             categorical, measurement$encoded$levels)
    dimnames(parameters$initial_probabilities) <- list(type_names, profile_names)
    # Taken from the expectation that is reported rather than from the M-step,
    # which saw the previous one -- and which never runs at all when `max_iter`
    # is zero, where reading the M-step's field left the assembly setting
    # dimnames on NULL.
    parameters$profile_prevalence <- matrix(
      .multilpa_transition_prevalence(best$expectation),
      n_group_classes, n_profiles, dimnames = list(type_names, profile_names))
    dimnames(parameters$transition_probabilities) <-
      list(profile_names, profile_names, type_names)
    names(parameters$group_probabilities) <- type_names
    subject_posteriors <- best$expectation$subject_posteriors
    group_posteriors <- best$expectation$group_posteriors
    dimnames(subject_posteriors) <- list(rownames(data), profile_names)
    dimnames(group_posteriors) <- list(groups$ids, type_names)
    n_parameters <- .multilpa_count_transition_parameters(
      n_profiles, n_group_classes, ncol(x), n_categories, variance_model,
      covariance_model, structure)
    log_likelihood <- best$expectation$log_likelihood

      vapply(best$expectation$sequence, `[[`, numeric(n_profiles * n_profiles),
             "transition"),
      c(n_profiles, n_profiles, n_group_classes),
      dimnames = list(profile_names, profile_names, type_names))
    # EM leaves the parameters one M-step behind the final expectation, so the
    # empty rows are re-read from the counts that are actually reported rather
    # than from the ones the last update happened to see.
    parameters$empty_transition_rows <- matrix(
      apply(transition_counts, c(1L, 3L), sum) <= 0, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
      dimnames = list(profile_names, type_names))
    starts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(attempts), function(start_index) {
      attempt <- attempts[[start_index]]
      data.frame(start = start_index, log_likelihood = scores[start_index],
                 converged = if (valid[start_index]) attempt$converged else FALSE,
                 iterations = if (valid[start_index]) attempt$iterations else NA_integer_,
                 error = if (valid[start_index]) NA_character_ else attempt$error)
    }))
    starts <- .latents_search_columns(starts, found, n_starts)
    observed_per_row <- rowSums(!is.na(x)) +
      if (is.null(codes)) 0L else rowSums(!is.na(codes))
    n_informative <- sum(observed_per_row > 0L)
    n_informative_groups <- length(unique(groups$index[observed_per_row > 0L]))

    # groups, as Mplus counts them; otherwise of every row and group (0.9.37).
    counted_rows <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) observed_per_row > 0L else rep(TRUE, nrow(x))
    counted_groups <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty))
      seq_len(groups$n) %in% groups$index[observed_per_row > 0L] else rep(TRUE, groups$n)
    group_sample_size <- if (isTRUE(drop_empty)) n_informative_groups else groups$n
    boundary <- .multilpa_covariance_boundary(parameters, min_variance)

    small_classes <- any(colSums(subject_posteriors) < 1) ||

      call = call, vars = vars, continuous = continuous,
      continuous_types = vapply(data[continuous], typeof, character(1)),
      categorical = categorical,

      n_groups = groups$n, n_profiles = as.integer(n_profiles),
      n_group_classes = as.integer(n_group_classes),
      n_occasions = layout$n_occasions, occasions = occasions,
      sequence_lengths = setNames(layout$span, groups$ids),
      balanced = all(layout$span == layout$n_occasions) &&
        !anyNA(layout$slot),
      variance_model = variance_model, covariance_model = covariance_model,
      covariance_structure = structure,
      missing = missing, min_variance = min_variance,
      standard_deviations = sqrt(parameters$variances),
      measurement_model = if (is.null(codes)) "gaussian" else
        if (ncol(x) == 0L) "categorical" else "mixed",
      transition_counts = transition_counts,

      group_classes = max.col(group_posteriors, ties.method = "first"),

      n_parameters = n_parameters, aic = -2 * log_likelihood + 2 * n_parameters,
      bic = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters,
      bic_groups = -2 * log_likelihood + log(group_sample_size) * n_parameters,
      bic_individual = -2 * log_likelihood + log(n_informative) * n_parameters,
      converged = best$converged, iterations = best$iterations,
      log_likelihood_history = best$history, starts = starts,
      best_start = best_start, n_failed_starts = sum(!valid), boundary = boundary,
      small_classes = small_classes,
      effective_profile_counts = colSums(subject_posteriors[counted_rows, , drop = FALSE]),
      effective_group_counts = colSums(group_posteriors[counted_groups, , drop = FALSE]),
      n_best_replicated = sum(valid & .latents_final_stage(found) &
                                abs(scores - log_likelihood) <=
                                1e-6 * (1 + abs(log_likelihood))),
      replication_tolerance = 1e-6 * (1 + abs(log_likelihood))),
      .latents_search_record(search, n_starts, screen, select_start, "allow"),
      list(max_iter = as.integer(max_iter), tol = tol, acceleration = acceleration))
    class(result) <- "multilpa_transitions"
    # Every qualification a caller might branch on carries its catalogued class,
    # so a simulation loop can muffle the ones it expects and let the rest through.
    if (any(!valid)) {

before.source:
.multilpa_restrict_transitions <- function(frame, estimated, stable) {
  keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(frame))
  if (!is.null(estimated)) keep <- keep & frame$estimated == estimated
  if (!is.null(stable)) keep <- keep & frame$stable == stable
  frame <- frame[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  row.names(frame) <- NULL
  frame
}

summary.multilpa_transitions <- function(object, ...) {
  stopifnot(inherits(object, "multilpa_transitions"))
  fields <- c("call", "n_observations", "n_groups", "n_profiles",
              "n_group_classes", "n_occasions", "occasions", "balanced",
              "variance_model", "covariance_model", "missing", "means",
              "variances", "standard_deviations", "covariances",
              "response_probabilities", "initial_probabilities",
              "transition_probabilities", "transition_counts",
              "profile_prevalence",
              "empty_transition_rows", "group_probabilities", "log_likelihood",
              "n_parameters", "aic", "bic", "bic_individual", "converged",
              "iterations", "boundary", "min_variance", "small_classes",
              "starts", "best_start", "n_best_replicated",
              "replication_tolerance", "effective_profile_counts",
              "effective_group_counts")
  # `covariances` exists only under a full covariance model and
  # `response_probabilities` only with categorical indicators. Every other
  # field is mandatory: subsetting a list by an absent name yields a NULL
  # element keyed NA rather than an error, so an absent field is caught here
  # instead of surfacing later as an `NA`-named hole in the summary.
  optional <- c("covariances", "response_probabilities")
  absent <- setdiff(setdiff(fields, optional), names(object))
  if (length(absent) > 0L) {
    stop(errorCondition(
      sprintf("The fit is missing fields the summary requires: %s.",
              paste(absent, collapse = ", ")),
      class = "latents_incomplete_fit", call = NULL))
  }
  result <- object[intersect(fields, names(object))]
  # The starts run to the end; under emEM the table also holds the screened.
  result$n_starts <- object$n_starts %||% nrow(object$starts)
  # Every table the fit can produce, built once here, so `get_results()` on the
  # summary serves the same tables the fit would and `print()` can show them
  # all without recomputing anything.
  result$tables <- get_results(object, "all")
  class(result) <- "summary_multilpa_transitions"
  result
}

.latents_tree_layout.name: .latents_tree_layout

before.name: .latents_tree_layout
before.documentation:
#' Shares, flows, positions and lineage colours of one tree
#'
#' Each row's classes are ordered by the flow-weighted centre of their parents,
#' so bands cross only where units really are reshuffled. A class that is its
#' dominant parent's main continuation keeps the parent's colour; any other
#' class takes a new one (Zappia and Oshlack, 2018).
#' @param x The grid.
#' @param tree One element of `.latents_tree_specs()`.
#' @param level `"individuals"` or `"groups"`.
#' @return The tree with `posteriors` and `weights` (one per row), `shares`,
#'   `flows` (between consecutive rows), `segments` (per row: `class`,
#'   `xmin`, `xmax`, `share`) and `colours` (per row, indexed by class).
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_tree_layout <- function(x, tree, level) {
  gap <- 0.03
  drawn <- lapply(tree$rows$at, \(at) {
    .latents_tree_posteriors(.latents_tree_fit(x, at), level)
  })
  posteriors <- lapply(drawn, `[[`, "posteriors")
  weights <- drawn[[1L]]$weights
  total <- sum(weights)
  shares <- lapply(posteriors, \(p) colSums(p * weights) / total)
  flows <- lapply(seq_along(posteriors)[-1L], \(row) {
    crossprod(posteriors[[row - 1L]] * weights, posteriors[[row]]) / total
  })
  segments_of <- \(share, ordering) {
    widths <- share[ordering]
    k <- length(widths)
    right <- cumsum(widths) + gap * (seq_len(k) - 1) - gap * (k - 1) / 2
    data.frame(class = ordering, xmin = right - widths, xmax = right,
               share = widths)
  }
  first_order <- order(-shares[[1L]], seq_along(shares[[1L]]))
  segments <- Reduce(\(previous, row) {
    parent <- previous[[length(previous)]]
    flow <- flows[[row - 1L]]
    centres <- (parent$xmin + parent$xmax)[order(parent$class)] / 2
    child_centre <- colSums(flow * centres) / colSums(flow)
    c(previous, list(segments_of(shares[[row]],
                                 order(child_centre, seq_along(child_centre)))))
  }, seq_along(posteriors)[-1L], init = list(segments_of(shares[[1L]], first_order)))
  first_colours <- character(length(shares[[1L]]))
  first_colours[first_order] <- rep_len(.gg_okabe_ito, length(first_order))
  colours <- Reduce(\(state, row) {
    flow <- flows[[row - 1L]]
    dominant_parent <- apply(flow, 2L, which.max)
    main_child <- apply(flow, 1L, which.max)
    continues <- main_child[dominant_parent] == seq_len(ncol(flow))
    fresh <- rep_len(.gg_okabe_ito,
                     state$used + sum(!continues))[-seq_len(state$used)]
    row_colours <- character(ncol(flow))
    row_colours[continues] <- state$colours[[row - 1L]][dominant_parent[continues]]
    row_colours[!continues] <- fresh
    list(colours = c(state$colours, list(row_colours)),
         used = state$used + sum(!continues))
  }, seq_along(posteriors)[-1L],
  init = list(colours = list(first_colours), used = length(first_colours)))$colours
  # Rows with one number of classes are one level of different solutions:
  # each class takes the colour of the first row's class it matches.
  if (length(unique(lengths(shares))) == 1L) {
    colours <- c(colours[1L], lapply(seq_along(posteriors)[-1L], \(row) {
      matched <- .latents_match_classes(
        crossprod(posteriors[[row]] * weights, posteriors[[1L]]))
      .latents_distinct_colours(
        ifelse(matched > 0L, colours[[1L]][pmax(matched, 1L)], colours[[row]]))
    }))
  }
  colours <- lapply(colours, .latents_distinct_colours)
  c(tree, list(posteriors = posteriors, weights = weights, shares = shares,
               flows = flows, segments = segments, colours = colours))
}

#' The flows of every tree, one row per pair of classes in consecutive rows
#'
#' @inheritParams .latents_tree_specs
#' @return A data frame: `tree`, `level`, `from_candidate`, `from_class`,
#'   `from_share`, `to_candidate`, `to_class`, `to_share`, `mass` (the share
#'   of all units the two classes share), `share_of_from` and `share_of_to`.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.latents_tree_table <- function(x, n_group_classes = NULL, n_profiles = NULL,
                                model = NULL, candidates = NULL, from = NULL,
                                to = NULL, level = c("individuals", "groups")) {
  if (identical(level, c("individuals", "groups")) &&
      identical(.latents_grid_kind(x), "families")) level <- "groups"
  level <- .latents_check_tree_arguments(level, n_profiles, n_group_classes, model)
  candidates <- .latents_tree_candidates(x, candidates, from, to, model)
  if (!is.null(from)) model <- NULL
  trees <- lapply(.latents_tree_specs(x, level, n_profiles, n_group_classes,
                                      model, candidates),
                  \(tree) .latents_tree_layout(x, tree, level))
  frame <- do.call(rbind, lapply(trees, \(tree) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(tree$flows), \(index) {
      flow <- tree$flows[[index]]
      cells <- expand.grid(from_class = seq_len(nrow(flow)),
                           to_class = seq_len(ncol(flow)))
      from_share <- tree$shares[[index]][cells$from_class]
      to_share <- tree$shares[[index + 1L]][cells$to_class]
      mass <- flow[cbind(cells$from_class, cells$to_class)]
      data.frame(tree = tree$name, level = level,
                 from_candidate = tree$rows$candidate[index],
                 from_class = cells$from_class, from_share = from_share,
                 to_candidate = tree$rows$candidate[index + 1L],
                 to_class = cells$to_class, to_share = to_share, mass = mass,
                 share_of_from = mass / from_share, share_of_to = mass / to_share,
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  }))
  rownames(frame) <- NULL
  frame
}

before.name: .gg_tree_frames
before.documentation:
#' The data of drawn trees: bars and bands, with each tree's facets
#' @param trees Anchored layouts.
#' @return A list of `bars` and `bands` data frames.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.gg_tree_frames <- function(trees) {
  half <- 0.16
  parts <- lapply(trees, \(tree) {
    facets <- data.frame(tree = tree$label, row_facet = tree$row_facet,
                         col_facet = tree$col_facet, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    position <- tree$rows$position
    bars <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(tree$segments), \(row) {
      segment <- tree$segments[[row]]
      cbind(segment, facets, row = position[row],
            fill = tree$colours[[row]][segment$class],
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
    bands <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(tree$flows), \(index) {
      parent <- tree$segments[[index]]
      child <- tree$segments[[index + 1L]]
      flow <- tree$flows[[index]]
      links <- expand.grid(from = parent$class, to = child$class)
      links$mass <- flow[cbind(links$from, links$to)]
      links <- links[links$mass > 0, , drop = FALSE]
      # Outflows stack inside a parent in child order and inflows inside a
      # child in parent order, so bands tile both bars without overlap.
      links$from_rank <- match(links$from, parent$class)
      links$to_rank <- match(links$to, child$class)
      links <- links[order(links$from_rank, links$to_rank), , drop = FALSE]
      links$top_right <- parent$xmin[links$from_rank] +
        stats::ave(links$mass, links$from, FUN = cumsum)
      links$top_left <- links$top_right - links$mass
      links <- links[order(links$to_rank, links$from_rank), , drop = FALSE]
      links$bottom_right <- child$xmin[links$to_rank] +
        stats::ave(links$mass, links$to, FUN = cumsum)
      links$bottom_left <- links$bottom_right - links$mass
      do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(links)), \(i) {
        band <- .gg_flow_band(links$top_left[i], links$top_right[i],
                              links$bottom_left[i], links$bottom_right[i],
                              y_top = position[index] + half,
                              y_bottom = position[index + 1L] - half)
        cbind(band, facets,
              group = sprintf("%s-%d-%d-%d", tree$name, index, links$from[i],
                              links$to[i]),
              fill = tree$colours[[index]][links$from[i]],
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      }))
    }))
    list(bars = bars, bands = bands)
  })
  list(bars = do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, `[[`, "bars")),
       bands = do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, `[[`, "bands")))
}

#' Draw one tree, or several as panels of one plot
#'
#' @param trees Anchored layouts, all drawn in this plot.
#' @param titles A list of `main`, `subtitle`, `caption` and `y`.
#' @return A ggplot object.
#' @noRd
before.source:
.gg_tree_plot <- function(trees, titles) {
  half <- 0.16
  # Rows sit at their count, so trees that start at different counts align
  # when drawn together; named candidates sit in the order given.
  keys <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(trees, \(tree) tree$rows$key))))
  trees <- lapply(trees, \(tree) {
    tree$rows$position <- if (anyNA(tree$rows$key)) seq_len(nrow(tree$rows)) else
      match(tree$rows$key, keys)
    tree
  })
  row_labels <- if (length(keys) == 0L) trees[[1L]]$rows$label else
    as.character(keys)
  frames <- .gg_tree_frames(trees)
  bars <- frames$bars
  bands <- frames$bands
  columns <- length(unique(bars$col_facet))
  # A share is written only where its segment is wide enough to hold it; the
  # more trees side by side, the narrower every segment.
  min_share <- 0.025 + 0.04 * (columns - 1L)
  bars$label <- ifelse(bars$share < min_share, "", .gg_percent(bars$share))
  bars$text_colour <- .gg_ink(bars$fill)
  row_levels <- unique(unlist(lapply(trees, \(tree) tree$row_facet)))
  col_levels <- unique(unlist(lapply(trees, \(tree) tree$col_facet)))
  bars$row_facet <- factor(bars$row_facet, levels = row_levels)
  bands$row_facet <- factor(bands$row_facet, levels = row_levels)
  bars$col_facet <- factor(bars$col_facet, levels = col_levels)
  bands$col_facet <- factor(bands$col_facet, levels = col_levels)
  several_rows <- length(row_levels) > 1L
  several_cols <- length(col_levels) > 1L
  facets <- if (several_rows && several_cols) {
    ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(row_facet),
                        cols = ggplot2::vars(col_facet))
  } else if (several_rows) {
    ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(row_facet))
  } else if (several_cols) {
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(col_facet), nrow = 1L)
  }
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_polygon(data = bands,
                          ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, group = group, fill = fill),
                          alpha = 0.4, colour = NA) +
    ggplot2::geom_rect(data = bars,
                       ggplot2::aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax,
                                    ymin = row - half, ymax = row + half,
                                    fill = fill),
                       colour = "white", linewidth = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = bars,
                       ggplot2::aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = row,
                                    label = label, colour = text_colour),
                       size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_identity() +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_identity() +
    facets +
    ggplot2::scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq_along(row_labels), labels = row_labels,
                             expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0.25)) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(0)) +
    .gg_titles(titles$main, titles$subtitle, titles$default_main,
               titles$default_subtitle, caption = titles$caption) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = titles$y) +
    .gg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                   panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                   panel.spacing = ggplot2::unit(1.5, "lines"))
}

#'   start that failed.
#' @param converged Logical vector of the same length.

#'   converged starts, falling back to every start when none converged.

#'   the starts with no variance at its lower bound. When supplied, only those
#'   starts are candidates, and the rule chooses among them; when none is
#'   flagged, every start is, with a `latents_all_starts_boundary` warning.
#' @return A single integer index.

#' Say that a two-level verb fitted a single-level model
#'
#' `multilpa()`, `multilca()` and `enumerate_classes()` are the verbs for
#' observations nested in groups. Given `id = NULL` they fit the single-level
#' model, which is a legitimate choice, so this is a one-line message rather
#' than a warning, naming the model that was estimated. `lpa()`, `lca()`,
#' `enumerate_lpa()` and `enumerate_lca()` muffle it, since their names
#' already say it.
#'
#' @param latent_class Whether every indicator is categorical.
#' @return `NULL`, invisibly, after signalling a `latents_single_level`
#'   message.
#' @noRd
before.definition_AST:
function(latent_class = FALSE) {
    analysis <- if (isTRUE(latent_class)) 
        "latent class"
    else "latent profile"
    .multilpa_notice(sprintf("Fitted a single-level %s model.", analysis), class = "latents_single_level")
    invisible(NULL)
}

#'
#' Sampling weights belong to the independent units the likelihood sums over:
#' the groups of a two-level fit, the rows of a single-level one, the persons
#' of a transition fit. A weight that varies inside a unit would be a

#' The weights are scaled to sum to the number of units, as Mplus does, so the
#' pseudo log likelihood and the information criteria stay on the sample's

#' @noRd
after.source:
.multilpa_alignment_values <- function(supplied, stored) {
  if (.multilpa_same_values(supplied, stored)) return(TRUE)
  if (!is.numeric(supplied) || !is.numeric(stored) || length(supplied) != length(stored) ||
      !identical(unname(is.na(supplied)), unname(is.na(stored)))) return(FALSE)
  observed <- !is.na(stored)
  original <- as.numeric(stored[observed])
  # Use R's actual decimal encoding: at rounding ties it can differ from
  # libc's sprintf(). This fallback recognizes a write.csv() round trip
  # without a relative band that grows with the indicator's origin.
  encoded <- character()
  connection <- textConnection("encoded", "w", local = TRUE)
  tryCatch(utils::write.table(data.frame(value = original), connection,
                              row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE),
            finally = close(connection))
  serialized <- as.numeric(encoded)
  if (anyDuplicated(serialized[!duplicated(original)])) return(FALSE)
  identical(as.numeric(supplied[observed]), serialized)
}

after.name: .latents_same_comparison_data
after.documentation:
#' Compare data signatures, allowing only weight-normalization roundoff
#' @param candidate,reference Lists with fitting data and normalized weights.
#' @return One logical value; outcomes and other data must agree exactly.
#' @noRd
after.source:
.latents_same_comparison_data <- function(candidate, reference) {
  stopifnot(is.list(candidate), is.list(reference))
  weights <- isTRUE(all.equal(candidate$weights, reference$weights, tolerance = 1e-12))
  indicators <- isTRUE(all.equal(candidate$indicators, reference$indicators, tolerance = 0))
  forward_matches <- function(centered, raw) {
    !is.null(centered$indicator_centers) && is.matrix(raw$indicators) &&
      identical(dim(raw$indicators), dim(centered$centered_indicators)) &&
      ncol(raw$indicators) == length(centered$indicator_centers) &&
      isTRUE(all.equal(sweep(raw$indicators, 2L, centered$indicator_centers, "-"),
                         centered$centered_indicators, tolerance = 0))
  }
  if (!indicators) {
    # The general LTA engine stores centered rows; adding its centers back
    # may round. Prove identity by the exact original forward subtraction,
    # rather than granting a numeric tolerance to outcomes at large origins.
    indicators <- forward_matches(candidate, reference) || forward_matches(reference, candidate)
  }
  candidate$weights <- NULL
  reference$weights <- NULL
  candidate[c("indicators", "indicator_centers", "centered_indicators")] <- NULL
  reference[c("indicators", "indicator_centers", "centered_indicators")] <- NULL
  weights && indicators && isTRUE(all.equal(candidate, reference, tolerance = 0))
}

#' Random-effects design of new rows in the fitted coding
#' @param spec The fitted growth specification.
#' @param newdata Rows on which to evaluate the random formula.
#' @return A finite matrix with the fitted columns and contrasts.
#' @noRd
after.source:
.growth_random_design <- function(spec, newdata) {
  random_terms <- spec$random_terms %||%
    stats::terms(stats::model.frame(spec$random, spec$model_data))
  xlevels <- spec$random_xlevels %||% stats::.getXlevels(
    random_terms, stats::model.frame(random_terms, spec$model_data))
  random_frame <- .mixture_prediction_data(
    stats::model.frame(random_terms, newdata, xlev = xlevels,
                       na.action = stats::na.fail))
  design <- stats::model.matrix(random_terms, random_frame,
    contrasts.arg = attr(spec$random_design, "contrasts"))
  if (!identical(colnames(design), colnames(spec$random_design)) ||
      any(!is.finite(design))) {
    stop(errorCondition(paste(
      "The random-effects design of `newdata` must be finite and have the",
      "fitted columns."), class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  design
}

.mixture_prediction_regression.name: .mixture_prediction_regression

after.name: .mixture_prediction_regression
after.documentation:
#' Evaluate the regression part without constructing membership groups
#' @param spec A fitted specification.
#' @param newdata Data frame of predictor rows.
#' @param with_response Whether to evaluate the response too.
#' @return The specification with its regression design and response replaced.
#' @noRd
after.source:
.mixture_prediction_regression <- function(spec, newdata, with_response) {
  stopifnot("`newdata` must be a data frame" = is.data.frame(newdata))
  model_terms <- if (with_response) spec$terms else
    stats::delete.response(spec$terms)
  frame <- stats::model.frame(model_terms, newdata, xlev = spec$xlevels,
                              na.action = stats::na.fail)
  full_design <- stats::model.matrix(model_terms, frame,
                                     contrasts.arg = spec$contrasts)
  new <- spec
  new$n <- nrow(newdata)
  new$x <- full_design[, colnames(spec$x), drop = FALSE]
  new$z <- full_design[, colnames(spec$z), drop = FALSE]
  new$offset <- as.numeric(stats::model.offset(frame) %||% rep(0, new$n))
  if (any(!is.finite(full_design)) || any(!is.finite(new$offset))) {
    stop(errorCondition("The evaluated regression design and offsets must be finite.",
                        class = "latents_bad_data", call = NULL))
  }
  new$kept_rows <- seq_len(new$n)
  if (with_response) {
    response <- .mixture_response(stats::model.response(frame), spec$family,
                                  spec$category_levels)
    new$y <- response$y
    new$trials <- response$trials
    new$log_normalizer <- switch(spec$family,
      gaussian = rep(0, new$n),
      binomial = lchoose(response$trials, response$y),
      poisson = ,
      negative_binomial = -lgamma(response$y + 1),
      ordinal = rep(0, new$n))
  } else {
    new$y <- rep(0, new$n)
    new$trials <- rep(1, new$n)
    new$log_normalizer <- rep(0, new$n)
  }
  new
}
